author: CNT Ponent
title: Vivir nos cuesta la vida
content:
Leer en

Castellano

Català


Castellano

Vivir nos cuesta la vida


Llevamos años viviendo una ofensiva sostenida contra las condiciones de vida de la clase trabajadora. Trabajar ya no garantiza vivir con dignidad, cobrar un salario no asegura acceder a una vivienda digna. La productividad mejora pero la jornada laboral se mantiene. Los beneficios empresariales baten récords, pero los salarios quedan estancados. El PIB sube, pero la precariedad se extiende.

La vivienda se ha convertido en un bien inaccesible para muchos de nosotros: hoy, el coste medio para acceder a un hogar supera el 50% de sus ingresos. Mientras los grandes especuladores concentran cada vez más propiedades, las trabajadoras somos condenadas a unos alquileres impagables, vivir endeudados, sufrir pisos en mal estado o no poder independizarnos.


Esta ofensiva no se detiene en la vivienda y los salarios, también se extiende sobre los servicios públicos que sostienen la vida cotidiana. El sistema sanitario y la educación pública sufren un proceso de desmantelamiento progresivo: infrafinanciación crónica, precarización de las plantillas y procesos crecientes de externalización, mientras el negocio privado gana terreno. Mientras, el dinero público se dedica al aumento del gasto militar para librar guerras que hacen subir aún más los precios.

Nos dicen que ésta es la legislatura de la vivienda, o que la economía va mejor que nunca. Pero, en la realidad, los trabajadores no hemos notado nada de esto y seguimos sufriendo para vivir dignamente.

Pero en los últimos meses hemos vivido también cosas esperanzadoras. La comunidad educativa ha hecho huelgas históricas. El campesinado ha conseguido paralizar autopistas y puertos por decir lo suficiente. Y las manifestaciones por la vivienda han logrado obligar a los gobiernos a hacer leyes que no querían hacer. Estos meses hemos visto cómo sólo luchando podemos conseguir mejorar nuestras vidas. Ahora es hora de redoblar la lucha.


Por eso exigimos:


Bajada de los precios de alquiler

El precio del alquiler no puede fijarlo el mercado. Por eso es necesario reformar el índice de referencia de los precios del alquiler y vincularlo a los salarios.


Prohibición de desahucios sin alternativa y contratos indefinidos

Es necesario garantizar las condiciones mínimas de estabilidad residencial como condición para tener una seguridad material. Por eso reclamamos la prohibición de todos los desahucios en casos de personas vulnerables y sin alternativa residencial y que los contratos de alquiler sean indefinidos.


Expropiación de viviendas de bancos y fondos voluntarios

Es necesario recuperar las viviendas de los grandes especuladores y ponerlas bajo control público, así como prohibir las compras especulativas para evitar su acaparamiento.


Construcción de un parque público de vivienda

Es necesario construir un verdadero parque público de vivienda, financiado mediante un impuesto especial al rendismo. También hay que asegurar que sea totalmente público, eliminando los topes de ingresos mínimo para acceder.


Reconocimiento de los derechos sindicales

Los derechos deben garantizarse a través de la autoorganización de los trabajadores. Por eso es necesario reconocer los derechos sindicales en materia de vivienda, incluyendo el derecho a la negociación colectiva, a la representación sindical ya la huelga de alquileres cuando se conviertan en situaciones de incumplimiento por parte de la propiedad.


Aumento del Salario Mínimo Interprofesional (SMI) hasta los 1.600€ y Pensión mínima igual al SMI.

El salario mínimo debe garantizar condiciones de vida dignas. Hoy no lo hace.


Reducción de la jornada laboral a 35 horas semanales que los convenios siempre podrán pactar su reducción.

Reducir la jornada significa repartir el trabajo y combatir el paro, mejorar la salud, la calidad de vida y la conciliación.


Incremento de los salarios con la pérdida efectiva de poder adquisitivo.

Por parte muy importante de la población trabajadora, el alquiler o hipoteca absorben entre el 40% y el 60% de los ingresos, pero su ponderación en el IPC es insuficiente, generando una distorsión entre inflación oficial y coste real de la vida.


Defensa de todos los servicios públicos.


Ni salarios por tierra ni vivienda por las nubes.


CNT PONENT SE SUMA A LA HUELGA GENERAL EL DÍA 11 DE NOVIEMBRE


¡VAMOS TODAS! HACIA LA HUELGA GENERAL


Català

Viure ens costa la vida

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Palantir Targets MPs With ‘Intimidating’ Letters
content:
British MPs who criticised Palantir in parliament received “intimidating” letters from the US spytech firm, Novara Media can reveal. The MPs say it won’t stop them from continuing to hold Palantir to account. 


Former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn and Labour and Cooperative MP Rachael Maskell both received letters from Palantir’s UK CEO Louis Mosley in June, detailing the MPs’ anti-Palantir contributions in the House of Commons, and offering to meet. 


Corbyn slammed the letters from Mosley as intimidation. “I am in no doubt as to why Palantir is writing these letters to MPs: to intimidate its critics into silence,” he told Novara Media. “Their tactics of intimidation will not work and they will not shut me up. I will never be deterred from speaking out against Palantir, which should have no place in our public services whatsoever.”


Palantir, co-founded by billionaires Alex Karp and Peter Theil, has close ties to the Trump administration. Its

increasing entrenchment in the British state

 via contracts with the NHS, Ministry of Defence and various police forces has sparked

significant national security

and

data privacy concerns

. 


Palantir’s letter to Corbyn listed his comments relating to the firm in the Commons on

1 June

 as part of a debate on the appointment of Peter Mandelson to the post of US ambassador despite his well-documented friendship with the late paedophile Jeffrey Epstein. Mandelson’s now-shuttered lobbying firm Global Counsel counted Palantir among its clients. 


The letter to Maskell listed her statements and questions about Palantir on four separate occasions in parliament, from 10 February to 1 June. Both letters were sent on 3 June. 


Maskell, who represents York Central, told Novara Media the letter from Palantir wouldn’t impact her approach towards the firm. “

Clearly there is a reason as to why Palantir has paid close attention to the scrutiny that MPs have brought to this company which has been handed lucrative contracts by successive governments,” she said. “I have continually expressed my deepest concern about the government engaging with this business, before it was awarded the NHS contract.” 


Independent MP for Leicester South Shockat Adam was also contacted by Palantir. He received an email this month from Palantir’s UK public affairs lead in response to critical tweets about the warfare and AI company’s involvement in the NHS and its now-ended

contract with Leicestershire police

.


Adam told Novara Media: “As public and parliamentary scrutiny grows, MPs who raise concerns are being sent letters from the company’s lobbyists. Palantir says it welcomes scrutiny. Then let it prove it. The public has a right to know how this American company’s software is used across our NHS, our armed forces and our police, on what terms, and who answers for it. 


“Peter Thiel, Alex Karp and Louis Mosley should come to parliament and explain their role in person. Free speech and democratic oversight of public contracts are not optional.”


A Palantir spokesperson said: “There are a great deal of incorrect claims about Palantir circulating online. When politicians – sometimes inadvertently – amplify these falsehoods, they risk misleading the public. The purpose of these letters was to set the record straight. If politicians continue to repeat false claims, we will continue to correct them.”


Clive Lewis, the Labour MP for Norwich South, revealed that he had received a letter from Palantir’s new UK senior VP, Tom Watson,

warning him that the company was surveilling his activities

 relating to Palantir last month. Lewis described this as “very Big Brother” and an “implicit threat”. 


Watson is a former minister and Labour party deputy leader who now sits in the House of Lords, alongside his Palantir job. 


Lewis told Novara Media the Mosley letters in June indicate that Palantir was panicking as the Starmer administration crumbled. “They put all their eggs in one basket with Starmer, and then the writing on the wall was that he wasn’t going to be around much longer.” 


Corbyn has repeatedly

questioned the wisdom

 of using Palantir’s tech in the NHS, given the company’s role in supplying military tech to the IDF during the genocide in Gaza and

surveillance tools to ICE

 as it

conducts brutal a immigration crackdown

 in the US. 


Palantir currently holds a

highly controversial patient data contract

 with the NHS, which campaigners and medics say has damaged trust in the health …

title: Stadtring Zweibrücken – Pride Month Edition
content:
Edit 2026-10-22: Das Video wurde schon im Sommer hochgeladen, war aber wegen eines Kopierfehlers nicht in tchncs.de auffindbar.


Nur sonntagsfrüh ist der Innenstadtring Zweibrückens per Fahrrad sicher und halbwegs erträglich zu radeln. Das Cockpitvideo zwischen Kirchgang-Aufbrüchen und Brötchenkaufverkehr zeigt die etwa vier Kilometer lange Strecke ungeschnitten – in der Version "vorwärts" gegen den Uhrzeigersinn. Die Rückwärtsstrecke im Uhrzeigersinn (rechtes Video) wurde an verschiedenen Markern geschnitten und die einzelnen Abschnitte in der Geschwindigkeit angepasst.


Eine Stadtringaufnahme vom Januar 2026 auf Youtube war in beiden Richtungen unbearbeitet. Die Strecken stimmen dort nicht so genau überein.


Zur Mitte des Videos gibt es einen Abschnitt, der wegen Einbahnstraßenregelung nicht auf der gleichen Route zurückgelegt werden kann. Hier folgt der UZS der Fruchtmarktsstraße, während gegen den UZS durch die Landauer Straße führt.


Das Projekt ist eine Arbeit im Voranschreiten mit ungewissem Ausgang. Eine Vierjahreszeiten-Collage wäre eine Idee, denn mittlerweile fehlt nur noch die Herbstversion.

author: hsa_oryx
title: HORROR AS FLEEING HUNTED STAG COLLIDES WITH CAR CARRYING WOMAN AND CHILD
content:
On the 12

th

 of October the Quantock Staghounds met in West Bagborough, an area which falls within the constituency of Liberal Democrats MP Rachel Gilmour. Rachel has recently spoken publicly about her support for “trail” hunting, presenting what is a grim and violent reality as something that reads like a Disney fairytale.


MP Rachel Gilmour at last year’s BHSA “trail” hunting day, reported in the West Somerset Free Press.


Although stag hunts do not profess to “trail” hunt, like their fox hunting counterparts, they too manipulate the current law, exploiting loopholes to ensure the continuation of barbarism that brings terror to the countryside.


Rachel’s comments come at a time when sickening reports of hunting in the area are piling up, and you would think someone who has previously worked as Head of Strategy at the Environment Agency, would have a greater understanding of the countryside and the views of those that live there.


12th of October 2026


North Dorset Hunt Sabs and Mendip Hunt Sabs were joined by Holford Against Hunting as they sabbed the Quantock Staghounds.

Reports and video footage

 from the day detail how a hunted stag crossed the path of sabs and was subsequently seen to safety, thanks to them calling the hounds off.


More stags were chased throughout the day, with one seeking refuge on land owned by the League Against Cruel Sports. Reports also detail how two pairs of hounds were out at the same time; only two hounds are permitted to be used under the relevant legal exemptions within the Hunting Act.


However, since the reports were published there has been a disturbing update.


A stag crosses the path of sabs as he desperately tries to escape the Quantock Staghounds.

© North Dorset Hunt Sabs


At 4:30pm, two members of the public were travelling along the A39 between Nether Stowey and Holford when they came across the hunt. As we continue to see, rabid hunt supporters will line roads, making as much noise as possible to prevent stags from crossing as they seek safety. This incident was no different, except that what was described as a “gigantic stag” ran across the road and collided with a vehicle.


A witness described how the terrified stag “

was flipped over the top of the car. Its leg kicked out smashing the rear nearside window. The Stag landed heavily on the verge.”


The driver of the vehicle was a young woman with a small child on board, and thankfully, neither of them sustained any injuries, but both were badly shaken up. The hunt, showing absolutely no concern or regard for the members of the public who had been involved in or witnessed this horrific incident, fled the scene as police were called.


The witness went on to say that, despite looking for the stag, they couldn’t see him. Sabs have since reported that it is believed the stag did get away and was not killed by the hunt. However, after being hit by the car, there is no way of knowing what injuries he sustained or whether or not he ultimately survived this horrifying ordeal.


Quantock Staghounds causing chaos and terror in an area of “outstanding natural beauty.”

© North Dorset Hunt Sabs


Excuses, excuses


Stag hunts often try to use the excuse of dispatching an injured or sick deer to justify their barbaric actions. However, on this occasion, when there was clearly an injured stag, albeit as a result of their actions, they were quick to flee the scene. 


In her recent defence of “trail” hunting, Rachel Gilmour has claimed that hunt meets offer “

companionship to retirees and widowers who might otherwise face isolation and loneliness.”

 She also added that hunting “

forms part of a long and richly woven rural social fabric that binds farms, villages and families together through shared work, ritual, and memories.”


Her comments are a far cry from the realities of hunting. Many people living within these communities are not only opposed to it but are also put in grave danger every time these hunts go out.


It’s not just stag hunting taking place under Rachel’s nose


As well as stag hunts operating in Rachel’s constituency, the Tiverton Foxhounds’ kennels are also located within it.


On the 10

th

 of October 2026 they met in Rackenford, an area represented by Rachel’s Liberal Democrats’ colleague Ian Roome. A Devon County Hunt Sabs

report

 from the day details how “

one fox after another”

 was chased as they kept watch from the ground and used their drone.


Fox caught on drone footage fleeing …

author: Selene Magnolia Gatti, Santi Donaire and Clare Carlile
title: In Pictures: ‘Armageddon’ at Europe’s Swim Spots Linked to Climate Change and Factory Farm Pollution
content:
A version of this article was published in

Euronews

 and Climatica

Across Brittany, tractors can be seen trundling onto beaches to remove truckloads of foul-smelling algae ahead of the tourist rush. 


Situated below steep cliffs and ancient forests, these once pristine beaches have been devastated by algal blooms – the rapid growth of toxic seaweed which kills off fish and plant life. This sea lettuce algae can also release a toxic gas that can cause humans dizziness, chest pain, breathing problems, and even cardiac arrest.


The French peninsula is not alone. Fed by harmful pollution from agriculture, and fuelled by seas warmed by climate change, lurid green blooms are increasingly appearing on beaches and lakes across Europe – prompting hundreds of swimming bans across the continent this summer. 


Subscribe to Desmog


Get the weekly intelligence you need to hold polluters accountable

Sign Up


Send me intelligence from:


All

UK/Europe team


Scientists are clear on the cause: for decades, chemicals including nitrogen and phosphorus have leached into waterways from human sewage, as well as fertilisers and excess manure fuelled by the rapid growth of Europe’s factory farms. 


These ‘nutrients’ are vital for plant growth – but in large quantities they destroy the delicate balance of ecosystems, allowing certain plants, including algae, to multiply at the expense of animals and other species.


Green algae on Plage du Yar, Plestin-le-Grèves, in Brittany, France. Agricultural run-off carries the algae down the river Yar and into the sea. Credit: Selene Magnolia Gatti


DeSmog visited some of the worst impacted spots in Europe, speaking to fishers, swimmers, and business owners whose livelihoods and wellbeing depend on healthy waters.


On the shores of lakes and beaches across France, Spain, Germany and Northern Ireland, we heard accounts of plummeting fish and insect numbers, swimming bans, and beach closures. 


The risks of algal growth have been known for decades, but higher temperatures and longer summers mean these dangerous blooms are growing larger and lasting longer in many of the continent’s most iconic waterways. 


“I remember our beautiful beach before the pollution,” says Brittany resident Jean Hascoet, who leads local campaign group Baie de Douarnenez Environnement. “Now, with thousands of pigs near our town, everything is different.”


Brittany resident and environmental campaigner Jean Hascoet, pictured here in Douarnenez Bay, France, says the surge in intensive farming in the region has devastated local beaches. Credit: Selene Magnolia Gatti


‘Spain’s Sacrificial Zone’


“You’ll never see me swimming in that water again,” Fina says. 


The 84-year-old from Murcia in southeastern Spain lives with her husband Francisco on the beachfront at Los Urrutias, on the west coast of the Mar Menor, Europe’s largest saltwater lagoon. Rotting seaweed piles up on the shore, giving off a foul stench. 


“This used to be paradise. The sea was teeming with seahorses,” Fina says. 


Brittany resident and environmental campaigner Jean Hascoet, pictured here in Douarnenez Bay, France, says the surge in intensive farming in the region has devastated local beaches. Credit: Selene Magnolia Gatti


The last decade has seen a sharp increase in algae growth in the Mar Menor – a hotspot for Spanish and international tourists. Cyanobacteria, also known as blue-green algae, is reliant on nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus to grow, and in this region, intensive farming has provided a ready supply. 


Spain is the EU’s largest producer of pork,

accounting

 for a quarter of the bloc’s production. In the Mar Menor catchment area, according to latest

government figures

, 305 pig farms house nearly 700,000 animals – producing vast amounts of manure and slurry, a liquid mixture containing faeces and urine. When it rains, the nutrient-rich mixtures flow from fields into rivers feeding the lagoon.


Algae piled up on one of the Mar Menor’s 22 beaches, Los Urrutias, near Murcia, Spain, due to excess nitrogen from industrial agriculture and livestock farming. Credit: Santi Donaire


“The land can’t accommodate it all,” says Pedro Luengo, a biologist and spokesperson for the campaign group Ecologistas en Acción in Murcia. “We’re a sacrificial zone.”


Tourists now steer clear of the area closest to the farmland – the western region where Fina lives, which was once an idyllic family …

Уже довольно долгое время на моём столе лежат пространные тексты Максима – ответ на замечания, которые я публиковал вслед за его статьёй в №96 Umanità Nova, и на статью Спартака, появившуюся в №75.

Место не позволяет мне опубликовать их полностью, но стоит рассмотреть его аргументы.

Максим говорит от имени коммунистов «русской школы» и, как помнят читатели, выступает за диктатуру. Но он настаивает на том, что диктаторские коммунисты и анархические коммунисты согласны в конечной цели: более того, он прямо-таки заявляет, что коммунизм и анархия – одно и то же. Действительно, он хочет упразднения государства, исчезновения классов, замены власти над людьми управлением вещами. И это хорошо: но он хочет прийти к анархии посредством диктатуры, а это вырывает глубокую пропасть между нами и «русскими»; ибо разделяет партии не столько конечная цель, к которой они хотят прийти, сколько путь, по которому они хотят идти. В конечной цели мы согласны со всеми теми, кто хочет человеческого освобождения, со всеми теми, кто искренне желает блага людям: кто же не скажет, что анархия – возвышенный идеал? С этим согласны даже полицейские начальники и судьи, которые между тем надевают на нас наручники и расстреливают нас.

Нам предстоит пройти часть пути вместе с друзьями Максима: нам предстоит совершить революцию, или, вернее, первый шаг революции, то есть разрушение нынешнего режима. Потом, тотчас же после этого, если они будут готовы предоставить нам полную свободу, как мы предоставили бы её тем, кто думает не так, как мы, мы сможем ещё сосуществовать в мире и даже помогать друг другу; но если бы они захотели навязать нам свою диктатуру (которая могла бы дойти до расстрела анархистов, как, по-видимому, дошло в России), тогда, поймёт друг Максим, соглашение было бы невозможно.

Максим распространяется о трудностях социального переустройства. Согласен; но то, что он должен был бы нам доказать, – это как и почему эти трудности были бы решены и преодолены диктатурой лучше, чем прямым и непосредственным действием трудящихся – понимая под трудящимися всех тех, кто рукой и умом, практическим опытом и теоретическими знаниями участвует в производстве. Он должен был бы доказать нам, как и почему наиболее деятельные, наиболее умные, наиболее влиятельные люди были бы полезнее в правительстве, где по необходимости лучшая часть их энергии тратилась бы на усилия удержаться у власти, нежели в массах, работая, побуждая других к работе примером и проявляя всякого рода благотворную инициативу.

Концепция Максима – это концепция всех консерваторов, всех реакционеров: страх, презрение к массам и вера в чудотворную (чудесную) силу, которую «власть» даёт любому, кто ей облечён. Он приверженец палки: но пусть он хотя бы скажет нам, в чьих руках должна быть эта палка.

Диктатура пролетариата – нам это ничего не говорит: конечно, Максим не должен подразумевать под ней диктатуру пролетариев, поскольку он весьма невысокого мнения о пролетариях.

Он сам хочет палку или хочет отдать её нам?

Поскольку в основе теоретического вопроса о диктатуре всегда лежит практический: кто должен быть диктатором?

Максим говорит: «Это жалостная иллюзия – думать, что революционный кризис развивает в людях чувство долга, братства и солидарности. Утверждать это – значит заниматься риторикой, подобной риторике патриотишек, для которых война должна была стать великой школой, великим очищением души нации. Мы видели результаты: с одной стороны – шайка разбогатевших на болях и утратах войны, с другой – толпа, в которой чувство необузданного насилия или бесстыдной трусости одинаково затмило всякое другое человеческое чувство. Революция вернёт нам людей такими, какие они есть, если не худшими... Теперь какие есть гарантии, что из …

title: Martin H. - Barry Pateman: An Appreciation
content:
Author

: Martin H.

Title

: Barry Pateman: An Appreciation

Date

: 2026-10-21

Notes

: [First posted on the Kate Sharpley Library website]

Source

: https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/c2ft1b


 It’s important to appreciate those who have come before us. I first met Barry through Albert Meltzer, probably at a bookfair. I’d learned to trust that if Albert thought well of someone, he was probably right. Barry was an impressive man, physically and mentally, with the sort of self-deprecating humour instantly recognisable to anyone brought up in a British working class environment. And he was able to talk to people, without the sort of academic language that can be so off-putting.


 The times I saw him were few and far between but they were always memorable. Barry was brimming with ideas, whether about anarchist history, theory and practice, sport or wider culture. Like Albert he had a high regard for the autodidacts – especially those miner militants whose self-education far outstripped those who had had a university education. He was good company.


 It was perhaps telling that I learned of Barry’s death a few days after returning from Ron Marsden’s funeral. Both had been intimately involved in the tension between organising as anarchists and remaining accessible to ordinary people. It’s a tension that runs through most of the anarchist organising and groups that I have been part of in my life, and one I kept promising Barry I would write something about – the organisations that can never get above Dunbar’s number

[1]

 in membership without splitting, the affinity groups claiming to be membership organisations, the strategies designed for different times, the insights from Stuart Christie’s autobiography about affinity groups. Sorry, mate, life always seemed to get in the way, I am way too easily distracted….


 He was generous with his time and his thoughts. He had many strings to his bow – as you would expect from someone who admired those self-educated working class militants – as was so warmly described by the guy who knew him from the New Zealand Cricket Museum at the memorial service.


 Barry would regularly talk about how militant young miners from South Yorkshire were interested in the Direct Action Movement, during the height of the 1984–5 strike. But as they weren’t fully formed anarchists, DAM couldn’t accept them, despite their hard won experience of class struggle. It was this discussion that led DAM to become the Solidarity Federation (alongside other struggles like the Ardbride dispute 1986–87). Unfortunately, with a fabulous sense of timing, SF’s orientation towards labour movement militants happened at exactly the time the pool of labour movement militants shrank, following the catastrophic defeats of the 80s and early 90s. Barry saw the effects of these defeats first hand, as the mutual aid of the strike gave way to desperation and the destruction of former mining areas by a vengeful government. There were successes, most notably the Workmates group on the privatised part of the Tube, but that also swerved the same organisational question by staying independent – it wasn’t part of SF and as far as I know no one outside the originators ever joined SF. The arguments around SF’s industrial strategy, of building trust and organisation in a workplace and then tackling issues from that base are not new

[2]

 – but the obstacles to winning over new people to an anarcho-syndicalist project through this activity remain substantial.


 One of the commitments of the KSL has always been to uncover the motivations and actions of the unknown militants, who didn’t leave piles of writings for posterity. Barry was assertive that we hear the true voices of our forebears, not mediated by what we think now and what we want to bolster our own current views. We are much richer for that approach. The histories published by KSL are accessible to the general reader. The context is there. The achievements are many: Recognising the importance of Guillamon’s work on the Spanish revolution and ending the myth of the spontaneous uprising in 1936, achieved without any groundwork. And his work on the early 20

th

author: Thorin Klosowski
title: Introducing Our New Surveillance Self-Defense Guide: Online Privacy for Parents and Youth
content:
The internet is a vast and confusing place no matter your age. Trying to help youth engage with it safely and privately is a complicated topic that touches on many different skillsets and ideas. But just because it’s complicated doesn’t mean it’s impossible. We’ve launched our

Online Privacy for Parents and Youth

 Surveillance Self-Defense guide in hopes to provide a framework for finding solutions that work for you. 


EFF rolls out this crucial resource as state and local governments consider

ill-advised laws

 that cut young people off from essential information and experiences. This particularly harms vulnerable youth and marginalized groups who often find safety in supportive online communities they can't access offline. Such laws also entail age gating, which compromises the privacy of all internet users and stifles young users’ ability to

learn, grow

, and

express themselves

.


Young people have unique needs and those needs change over time. Trying to protect from everything all the time is an exhausting process, but the security community has long had a solution for this:

security planning

 (also called threat modeling). The idea is to provide a series of questions designed to help you focus on what’s truly important. When it comes to online privacy, this is as applicable for youth and parents as it is for anyone else. 


We used a security plan as our foundation for this guide because deciding what is and isn’t important is the first step we should all take when assessing our privacy risks. But this isn’t a place for quick fixes, and every young person has their unique needs and considerations. There is no single tool or technology fix that can substitute for spending time learning, and then teaching a young person, how the internet works, how to use it, what sorts of harms exist, and how to navigate those harms.


Solutions are rarely about the tools or software you use. It’s about understanding the threats and concerns you have, and then determining what steps you can take to mitigate those risks. We hope our

Online Privacy for Parents and Youth

 guide can help provide the outline to get the conversation started.

title: Buchlesung: Land und Freiheit von Aurélien Berlan
content:
Warum und wie sollen wir uns gegen ein System auflehnen, das Freiheit verspricht, von dem wir aber für den eigenen Lebensunterhalt abhängig sind?


Dieser Frage geht Aurélien Berlan in seinem Buch nach. Dafür kritisiert und analysiert er den kapitalistischen Freiheitsbegriff und stellt diesem ein Verständnis von Freiheit als kollektive Autonomie gegenüber.


Kollektive Autonomie bedeutet u.a., asymmetrische Abhängigkeiten abzulehnen, sich vom blinden Glauben an technische Problemlösungen zu befreien und das eigene Leben möglichst mit den Ressourcen der eigenen Region zu gestalten.


Aurélien Berlan ist Philosoph, Gärtner und Teil der „Soulèvements de la Terre“-Bewegung. Er hat sich in den vergangenen zehn Jahren mit Digitalisierung und der ZAD-Bewegung auseinandergesetzt.


Kurzweilig und auf Deutsch liest Aurélien aus seinem nun auf Deutsch herausgegebenen Buch „Land und Freiheit“.

title: Getting Involved
content:
Getting Involved


In this time of reduced anarchist projects, we’re seeing if there’s energy for us to expand a little. So this is us officially opening up to folks who want to be involved. Here are some of the projects that would be fun and simple to engage in. A list of more-involved options follows.


1. Writing one, or some, opinion pieces for the podcast. You can read it yourself or have one of our regular voices read it for you.

2. Writing a, or some,

Topic of the Week prompts

.

3. Re-starting the ANews weekly digest (ATUBES) for printing out, leaving about, starting conversations with new people.

4. Recording readings from The Anarchist Library for possible airing on the ANews podcast.

5. Signing up to be one of the weekly conversants for the Topic of the Week prompt featured on the ANews Podcast.

If any of these appeal to you, get in touch via emai at: thecollective at anarchistnews dot org


For the future, maybe. (If there is one!)


We’d like to have a radio project. Imagine 24/7 radio stream that is at times live on air and at other times recorded. This would take probably at least a couple people who are consistent and dedicated. Is that you and a friend? You and an interesting enemy? You and a friend and an interesting enemy? Let us know!

 


We'd like to have more regular feedback and report backs from the various events that anarchists attend and/or organize. Finding and encouraging these report backs would be a potentially easy starting project that could get more involved as it goes along, or just remains checking in with folks you know to give us their (un)biased opinions on what went down, or didn't.

author: By Sean Summers, Unicorn Riot
title: Line 5 Opponents Confront Wis. Gov. Evers: ‘Drink the Future Water of Lake Superior’
content:
Milwaukee, WI — As Governor Tony Evers took the stage during the annual Wisconsin Association for Justice dinner, an audience member rose to lead a toast for the state’s leader.


But rather than honoring Evers’ accomplishments, the patron issued a challenge. Thrusting a glass of thick black fluid into the air, Tom Hoy asked Evers to drink the liquid which served as a representation of Lake Superior’s waters which protesters say will be contaminated by oil and other hazardous waste from Enbridge’s Line 5 pipeline if the state, and Evers specifically, doesn’t revoke the company’s construction permits.


“I have a glass of water with crude oil,” Hoy announced, holding aloft a cup filled with liquid resembling oil-laden water. “Will you drink the future waters of Lake Superior, sir?”


Hoy, an activist with the group

Climate Defiance

, continued to challenge Evers to have a drink as attendees, security personnel and police shoved them out of the audience and toward the door.


Protesters attended the dinner calling on Evers to reject the pipeline not on vague objections to the project but under specific conditions spelled out in the state’s agreement with the company.


See all of Unicorn Riot’s Line 5 Coverage


Under the Line 5 reroute

permit issued

 in 2024 to Enbridge by the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, or DNR, the state has the right to terminate the project for good cause, including if the project is not completed according to the conditions of the permit.


Activists, and increasingly the state itself, say that Enbridge’s work has fallen outside the scope of the original permit and violated numerous state regulations.


On October 13, the Wisconsin DNR issued a

Notice of Violation

 to Enbridge for what it calls a “persistent pattern of non-compliance” stretching back to at least March of this year.


The violations listed in the notice include unpermitted construction, unpermitted activity in wetlands and other waterways, and violations of air quality laws, among others.


Language in the permit says that no work outside the originally approved plan the company submitted is allowed, but in September the company

began construction on an unpermitted reroute

 for the pipeline in response to a rupture this summer.


And on August 25, the company was responsible for what’s been called the state’s

largest oil spill

 in more than 50 years when an unoccupied truck rolled into a section of Line 5 at a work site. The

line ruptured

, leading to 31,000 barrels, or 1.3 million gallons, of natural gas spilling just east of the Bad River Reservation in Iron county.


Related:

Enbridge Line 5 Spills Natural Gas Liquids in Northern Wisconsin


In light of the violations and pattern of not complying with state rules, opponents are calling on Evers, the state’s top executive, to exercise his power to revoke the permit.


“If he has a conscience, he needs to act now on the power he has right now to cancel the Line 5 permits,” Hoy, the oil-toasting protester, said in a recorded statement shortly after the disruption happened.


Immediately after Hoy was ejected, another Climate Defiance activist approached the stage calling on Evers to reject the Line 5 permits. They were quickly confronted by an attendee, but resisted removal while demanding the governor consider his legacy and stop work on the pipeline.


The action is the latest in an ongoing battle against the Canadian oil company’s reconstruction of the Line 5 pipeline. For years, organizers have opposed the project on the grounds that it violates Native sovereignty and poses a dire threat to the region’s fresh water, all while accelerating climate change by propping up fossil fuel infrastructure.

title: 30 October International Day of Action: Find Your Local Port Action (No Harbour for Genocide // Europe Palestine Network)
content:
A post shared by No Harbour For Genocide (@noharbour4genocide)

In nine days, on 30 October, dockworkers in more than 100 ports across Europe, Asia, Africa and America are taking action together, under the slogan: Dockworkers do not work for war. The unions call it one of the biggest coordinated workers’ actions the docks have ever seen.

Dockworkers who act without people at the gates will bear the brunt of the repression that follows, so stand with them.

We’ve built a tool to help you find the action nearest to you. Use it at the link in bio.

The map shows every port we can name so far, grouped by country, with times and meeting points added as unions confirm them. Check back before the 30th; the list is still growing.

It also tells you what passes through your port. We have documented 315 shipments of Elbit Systems components through 56 commercial ports and 3,400 shipments supplying US military bases through 67 ports. Where we have documented transfers from this database or the press for 2025-2026, the port’s entry says so.

Not near a port? Join a solidarity action in your city, push the Istanbul Declaration, share the poster. If you are a union member, dockworker, port worker or seafarer, use our template to write to your union. If you live in a port city, use our template letter to write to your port authority.

Organising something on the day that isn’t on the map yet? Tell us through the form on the page and we’ll add it once it’s confirmed.

Translations of the templates are coming soon.

title: Viminale identifica i camnionisti per rimuovere i presidi. “Non ci fermiamo”, i blocchi a sud continuano
content:
Contro il caro-carburanti

 Scaffali vuoti in Calabria, Basilicata, Campania (bloccata la A1) e in alcuni casi anche in Puglia e Sicilia; in queste 2 ultime Regioni solo alcune sigle sindacali hanno ritirato i blocchi mentre il governo, per bocca del ministro Urso, ha iniziato a identificare i camionisti “per rimuovere tutti i presidi nelle prossime ore”. I primi numeri del Viminale parlano di 1.339 identificati, 71 denunciati, 242 sanzionati sul piano amministrativo, oltre a disporre scorte di polizia per i tir non in blocco.


Da Radio Onda d’Urto


Per ora la situazione più estesa, a livello di mobilitazione resta quella in

Calabria

, dove sono fermi anche 870 panificatori, mentre gli aeroporti di Crotone e Reggio Calabria sono senza carburante; l’Enav avverte gli aerei in transito da Crotone e Reggio Calabria di “pianificare il rifornimento in precedenza e in quantità sufficiente per le tratte successive”. Le proteste, comunque, continuano e si aggiunge nelle ultime ore anche la mobilitazione dei pescatori.


Una panoramica su quanto sta accadendo in Calabria con Peppe Marra, compagno di Reggio e direnge di Usb Calabria che sta seguendo le mobilitazioni.


Non ha per ora quindi sortito troppi effetti quindi l’incontro di alcune sigle sindacali con Salvini, che ha annunciato lo stanziamento di 480 milioni agli autotrasportatori (soldi già stanziati in estate ma mai sbloccati) per far fronte al caro-carburante per il periodo da marzo a ottobre.


“Sono arrivate 32mila domande e da oggi cominciano i pagamenti”, dice il leghista; a fargli da sponda c’è Coldiretti, da anni braccio agricolo della destra di governo, che ha annullato la manifestazione con i trattori fissata per domani a Napoli dopo la mancia di Salvini. Sempre a Napoli, però, da domani l’intera Università L’Orientale – il più grande ateneo del CentroSud – entra in didattica a distanza, a causa dei blocchi e della mancanza di carburante per raggiungere le aule.


Da Napoli Raul del Si Cobas, lavoratore di un’azienda di logistica

author: Erica Malatesta
title: Scotland: Anti-Data Centre Movement Gathers Momentum
content:
“Every time you ask ChatGPT a question, read a Google summary or make an online bank payment, a data centre is working behind the scenes. Now Scotland is part of a global race to build many more of them – on a massive scale. The explosion in artificial intelligence (AI) over the past few years has seen tech firms scrambling to build new “hyperscale” data centres, including some which would rank among the biggest in the world. Plans are in place to build at least 23 giant AI-powered data centres” (

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6qxv55882z1o

).


AI has insinuated itself into all areas of life and society. For example in education, it has managed to secure huge contracts with universities and schools, leading to the forcing of AI on teachers and students.


AI is controlled by Big Tech capitalists and by heads of state. It hopes to create huge dividends for shareholders and profits for its owners while claiming to be good for society.


AI has not stopped war. It is developing techniques to destroy cities and kill people remotely. It has not created better working conditions, the end of unemployment, and an improvement in living standards. It has done the opposite. It has not led to a solution to climate change. In fact, the mass development of data centres will accelerate climate change. It has not led to social progress. In fact, the plutocrats are increasingly taking over and controlling the media, political and social power and moving towards increasingly more authoritarian forms of rule, in order to preserve and regenerate a failing capitalism.


The uprising against data centres is therefore also a revolt against AI and against a system that puts profits before people and the planet.


Where are the Data Centres


The map, produce by the Action for the Protection of Rural Scotland (APRS), shows the extent of proposed data centres (

https://aprs.scot/data-centres-campaign/

).


Some of the biggest ones planned are:


Chapel Stile Data Centre (Dumfriesshire)


The Ferret, well-known for its hard-hitting, independent and thoroughly-researched journalism says:


“CX Tech Limited has lodged plans for a 1,000 megawatt (MW) data centre at the site of the former Chapelcross nuclear plant in Dumfriesshire, which could benefit from up to £23m in taxpayer support. Company records show CX Tech’s controlling shareholder is Wpgss Limited, which is owned by property mogul and Tory treasurer Graham Edwards through a holding company registered in the British Virgin Islands (BVI) – a notorious tax and secrecy haven.” (https://www.theferret.scot/scotland-data-centre-graham-edwards/)


Auchertool: Fife


The site would span 60 hectares, about the size of 84 football pitches. It would be bigger than the village itself, completely transforming the life of the village. People are concerned at the noise and pollution, the impact on health and the sheer size of the development. As one villager said: “The village will be left in the shadows of the data centre. It’s huge. It is like having a tower block laid on its side plonked in the middle of the countryside.” (https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cddle43jr1go)


‘Green’ Data Centres


The applications for the big data centres are claiming to be ‘green’. This way they can be considered to be part of “National Development 12”. It is up to the planning authority to interpret and apply the guidelines. According to Action for the Protection of Rural Scotland: “We believe that there will be serious unintended consequences of this policy until a strict definition of a green data centre is established, combined with an overall limit to the amount of energy that Scotland intends to divert to data centres. We have looked at data centres in development around Scotland and have seen that, in many planning application documents, or pre-application consultations, they are describing themselves as ‘green’ data centres. This can range from claiming to be green because they have solar panels on the roof to claiming the fact they use grid electricity in Scotland makes them green, some mention using waste heat in heat networks.”


The Ferret

 has found that data centre companies themselves are working closely with government to define ‘green’. “The Ferret has found that in the months leading up to that announcement officials had discussed the definition with Apatura, which is behind more Scottish data centre proposals than any other firm. content:
L'union syndicale Solidaires organise une soirée débat sur le syndicalisme et les Fronts populaires en France et en Espagne, avec les historien.ne(s)-militant.e(s), Ludivine Bantigny et Ramon Pino. La soirée aura lieu le 3 novembre à 19h00, dans les locaux de l'Union syndicale Solidaires, 31 rue de la Grange aux Belles.


L'été 1936, en France et en Espagne, est souvent présenté comme l'été du Front populaire. Mais au-delà de ces alliances gouvernementales, quelles réalités sociales

content:
“Τη Δευτέρα 12 Οκτωβρίου στις 21:00 το βράδυ, ομάδα 15-20 φασιστών επιτέθηκε σε βάρος δύο προσφύγων μαθητών έξω από το 6ο Εσπερινό ΓΕΛ Αθηνών – ένα σχολείο όπου φοιτούν παιδιά της εργατικής τάξης, ντόπιοι και μετανάστες που παλεύουν για ένα μεροκάματο. […] Απέναντι στον διαχωρισμό με βάση τη φυλή ή την καταγωγή, εμείς προτάσσουμε την ταξική αλληλεγγύη. Φασίστες, κράτος και κεφάλαιο θα βρίσκουν απέναντί τους την οργανωμένη, κοινή μας δράση για ζωή, στέγαση, δουλειά και αξιοπρέπεια.”


Καλέσματα:


ΣΥΛΛΟΓΟΣ ΕΚΠΑΙΔΕΥΤΙΚΩΝ Π.Ε. «Ο ΑΡΙΣΤΟΤΕΛΗΣ»


Αθήνα, 21-10-2026


22 του Οκτώβρη και ώρα 18:30


Συμμετέχουμε στην αντιφασιστική – αντιρατσιστική


συγκέντρωση στην πλατεία Βικτωρίας


Τη Δευτέρα 12 Οκτωβρίου στις 21:00 το βράδυ, ομάδα 15-20 φασιστών επιτέθηκε σε βάρος δύο προσφύγων μαθητών έξω από το 6ο Εσπερινό ΓΕΛ Αθηνών – ένα σχολείο όπου φοιτούν παιδιά της εργατικής τάξης, ντόπιοι και μετανάστες που παλεύουν για ένα μεροκάματο. Ο απολογισμός ήταν να νοσηλευτεί ο ένας σε σοβαρή κατάσταση και διασωληνωμένος έπειτα από πισώπλατη μαχαιριά που δέχτηκε, και ο άλλος με τραύματα από ξυλοδαρμό. Η έρευνα της αστυνομίας για το περιστατικό κωλυσιεργεί και προσιδιάζει σε συγκάλυψη, όμοια με τα «στραβά μάτια» που έκανε στις επιθέσεις της Χρυσής Αυγής, ενώ ήδη κυκλοφορούν βίντεο που ταυτοποιούν τους δράστες. Η παραπάνω δολοφονική επίθεση έρχεται να προστεθεί σε μια σειρά φασιστικών χτυπημάτων που έχουν σημειωθεί σε βάρος προσφύγων, μεταναστών και αντιφασιστών αγωνιστών του κινήματος, τόσο στις λαϊκές γειτονιές του Κέντρου (Άγιος Παντελεήμονας, Σεπόλια, Κολωνός,Κυψέλη,Παγκρατι) όσο και σε εργατικές περιοχές, όπως η πρόσφατη επίθεση με μαχαίρι στην Ελευσίνα.


Τα παραπάνω θυμίζουν έντονα τα πογκρόμ της Χρυσής Αυγής. Η πρόσφατη αποφυλάκιση του φασίστα Κασιδιάρη, η δραστηριοποίηση μελών της Propatria και η επανεμφάνιση του μετώπου νεολαίας της Χρυσής Αυγής μαρτυρούν την οργανωμένη προσπάθεια των φασιστών να ξαναβγούν στους δρόμους. Στόχος τους είναι να λειτουργήσουν ξανά ως το μακρύ χέρι του συστήματος: να στρέψουν τον εξαθλιωμένο κόσμο της δουλειάς ενάντια στους πιο καταπιεσμένους, κρύβοντας τον πραγματικό υπεύθυνο για τη φτώχεια μας. Η ευθύνη της κυβέρνησης είναι τεράστια και εγκληματική. Την ίδια στιγμή που η κυβερνητική πολιτική τσακίζει τις ζωές μας, ο Υπουργός Προστασίας του Πολίτη προαναγγέλλει πογκρόμ και καλεί σε χαφιεδισμό σε βάρος μεταναστών, κλείνοντας το μάτι στα φασιστικά τάγματα εφόδου για να αποπροσανατολίσει την κοινωνική οργή. Μη χάνοντας ευκαιρία, στις γειτονιές της Κυψέλης κυκλοφορεί κάλεσμα από ένα σύλλογο που καλει τον κόσμο να καταδιδει σε αυτους και την αστυνομία όπου εντοπίζει συγκατοίκηση μεταναστών, προσπαθώντας να κανιβαλίσουν την κοινωνική δυσαρέσκεια.


Κυβέρνηση, αστυνομία, αφεντικά και φασίστες συνεργάζονται για να επιβάλουν τον φόβο. Την ώρα που η καλπάζουσα ακρίβεια στα είδη πρώτης ανάγκης, τα απλησίαστα ενοίκια και η στεγαστική κρίση διώχνουν τις εργατικές οικογένειες και τη νεολαία από τις ίδιες τους τις γειτονιές, η κυβέρνηση και το κεφάλαιο θέλουν τους μετανάστες χωρίς έγγραφα και δικαιώματα. Τους θέλουν απομονωμένους, ώστε να αποτελούν ένα απόλυτα αναλώσιμο και φθηνό εργατικό δυναμικό, έρμαιο στις ορέξεις της εργοδοσίας, συμπιέζοντας τους μισθούς όλων μας. Θέλουν να επιβάλουν παντού «νέες Μανωλάδες» της άγριας εκμετάλλευσης. Χαρακτηριστικό παράδειγμα αποτελεί η σωρεία εργατικών ατυχημάτων (εργατικών δολοφονιών) Αράβων μεταναστών στο μεγάλο κατασκευαστικό κάτεργο του Ελληνικού, εκεί όπου τα κέρδη των κεφαλαιούχων ποτίζονται με το αίμα της τάξης μας.


Οι γειτονιές, τα σχολεία και οι πλατείες μας ανήκουν σε ντόπιους και μετανάστες που ζουν, υποφέρουν από την ίδια ακρίβεια και παλεύουν μαζί. Δεν θα επιτρέψουμε στους φασίστες να γίνουν οι μαντρόσκυλα των αφεντικών και της κυβέρνησης στις γειτονιές μας. Απέναντι στον διαχωρισμό με βάση τη φυλή ή την καταγωγή, εμείς προτάσσουμε την ταξική αλληλεγγύη. Φασίστες, κράτος και κεφάλαιο θα βρίσκουν απέναντί τους την οργανωμένη, κοινή μας δράση για ζωή, στέγαση, δουλειά και αξιοπρέπεια.

author: Τάσος Θεοφίλου
title: Υπερπληθυσμός στις φυλακές: παρακαλώ, σταματήστε να μιλάτε για τετραγωνικά μέτρα
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Υπερπληθυσμός στις φυλακές: παρακαλώ, σταματήστε να μιλάτε για τετραγωνικά μέτρα


Ο Elton Kalica, διδάκτορας στο Πανεπιστήμιο της Πάδοβα, με προσωπική εμπειρία πολύχρονης κράτησης στις ιταλικές φυλακές, είναι μεταξύ άλλων και ιδρυτής της «Ιταλικής Εγκληματολογίας των Κρατουμένων». Ανάμεσα στα ερευνητικά του πεδία είναι η Κριτική Εγκληματολογία, η Εθνογραφία των Φυλακών, η Εγκληματολογία των Κρατουμένων και ο Καταργητισμός. Από το 2002, είναι μέλος της συντακτικής επιτροπής του περιοδικού

Ristretti Orizzonti

.


Στο πλαίσιο της πλούσιας αρθρογραφίας του υπάρχει

και ένα άρθρο με τίτλο «Υπερπληθυσμός στις φυλακές: παρακαλώ, σταματήστε να μιλάτε για τετραγωνικά μέτρα»

 το οποίο αναφέρεται την κατάσταση των φυλακών στην γειτονική Ιταλία το όχι και τόσο μακρινό 2011. Καθώς είναι επίκαιρο λόγω της διαχρονικότητας του, τα κύρια σημεία του μπορούν τεθούν και στον δημόσιο λόγο για τις ελληνικές φυλακές.


Ο υπερπληθυσμός δεν είναι ένας απλός μαθηματικός υπολογισμός


Το κύριο επιχείρημα του Έλτον Καλίκα είναι, ότι η αναγωγή του προβλήματος του υπερπληθυσμού σε έναν απλό μαθηματικό υπολογισμό της ελάχιστης διαθέσιμης επιφάνειας για κάθε κρατούμενο θα μπορούσε να καταλήξει σε μια άκαρπη διακήρυξη δικαιωμάτων, αντί για μια πρακτική προσπάθεια εξεύρεσης κατάλληλων μέτρων για τη μείωση του κινδύνου υποτροπής.


Ως αφορμή για την ανάπτυξη του επιχειρήματος του, ο Καλίκα παίρνει τον θάνατο ενός κρατουμένου, ο οποίος πέθανε αφού προσπάθησε μάταια να πείσει τον γιατρό ότι είχε συμπτώματα καρδιακής προσβολής, η οποία τελικά τον σκότωσε στον ύπνο του.


«Όταν μιλάμε για υπερπληθυσμό, συζητάμε για τη σχέση μεταξύ του αριθμού των κρατουμένων και της επιφάνειας του κελιού που καταλαμβάνουν, ενώ αυτή η οπτική του υπερπληθυσμού κινδυνεύει να δώσει μια λανθασμένη εικόνα για το τι αποτελεί την πραγματική καταστροφή των σημερινών φυλακών. Ειδικά όταν μιλάμε για θανάτους…»


Ο κρατούμενος που πέθανε εκείνες τις ημέρες δεν ήταν θύμα της ελάχιστης επιφάνειας του κελιού που αναλογεί σε κάθε άτομο. Το ζήτημα είναι πιο περίπλοκο καθώς «το πραγματικό πρόβλημα δεν είναι τα τετραγωνικά μέτρα του κελιού που μειώνονται, αλλά το καθεστώς διαβίωσης που κρατά τους ανθρώπους ξαπλωμένους στα ράντζα τους για περισσότερες από είκοσι ώρες την ημέρα, η μονοτονία της καθημερινότητας που αποβλακώνει τους ανθρώπους και η έλλειψη δραστηριοτήτων».


Κάτι που επισημαίνει ο Καλικά στο άρθρο του είναι ότι η αύξηση του αριθμού των κρατουμένων ακολουθούν, κάθε χρόνο, επαναλαμβανόμενες περικοπές στα κονδύλια που προορίζονται για τις φυλακές. Και δεν ήταν δύσκολο να διαπιστώσει κανείς τις επιπτώσεις αυτού του δραματικού συνδυασμού σε θέματα υγιεινής, διατροφής, καθημερινής διαβίωσης, εκπαίδευσης και προγραμμάτων απεξάρτησης και κοινωνικής επανένταξης…


«Το πραγματικό πρόβλημα της φυλακής είναι τα άτομα με λιγότερα εφόδια, εκείνα που μένουν ξαπλωμένα στα κρεβάτια τους, συχνά γεμάτα ψυχοφάρμακα, απογοητευμένα να περιμένουν το χρόνο να περάσει, σε πραγματικά επισφαλείς σωματικές και ψυχικές συνθήκες. Και η φυλακή κάνει πραγματικά ελάχιστα γι’ αυτό, καθώς δεν υπάρχει κανείς που να αναζητά αυτούς τους ανθρώπους, να τους παρακολουθεί και να τους παρακινεί να βγουν από το κελί τους και να κάνουν κάτι χρήσιμο. Ως εκ τούτου, δημιουργείται σχεδόν φυσιολογικά ένας διαχωρισμός μεταξύ των λίγων που κάνουν πολλά -εργασία, σχολείο, μαθήματα- και των πολλών που δεν κάνουν τίποτα. Αυτό είναι και το πρόβλημα του υπερπληθυσμού».


Λίγα μέτρα από τις φυλακές της Πάδοβας στις οποίες αναφέρεται ο Καλίκα βρίσκεται το προανακριτικό κέντρο, όπου κρατούνται τα άτομα που περιμένουν τη δίκη τους. (Καθώς στη Ελλάδα δεν υπάρχει τέτοια διάκριση μπορούμε να φανταστούμε ότι πρόκειται για έναν τύπο φυλακής μεταξύ των φυλακών Κορυδαλλού και του Τμήματος Μεταγωγών).


Σύμφωνα με την μαρτυρία ενός συμπατριώτη του Καλικά, «οι μέρες περνούσαν ανάμεσα σε μακρές αναμονές για να πάμε στο ντους και αμήχανες σειρές για να μπορέσεις να χρησιμοποιήσεις το μπάνιο. Μέσα σε όλη αυτή την κίνηση ανθρώπων, μέσα σε εκείνο το ποτάμι αγωνίας, δεν υπήρχε χρόνος να σκεφτείς τίποτα. Δεν μπορούσες να επιτρέψεις στον εαυτό σου αδυναμίες και περισπασμούς, έπρεπε να είσαι δυνατός, ακόμα και όταν ένιωθες αδύναμος, έπρεπε να επιβιώσεις.


»Οι μήνες περνούσαν και κάθε μέρα έβλεπα ανθρώπους να τσακώνονται για το ντους, για τη σειρά στο μπάνιο, για το φαγητό, για το τηλεχειριστήριο ή για πολλά άλλα πράγματα που μπορεί να φαίνονται παράλογα σε πολλούς έξω από εκεί. Ήταν μια συνεχής σύγκρουση διαφορετικών …

author: Moussa Traoure
title: The Palace Guard Against the Trenches : What the Mutiny in Niamey Revealed
content:
The mutiny that broke out in

air base 101 in Niamey

 in the night of 29 August 2026 failed. The real question now is to understand why it took place. Those who took up arms against General Abdourahamane Tiani were young soldiers from the front lines, those who fought the ‘jihadists.’ For all of the Sahel, it’s a much more worrying sign than any plot from the army high command.


Until Saturday morning, fighting took place in the Nigerien capital near to Diori Hamani airport, the presidential palace, and the public television channel RTN.

Loyalists retook control only with the support of the Russian Africa Corps

.

The state television broadcast

 the live arrest of several tens of soldiers being arrested, most of them extremely young.


Three juntas, one promise


In Mali, in Burkina Faso, and in Niger, soldiers took power putting forward the same argument: civilian leaders had failed in front of the ‘jihadists,’ and the army would now do better. Assimi Goïta carried out two coups in Mali in 2020 and 2021. Ibrahim Traoré took control of Burkina Faso in September 2022 and overturned another putschist, Paul-Henri Damiba. Tiani deposed President Mohamed Bazoum in July 2023.


The French were asked to leave, and the Russians invited to come in. The three countries concerned founded the Alliance of Sahel States and

withdrew from ECOWAS in January 2025

. Each then solidified its grip on power through legislation. In Mali,

political parties were banned in 2025

, and the leadership was granted a

five-year renewable term in office

—without elections.

Until 2030, Tiani will remain president of the transition

. In Burkina Faso,

all political parties were dissolved in January 2026

, clearing the way for the regime to consolidate control.


The promised security, however, never materialised. This gap between promises and actions has fuelled anger—an anger that is now festering in the barracks.


Two armies in one


Niger effectively has two armies

: the Presidential Guard, and everyone else. Tiani commanded the Guard for twelve years; since the coup, it has received the best equipment and the most secure and comfortable postings. Meanwhile, regular units stationed in the southwest and along the Nier’s borders are losing personnel in the fight against the Islamic State in the Sahel and the al-Qaeda-linked JNIM.


According to observers, it is these soldiers who have mutinied. US researcher

Alex Thurston

 that most accounts align: regardless of infighting at the top, it is the anger of the rank-and-file that has driven the revolt.

Paul Melly, of Chatham House

, aptly summari the sentiment among young officers: three years ago, things seemed to be improving; today, the opposite is true.


When dealing with generals, a regime can either negotiate or simply swap out loyalists for other trusted figures. But for soldiers suffering from a lack of ammunition and reinforcements, a reshuffle within the high command changes nothing.


Niamey, Niger.


How the juntas protect themselves


The first pillar: the purges. In Mali, following a

reported coup attempt in August 2025

, two generals and more than fifty military personnel were arrested. At the end of December,

a decree mandated the forced retirement

 of several high-ranking officers, including the former intelligence chief. In Burkina Faso, after a plot was uncovered in January 2026, Damiba—identified by Ouagadougou as one of the organizers—

was extradited to Togo

. Tiani has taken a more cautious approach: on 11 September,

he replaced Chief of Staff Moussa Salaou Barmou with Mamane Sani Kiaou

. Former Defense Minister

Kalla Moutari has been arrested

, and former RFI journalist

Moussa Kaka

 has been shot. According to Thurston, this reaction suggests that

Tiani does not wish to appear fearful

.


The second pillar is the law. With political parties banned and terms of office extended, the opposition has no remaining legal path to power.


The third pillar is an external protector.

Between 200 and 300 fighters

 from the Russian African Corps are stationed in Niger, with their headquarters located south of Base 101. Russian Ambassador

Viktor Voropaev maintains that Niamey merely requested assistance

. According to Thurston,

the Algerian air force also provided support

 to the loyalists. For the first time, forces tasked with fighting jihadists have openly opened fire on soldiers from the very countries that employ them.

author: Mzi Velapi
title: Austerity under fire as Godongwana pauses fuel levies and low-cost housing
content:
Residents, activists, members of trade unions and civil society groups took to the streets of Cape Town earlier today against budget cuts. This was before the Medium Term Budget Policy Statement was delivered by the Minister of Finance, Enoch Godongwana. Led by Cry of the Xcluded, some of the protesters’ demands included the right to decent work, an end to exclusionary access to free basic services, an end to privatisation, an increase in health, education and policing, and an universal basic income amongst others.


Equal Education’s secretary general, Itumeleng Mothlabane said that the budget cuts in education have resulted in the existence of plain pit latrines in schools, overcrowded classrooms and learners having to walk on dangerous roads when they go to school.


“We reject a budget that continues to deprioritise the education of a poor black learner. We demand an increase in the allocation that is given to each and every learner. We demand an increase in the school infrastructure budget in Limpopo, KwaZulu-Natal, the Eastern Cape and all the rural provinces,” Mothlabane said.


Lusanda Dyan from Rural Women’s Assembly said they are calling for the allocation of land to women and youth in rural areas and funding of centres that offer assistance to victims of gender-based violence in the rural areas. “Give us 2 hectares of land, seeds and access to water and we will feed this country,” she said.


The protesters also demanded land with water redistribution, and for the government to deal with the housing backlog.


Member of the Movement for Change and Social Justice, Lindiwe Mvandaba said the austerity measures that are implemented by the government are a political choice. “We reject the R370 SRD [social relief of distress] grant because it is not enough for us to feed ourselves and families,” she said.


Speaking to

Elitsha

, SRD grant recipient, Bernice Benjamin from De Doorns said that she is only able to buy bread, electricity and a few toiletries with the R370 that she receives. Benjamin is currently unemployed and gets support from her parents who receive an old age grant. “My R370 and my parents’ old age pensions only allow us to buy food for two weeks. For the rest of the month, we have to buy food on the book [credit] and we have to get loans for electricity and other stuff that we need. If you borrow R100, you must return it as R150,” she said.


Another SRD grant recipient from Ceres, Wendy Samson said that her R370 is enough to pay her municipal bill only. “We demand that the grant be increased,” she said.


Protesters called for an end to budget cuts because of their negative effect on the poor. Photo by Mzi Velapi


The South African Communist Party leader in the Western Cape and former provincial legislature member for the African National Congress, Benson Ngqentsu told the crowd that the aim of the budget cuts is to hollow the capacity of state entities so that the government can privatise them. “All police stations in this province and around the country do not have enough detectives and police vehicles,” Ngqentsu complained. He was a member of the standing committee on police oversight in the Western Cape legislature.


“We know that Godongwana will announce neo-liberal policies in local government in order to pave the way for privatisation. We therefore say no to the auctioning of solid waste, and water and sanitation departments,” he said.


Cosatu and Saftu united


Zwelinzima Vavi, the general secretary of the South African Federation of Trade Unions (Saftu), called for unity between the federation and the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu). Vavi shared the stage with the newly elected president of Cosatu, Mike Shingange.


“I want to propose that we have a meeting now in October and next month with Cosatu that will result in a joint 77 notice to the government and inform them that in February next year, during the budget speech, all workers in the Western Cape and around the country, will demand an end to austerity measures and we say voetsek Godongwana,” Vavi said.


Shingange said that the next austerity protest in February should lead to a national shutdown. “Workers have no luxury to be divided because of the badge on their T-shirt or colour of their T-shirt. The enemy knows no name of the union, colour or badge. They only know exploitation and will exploit workers irrespective of the union they belong to,” he said.

author: Mada Masr
title: Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah released by prosecutors on LE100,000 bail
content:
After investigations that lasted for over six hours, Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah was ordered released by prosecutors on Wednesday evening on LE100,000 bail.


Attalah was questioned by the Supreme State Security Prosecution in Case 9072/2026 on charges of publishing false news inside and outside the country, with questions touching on a recently-published Mada Masr

report

 concerning a wave of protest actions at a number of prisons across the country.


She was also questioned about Mada Masr’s work since its foundation, as well as about the steps its management has taken to obtain a license, according to lawyer Mokhtar Mounir.


Mada Masr has sought to obtain a license from the Supreme Media Regulatory Council (SMRC) on

two


occasions

 since 2018.


On both occasions, it

received

 no response. It was only informed of the SMRC’s rejection of the application in 2022, when Attalah was

summoned

 for questioning in another case on charges of “running a website without the proper license.” She was presented with the rejection during that session.


Since then, Mada Masr has

filed

 a lawsuit against the SMRC for damages incurred by its failure to inform the organization about its rejection of the application. The lawsuit was

rejected

.


The new case is the sixth to be brought against Mada Masr, its journalists and editors in the past six years. The latest case against the outlet was in August 2025, when the prosecution released Attalah on LE30,000 bail, after charging her with “broadcasting false news” and “using a website without a license” in Case 6182/2025.

Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah released by prosecutors on LE100,000 bail

Mada Masr

author: Tosin Durodola
title: Deported to Liberia, again
content:
In 1816, a group of white people in the US created the

American Society for Colonizing the Free People of Color of the United States

 (later simply the American Colonization Society), aimed at resolving the “problem” of a growing population of free black people in the country. Both slave owners, fearing that large numbers of free black people would lead to slave uprisings, and some white abolitionists, who viewed their presence as either a security threat or a barrier to emancipation, joined hands in a plan to quite literally deport free black Americans and freed slaves to a settlement they hoped to create in the African motherland. 

This is the origin story of the African state of Liberia, one where race, racism, and anti-black slavery meet yet another type of forced movement: deportation. And in a continuum with centuries past, the African continent, which had solved a problem of lack of (free) labor for white US elites and landowners, now solved yet another perceived problem for their descendants: a population of free black people they considered undesirable. As Jonathan Ort

has shown

, today’s deportation system revives that colonial blueprint.

A little more than 200 years later, an overwhelmingly white US executive power again uses Liberian territory as a deposit for its undesirables, with one difference: the constructed enemy deported from the white nation is another racialized figure, the immigrant. The US has

historically applied a racialized migratory policy

, restricting on racial and class grounds those welcomed into the nation while profiting from the cheap undocumented labor those restrictions produce. Many of these workers are non-white immigrants from Latin America, a pattern shaped by geographical proximity and by a long

US imperial presence in the region

. Continuous political and economic interventions have fueled conflicts, generalized violence, and socioeconomic chaos in Latin America while enriching the US, and those fleeing have formed a cheap workforce in the north as temporary laborers, undocumented workers, and asylum seekers. However,

migrants have become the scapegoats

 for everything that challenges the US’s self-perception of “greatness.” And while the US has long detained and returned Latin Americans, the current government has not only entered

a new era of interventions in the region

 but also further escalated forced returns.

Thus far, the second Trump administration (Trump 2.0) has signed largely secretive bilateral agreements for (forced) returns with at least 35 countries, overwhelmingly in the Global South. Migrants, including asylum seekers and people whom US judges have protected from return to their home countries, are the bargaining chips in these unequal agreements. Partner countries end up taking part in one of the cruelest return practices the US has used: removing people with almost no warning and little chance of defense to countries where they have no ties and may face inhuman treatment or torture, as

UN human rights experts warned

 in September.

In a chilling roundabout way, Liberia once again becomes a place where unwanted deportees arrive on its shores, with little to no say in the matter, and with no medium-term plan for their protection and well-being, or that of local communities. On August 18, 2026,

Liberia’s government announced

 that it would accept up to 1,200 third-country nationals, one of the largest agreements struck by Trump 2.0. Two days later, about 20 people landed at Roberts International Airport;

14 stayed

, from Cameroon, Eritrea, Venezuela, Honduras, Colombia, Brazil, and Guatemala. Most had won US court protection against return to their home countries because they faced persecution or torture there, and

some only learned their destination mid-flight

. None of the Latin Americans interviewed wants to remain in Liberia. Housed in a hotel and fed by the

International Organization for Migration

, free to apply for asylum but unable to work, they have been

separated from their families

 and long for a safe place with ties, a shared language, the right to work, and a community. Is Liberia that place? And what does their arrival mean for Liberians?

The imbalance of power between Liberia and the US is part of the answer. In June 2025, a State Department memo

placed Liberia among 36 countries

 facing a possible US travel ban and suggested accepting deportees as a way out. Washington had already

cut aid

author: Omar Kalinge-Nnyago
title: Uganda: The Entrenchment of a Hereditary Military Oligarchy
content:
Uganda is approaching one of the most precarious political transitions in its post-independence history. The likely trajectory is not democratic consolidation but the slow institutionalization of a hereditary military oligarchy. Four developments are driving this shift: President Yoweri Museveni’s advanced age; the elevation of his son, Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, to Chief of Defence Forces (CDF); the operationalization of the Patriotic League of Uganda (PLU) as a parallel mobilization vehicle; and the legal entrenchment of military authority over civilian institutions. Taken together, these amount to what might be called a “slow-motion coup” already under way.


The most probable outcome is best described as contested dynastic authoritarianism, a system in which elections continue to serve as instruments of international legitimacy, while substantive power is contested within the first family and the military elite rather than at the ballot box. The formal opposition faces structural decapitation through repression and co-optation. Yet two under-examined institutions – the Anglican and Catholic Churches, and segments of Uganda’s Muslim community – offer potential, if imperfect, nonviolent pathways for mediation or resistance over the coming decade, complicated by the risk of Muslim youth radicalization.


A conventional, extra-constitutional military coup remains possible even as the regime works to secure de facto military dominance through promotions, strategic retirements of senior officers, legislative amendment, and patronage. The PLU’s grassroots strategy is designed to insulate the succession from exactly this risk, cultivating broad loyalty and framing dynastic continuity as patriotic inevitability rather than rupture. The principal danger to the plan, accordingly, lies less in popular revolt than in intra-elite fracture or palace intrigue should the succession falter.


Anatomy of a slow-motion coup


The regime has moved beyond personalist autocracy toward a durable, self-perpetuating system built on four pillars: fusion of military command with the first family, political mobilization through the PLU, subordination of parliament, and kleptocratic control of the state’s resources.


Uganda’s slide toward dynastic rule no longer needs to be projected; it can be observed directly. In 2024, Museveni handed his son the office of Chief of Defence Forces, together with an unusual personal grant of authority to promote senior officers – a clear departure from the constitutional design of a professional military answerable to civilian rather than familial command. Muhoozi has used this platform expansively, maintaining an active, often combative social media presence, intervening openly in partisan disputes, and, in June 2026, ordering troops to shut down Nation Media Group’s operations after critical coverage of his conduct. He has also directly ordered the arrest of opposition lawyer Erias Lukwago and the deportation of Kenyan lawyer Martha Karua, both members of Dr Kizza Besigye’s defence team – a signal that the regime now treats defence counsel, and not only defendants, as targets. In his national address of 4 July 2026, President Museveni appeared to defend his son’s actions, placing blame on Besigye for allegedly delaying court proceedings.


The institutional scaffolding around Muhoozi has matured alongside his personal profile. The Patriotic League of Uganda, rebranded in 2024 from an informal network of birthday rallies and fan clubs known as the “Muhoozi Project”, now runs village-level structures, community clean-up campaigns, and youth roadshows, and openly courts the same rural base the National Resistance Movement (NRM) has cultivated for four decades. It functions less as a political party than as an insurance policy: it absorbs potential rivals into patronage, builds a loyalty network running parallel to the NRM’s own, and softens the ground for a hereditary handover by presenting it as continuity rather than rupture. Leadership changes, such as the appointment of Hon. Fadil Twaha as Secretary General, signal a deliberate effort to deepen outreach among Muslim communities that feel marginalized in the League’s rise.


The 12

th

 Parliament offered an early demonstration of the PLU’s reach. The League withdrew its earlier backing for then Speaker Anita Among and her deputy, Thomas Tayebwa, clearing the way for Jacob Oboth-Oboth’s election as Speaker – a small but telling exercise of veto power …

author: ROAPE
title: Bought, held, and sworn
content:
Somalia’s parliamentary election is not one election. It is 275 simultaneous, separate auctions. Each of Somalia’s 275 House of the People seats belongs to a specific sub-clan. Each is contested by a separate and distinct pool of delegates — assembled only for that seat, voting only on that seat, with no overlap with any other. What looks from outside like a single national election is, on the ground, 275 parallel closed markets operating at the same time — each with its own elder-broker, its own candidate payments, its own hotel rooms full of men who have been paid, sequestered, and made to swear on the Quran before they are allowed to vote. This is not electoral dysfunction. It is the operational logic of a system designed to convert clan identity and foreign financing into a self-reproducing governing class — one that controls parliament, elects the president, and uses both to block accountability for those who commit abuses in its service.


This investigation draws on primary source interviews with more than a dozen electoral delegates, parliamentary candidates, and traditional clan elders who participated directly in Somalia’s 2016–2017 and 2021–2022 parliamentary election cycles. It is corroborated by field research conducted by

Marqaati

 — Somalia’s leading independent accountability organisation — across five federal states, and by an academic study of Somalia’s electoral corruption published in the International Journal of Multicultural and Multireligious Understanding (

Bincof, 2023

). The companion piece to this investigation, “The Debt That Governs,” documents what happens next: how the parliament assembled through this process feeds directly into the presidential election — and how the president who emerges repays his debt through Somalia’s ports, procurement budget, and foreign policy.


The hotel room


The invitation arrives as a courtesy. A candidate’s representative calls to say there will be a dinner — a chance to meet the person seeking the parliamentary seat, to hear their plans, to share a meal. The delegate, one of those chosen by his sub-clan elder to cast a vote for their specific seat, accepts. It seems reasonable. It seems normal. It is neither.


After the dinner — plates of rice and camel meat, sweet tea, pleasantries — the delegates are not taken home. They are taken to a hotel. Or a large private residence. Somewhere with rooms, with guards, with doors that are not locked but might as well be. They are fed again the next morning. And the morning after that. Their phones are watched. Their movements are noted. And at some point, over tea or in a quiet room, they are asked to place their right hand on the Quran and swear that their vote, when election day finally comes, belongs to the candidate who is feeding them.


“They take you to a hotel. They feed you. They watch you. And then they make you swear on the Quran. After that, you are not a delegate anymore. You are a captive.” — A former delegate, speaking on condition of anonymity


This is not an isolated incident. The same sequence emerged with striking consistency across both the 2016–2017 and 2021–2022 election cycles: the invitation, the dinner, the hotel, the oath, the vote. And it is happening not once but 275 times simultaneously — one operation for each of Somalia’s 275 parliamentary seats, across every contested race in the country, at the same time.


How the system is built


On paper, Somalia’s indirect election system is a carefully constructed compromise. In a country with no functioning voter registration infrastructure and a political landscape organised primarily along clan lines, each of the 275 seats in the House of the People belongs to a specific sub-clan. The four major clans — Hawiye, Darod, Dir, and Digil and Mirifle — receive 61 seats each, and every smaller and minority clan is folded into a single combined share of 31 — a structure known simply as the “4.5” system: four equal shares for the big clans, half a share for everyone else. Each seat belongs to a precise lineage group within those larger blocs, and competition for it is always internal — always within the sub-clan, always intimate.


In the 2016–2017 cycle, each seat had 51 delegates, giving a total delegate universe of approximately 14,025 people across all 275 seats. By the 2021–2022 cycle, that pool had grown to 101 delegates per seat — approximately 27,775 people in total. Each delegate pool is its own closed market: its own elder, its own …
