author: Blanca Missé
title: As More Unions Oppose ICE and Israel, the Right Is Cracking Down
content:
The right is trying to gain access to labor unions’ minutes, membership lists, and Zoom chats.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On September 22, The Free Press attacked the California Faculty Association (CFA), which represents about 29,000 faculty, librarians, counselors, and coaches across the California State University (CSU) system. Drawing on private discussions about a proposed Jewish caucus, including communications from a union Zoom meeting, the article accused CFA of antisemitism. How those communications reached the publication remains unclear. Two days later, the Jewish Journal amplified those allegations, urging Gov. Gavin Newsom to consider them as he weighed California Assembly Bill (AB) 2551, CFA-sponsored legislation challenging campus protest restrictions imposed after the 2024 Palestine solidarity encampments. Less than a week after The Free Press story was published, Newsom vetoed the bill.

Pro-Israel and Jewish advocacy organizations had already campaigned against AB 2551 before the union’s internal deliberations were targeted, arguing that greater scrutiny would weaken rules needed to protect Jewish students from harassment and intimidation. Newsom’s veto does not prove coordination, but the campaign portraying CFA as hostile to Jewish students had become entangled with the union’s fight against campus protest restrictions.

The CSU’s systemwide policy prohibits encampments, overnight demonstrations, and unauthorized structures. The CSU Academic Senate immediately condemned the restrictions as undermining academic freedom when it was instituted in 2024, while CFA warned that vague definitions of disruption threatened constitutionally protected speech, assembly, protest, and future strike activity. A major 2026 ACLU-Amnesty study, investigating 80 campuses over two years, documented sweeping repression of Palestine solidarity protests. As the report found, universities “have imposed sweeping restrictions on student speech, initiated disciplinary actions against students, and imposed severe punishments, including expulsions and suspensions.” The ACLU has insisted that even legitimate time, place, and manner restrictions “must leave ample room for students to express themselves.”

The controversy reaches beyond CFA and CSU. Unions and rank-and-file organizations committed to Palestine solidarity have been forced to relitigate, again and again, whether anti-Zionism and solidarity with Palestinians constitute antisemitism — and whether such organizing should be systematically policed, investigated, or surveilled. At stake is a more fundamental right of the exploited: Can workers democratically connect economic struggles with Palestine solidarity, resistance to anti-immigrant and anti-Black racism, and the defense of civil liberties without exposing their organizing and deliberations to external pressure or repression?

We already have a word for the use of legal process as a political weapon: lawfare. You do not necessarily have to win. Investigation, expense, compelled disclosure, and possible sanctions can exact their own price.

Call its media counterpart pressfare: leaked material, selective or doctored quotations, and public identification can turn people into political targets and invite pressure on employers, universities, or government agencies.

The leaked CFA meeting should not be adjudicated through fragments selected for publication, especially when CFA’s statewide record contradicts the portrayal of a union indifferent to antisemitism. During the 2024 encampments, CFA opposed antisemitism and Islamophobia “in all forms” while supporting the encampments. Amid a 2025 federal antisemitism investigation, it stated that “as CFA members, we are united against antisemitism; it has no place in our communities,” while defending members’ academic freedom. CFA’s Palestine, Arab, and Muslim Caucus likewise defines its mission as confronting racism “in all its manifestations,” explicitly including antisemitism. The Free Press story — a clear example of pressfare — sought to overwrite this legacy with weaponized accusations, undermining the trust that workers place in the sanctity of their union spaces and processes.

Antisemitism demands to be taken seriously — which is why accusations of anti-Jewish discrimination should not be instrumentalized. Kenneth Stern, director of the Bard Center for the Study of Hate, has …

author: Franco Giandana Gigena
title: Openness in AI development: a path to long-term independence
content:
As concerns grow over

deepening dependencies

 on a handful of Big Tech companies and the

outsized influence

 of the U.S. and China, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk used his speech during July’s inaugural

Global Dialogue on AI Governance

 to call on humans to

“take back our agency”

 over AI. But what does agency over AI really mean? What policies and practices can allow people to shape AI in ways that respect, rather than undermine,

human rights

? 


This blog post unpacks concrete initiatives that show how openness in AI development can increase people’s agency over AI and advance the development of public interest technology. At the same time, we reflect on how openness is not the same thing as mere access, and how short-term pragmatism can pave the way toward long-term independence.


Why is AI development so concentrated? 


Last year, the UN formally established an

Independent International Scientific Panel on AI

, intended to “advance scientific understanding and ensure that international deliberations are informed by the best available evidence.” The panel’s

preliminary report

, published this past July, contained a stark warning about the concentration of AI capabilities in a small number of firms and countries, which it says “could enable authoritarian capture and undermine democratic accountability.” But how has this concentration of power come about? 


One of the main reasons is that

building

 a complete, multilayered “

AI stack

” is both an astronomical investment and a complex technical challenge. This technological stack comprises:


The hardware layer, which provides the computing power that AI demands, mainly via advanced chips known as graphics processing units, or GPUs; 


The data layer, used for training and post-training; 


The model layer, which consists of the models themselves, such as GPT-4 or Claude, and the tools to service them; 


And finally, the application layer, which is the interface that users interact with. 


Currently, the U.S. and China are the only two countries realistically capable of building a fully national version of the entire stack, where they build and control all necessary infrastructure within their borders. However, even then, they would continue to depend on other countries for some elements, whether that’s for sourcing the chips or the critical minerals used in the hardware layer. Meanwhile, most other countries’ reliance on U.S. or Chinese companies creates critical safety and accessibility vulnerabilities. 


However, all is not lost for other countries and regions that want to build agency across the stack. There are several parts in the AI stack — notably

the data, model, and application layers

 — where greater openness and geopolitical collaboration could help foster collective agency. In this way, we can work towards what Martin Tisné, founder and CEO of the Collaborative for AI in the Public Interest, calls a “

global, open, resilient, non-aligned stack

” adaptable to local needs. 


How does openness support greater agency over AI? 


When considering how to gain more agency over AI, it’s worth looking at the free and open source software (FOSS) movement; a longstanding and major driver pushing for increased agency over technology, from the software running the internet, to the tools millions of people rely on every day, such as the Firefox internet browser. Although definitions of FOSS vary from

source

 to

source

, the essential principle means ensuring that anyone can access a given technology’s source code, study how it works, modify it, and share modified or unmodified copies with others.


The Open Source Initiative (

OSI

) has already applied this in the context of AI, with their

open source AI definition (OSAID)

 according to which an open source AI system is one that enables four key freedoms:


Use

 the system for any purpose and without having to ask for permission.


Study

 how the system works and understand how its results were created.


Modify

 the system for any purpose, including to change its output.


Share

 the system for others to use with or without modifications, for any purpose.


None of the offerings from major AI tool providers, such as OpenAI or Anthropic, currently enable any of these freedoms. Until now, the overwhelming preference in AI development has been for closed systems, accessible only through online interfaces or

application programming interfaces (APIs)

. This …

author: EDRi
title: EDRi celebrates Global Encryption Day 2026
content:
On 21 October 2026, we celebrate the Global Encryption Day! Part of EDRi’s KISS campaign, we celebrate this day with our partners, online, in Brussels and in different European capitals.

On 21 October 2026, we celebrate the Global Encryption Day! Part of EDRi’s KISS campaign, we celebrate this day with our partners, online, in Brussels and in different European capitals.

A recent survey conducted by CDT Europe shows that across several European countries (France, Sweden, Poland, and Ireland), people consistently oppose measures that would compromise encrypted communication platforms. In France, 92% of respondents agree they have the right to have private conversations online, while the figure goes to 94% in Poland, 88% in Sweden and 93% in Ireland.

Encryption is great for protecting the way our messages travel on the internet. Through “end to end encryption”, anyone can make sure that the content of an online conversation can not be intruded upon, not even the server that facilitates the transmission.

This year, we have coordinated several campaign actions to celebrate encryption.

1. Raising awareness in European Capitals through LED “Encryption trucks” driving around Paris, Berlin and Dublin and a metro poster campaign in Prague.

To visibilise people’s support for encryption, we partnered with the Irish Council for Civil Liberties, Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement and Digitale Gesellschaft who are in the streets today, talking to people and press about the “Encryption trucks” and the importance of encryption. In Prague, our partner Iure has been supporting the Metro Posters campaign for the past weeks.

2. Working across silos with groups promoting gender justice, and sex workers rights in the digitalised society.

In the case of women defenders, land defenders from indigenous groups, racial justice activists, sex workers defenders and defenders of migrants, unsafe communications can have life or death consequences. For human rights defenders, secure and trusted communication is often a matter of physical safety and democratic organising.

For 21 October 2026, we have partnered with European Sex Workers Alliance and Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement (France) to raise awareness on the importance of safe and secure communications for sex workers as well as womens’ rights. Check ESWA’s Instagram video and

3. Visibilising the testimonials of activists from Privacy Camp and across Europe

During 14th edition of Privacy Camp gathering that happened recently in Brussels, EDRi asked a few participants why encryption mattered for them. The people we interviewed came from a variety of causes: those fighting for a healthy European civic space, and for digital rights in Netherlands, Portugal and Germany. More, we asked EDRi’s over 35.000 supporters why encryption mattered to them too. Their answers inspired us to post some of them, and we will post them during the next couple of weeks. Check the content on EDRi’s social media channels – on Instagram , Mastodon or LinkedIn.

4. Connecting with global experts to advocate for encryption

During the Global Encryption Summit taking place at 4pm CET, EDRi’s expert Chloé Berthélémy will join a panel in an event organised by Internet Society, the Center for Democracy and Technology, Mozilla, and Global Partners Digital.

Europol and law enforcement are pushing to legalise hacking methods that weaken encryption. These methods rely on ordering a service provider (those who develop or maintain the software, computer system, network, or electronic device) to build vulnerabilities in their systems. With this demand, state actors want to enable the police or intelligence agencies to have access to our data and break encryption. Client-side scanning (scanning of all content such as text,images, videos, etc. on a device or shared in a communication channel) is a method proposed under the EU CSA Regulation. Key escrows or “key recovery”, involves placing decryption keys in a “vault” managed by a trusted authority or group of trusted authorities, who can break them out when access to the encrypted data is needed. Finally, ghost proposals refer to the modification of the encryption system to enable a third-party listener to be silently added to encrypted conversations.

In democratic societies, communication systems are vital for our lives and connections with others. Safe and secure communications and devices allow us to work, socialise, organise, express ourselves, and connect …

Les écrans, explique-t-il, feraient des élèves des « zombies », que leur téléphone, « stupéfiant-image », arracherait au monde. Leur confiscation aurait ainsi fait l'effet d'un électrochoc. Privés d'écran, les porcelets auraient enfin levé les yeux au ciel pour y découvrir leur misérable existence, et avec elle, ce que les adultes font de leur monde.


L'hypothèse est sans doute bienveillante. Le professeur précise qu'il écrit « sans aucune agressivité ni mépris envers mes élèves, que j'aime et apprécie ». On le croit, et c'est bien le problème. Le berger peut parfaitement aimer son troupeau : il n'en reste pas moins un berger. Or en matière de pouvoir pastoral, la sollicitude est parfois pire que le mépris.

Car de porcherie, il est bien question, mais pas de celle du groin dans les réseaux. Ce sont les rats, les chiottes bouchés, les canicules dans les préfabriqués. author: Fundi Skweyiya-Gushu
title: Africa’s Cybersecurity Gap Is Not a Treaty Problem. It Is a Readiness Problem
content:
Africa’s digital economy is expanding faster than its ability to protect it.

INTERPOL’s African Cyberthreat Assessment Report 2026

, drawing on information from 36 countries, found that artificial intelligence was involved in 55 per cent of reported cybercrimes across the continent. Reported losses rose from $192 million in 2024 to $484 million, while 72 per cent of surveyed countries reported scam centres operating within their borders.


The figures expose a growing vulnerability. Africa’s digital transformation is creating economic opportunities but also expanding the terrain on which criminals operate. The question is whether African institutions can respond collectively when attacks cross borders, exploit financial systems and use AI to target victims at scale.


Morocco Cybersecurity Week

, held in Rabat from 12 to 14 October 2026, placed regional cooperation firmly on the agenda. The emphasis was appropriate. Yet Africa’s challenge extends beyond convening officials and announcing strategies. It is making institutions cooperate effectively under pressure.


Africa does not lack legal frameworks.

The African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection

, known as the

Malabo Convention,

 entered into force in June 2023 after years of delays. Morocco, meanwhile acceded to the

Council of Europe’s Budapest Convention on Cybercrime

 in 2018 and signed its

Second Additional Protocol on electronic evidence

 in 2022.


These instruments provide important foundations for criminal investigations, data protection and cross-border cooperation. But legal commitments cannot, on their own, ensure that investigators obtain evidence quickly, financial institutions exchange actionable intelligence or police services coordinate an effective response.


Cybercrime crosses institutional boundaries. A fraudulent transaction may involve a mobile-money provider, a bank, a telecommunications company, a cryptocurrency exchange and digital infrastructure spread across several jurisdictions. Each holds part of the evidence. When requests are delayed or responsibilities are unclear, investigators lose valuable time while criminals move money and erase their tracks. African institutions must therefore measure cooperation by what they can accomplish together, not by the number of agreements they endorse.


There is evidence that coordinated action works.

INTERPOL’s Operation Serengeti 2.0

, conducted between June and August 2025, brought together law-enforcement authorities from 18 African countries and the United Kingdom. It resulted in 1,209 arrests, the dismantling of 11,432 malicious infrastructures and the recovery of $97.4 million. Private-sector partners contributed intelligence and technical expertise.


The lesson is not that treaties are unnecessary. Investigations still require lawful powers, admissible evidence and safeguards. Rather, Serengeti demonstrates the value of shared objectives, established channels and institutions equipped to act on intelligence together.


This is where Africa should look beyond calls by some of its leaders for a continental equivalent of

NATO’s Article 5

. On 19 May 2025, Rwandan President Paul Kagame made these remarks in his keynote address at the inaugural

International Security Conference on Africa (ISCA)

, held at the Kigali Convention Centre. Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has also raised related questions at the

African Defence Chiefs Conference on Military Operations

. While these calls reflect growing interest in collective African security, NATO’s experience offers a more specific lesson for cybersecurity governance.

NATO recognises cyberspace as an operational domain

, and significant cyberattacks may, in certain circumstances, constitute an armed attack. However, invoking collective defence is not automatic: each case is assessed individually by the North Atlantic Council.


For African governments confronting cyber-enabled fraud, ransomware and attacks on public services, the more immediate lesson is not collective retaliation. It is collective preparedness.


Consider

NATO’s annual Locked Shields exercise

, organised by its

Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence

. The 2026 exercise brought together approximately 4,000 participants from 41 countries to defend simulated digital systems against complex attacks. Participants tested technical responses while confronting the coordination challenges that emerge during a crisis. The …

author: Dulce Amor Rodriguez
title: Social media ban may exclude children instead of protecting them, advocates warn
content:
Child rights advocates have warned that a proposed social media ban could restrict children’s access to information, education, expression, and participation without addressing the perpetrators and platforms responsible for online abuse.


The warning followed the Senate’s approval of Senate Bill No. 2424, or the proposed Safe Media Access and Responsible Technology for Kids in Digital Spaces (SMART KIDS) Act, on third and final reading on October 8.


The Senate approved the measure by a vote of 16-1, with no abstentions, advancing a proposal sponsored by Sen. Robinhood Padilla that would restrict minors’ access to digital services classified as high-risk.


Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns argued that the government must protect children from online exploitation, grooming, bullying, and other forms of digital harm without treating their access to digital spaces as the problem.


“Banning children from social media does not make the internet safe. It impedes children’s right to participation while the perpetrators remain,” said Teacher Elle Buntag, Salinlahi secretary general.


The group warned that restricting children’s access would not, by itself, establish whether platforms would respond more effectively to abuse or whether authorities would investigate and prosecute offenders more consistently.


Instead, Salinlahi called on the government to strengthen investigations into online sexual abuse and exploitation, require platforms to detect and remove abusive content, improve reporting and rescue mechanisms, and provide survivors with psychosocial and legal support.


“If the government’s answer to online abuse is simply to remove children from the platform, then we are asking children to bear the burden of a problem created by perpetrators and enabled by weak systems,” Buntag said.


The group maintained that children have rights to information, expression, education, participation, and connection in digital spaces, and urged the government to protect these rights while making online environments safer.


“The state must not confuse restricting children’s access with protecting children. Protection means making the digital spaces they inhabit safe and holding those who exploit them accountable,” Salinlahi said.


Different approaches


The debate over the Senate measure centers partly on whether an under-18 restriction offers a proportionate response to online harm or whether lawmakers should adopt age-specific safeguards.


Sen. Risa Hontiveros, the sole senator who voted against the measure, argued for a more targeted approach that would allow older adolescents to use social media with adequate safety measures.


Hontiveros had proposed restricting access for children under 13 while allowing those aged 13 to 18 to use social media if platforms provided adequate safeguards.


The Child Rights Network Philippines’ explainer questioned the basis for setting the minimum age at 18, and urged lawmakers to examine the evidence behind a blanket restriction before limiting children’s digital rights.


Sen. Win Gatchalian, a co-author and co-sponsor of the Senate measure, argued that aligning the age threshold with the legal definition of a child under existing laws would make enforcement more consistent and easier for authorities, according to the network’s explainer.


Padilla, meanwhile, said lawmakers could amend the measure after assessing its effects, and cited other countries’ experiences with restrictions and subsequent policy reviews, the explainer said.


The Child Rights Network challenged the idea that ease of enforcement should determine the age threshold, arguing that lawmakers must also consider the measure’s effects on children’s rights and daily lives.


The debate therefore goes beyond whether authorities can enforce an age restriction and asks whether the restriction would protect children effectively without imposing unnecessary limits on their participation.


Beyond entertainment


Child rights advocates said children use social media for more than entertainment, including research, learning, creative work, communication, and maintaining relationships.


The Child Rights Network noted that children also use digital platforms to connect with friends and peers and to communicate with parents working overseas.


Salinlahi argued that the government must account for these uses when designing online safety policies, rather than assuming that removing children from platforms would resolve the …

author: April Holcombe
title: Chinese youth in a very shit time of their lives
content:
Certain quarters of the internet are filling with content lauding contemporary China as an advanced, anti-imperialist, even socialist society. Its unrivalled high-speed rail network and its continued use of Communist jargon have encouraged some disillusioned Western youth to declare themselves in “a very Chinese time of my life”.

State-of-the-art infrastructure and Communist iconography have obvious appeal to a section of people living in decaying, imperialist and increasingly far-right-controlled Western capitalism. But there is a big difference between Instagram China, a Potemkin country showcased by influencers at the invitation of the tourism bureau and marketed to disillusioned Western youth, and the real China, a nuclear superpower ruled by bureaucrat-businessmen.  

Young Chinese people on social media—students, workers and the unemployed—use a very different kind of language than influencers do. Theirs is the language of alienation, exploitation and oppression in a society every bit as capitalist as our own.

“Involution”: an obscure word for a common problem

Ever heard of “involution”? Me neither. This obscure academic term, translated into Chinese (内卷

neijuan

), has entered common parlance among young people trapped in the country’s hypercompetitive economy. Literally meaning “inwardly curling”, anthropologists repurposed the term to describe activities that increase in complexity but lead nowhere. Chinese youth decided it captured their social predicament: instructed to work ever harder to stay ahead of their peers, they end up doing much more without being any better off.

Neijuan

describes many things: the gruelling hours at Big Tech companies; the notoriously competitive university entrance examinations; the apps pushing food delivery workers to ride ever faster; and the impossible social media-influenced beauty standards. The second character is now used as a standalone verb, meaning “to work or try too hard”.

Many young people who reject the

neijuan

 rat race opt instead to “lie flat” (躺平

tang ping

), a vibe somewhere between “quiet quitting” and “bedrotting”. The Ministry of State Security finds it deeply disturbing that anyone would want to lie flat, claiming in a Douyin (like TikTok) video that “an unnamed overseas organisation heavily funds ‘lying flat’ influencers, mass producing short videos promoting ‘anti-involution equals anti-exploitation’”.

Successive surveys show scepticism and pessimism rising sharply. In 2014, 62 percent of 10,000 respondents agreed that “effort is always rewarded in our country”; only 28 percent agreed a decade later. One-fifth blamed “the unfair economic system” for poverty in 2014; more than one-third did a decade later. Two-thirds agreed their families’ lives would improve from 2014-19, but less than half thought so for 2023-28.

“Graduation means unemployment”

University degrees once guaranteed well-paid government or tech jobs, providing the Communist Party’s dictatorship with a large, stable base of middle-class support. But now, often, “graduation means unemployment” (毕业即失业

biye ji shiye

). The gradual slowdown in economic growth has intensified competition for entry-level positions (more than 600 people, for example, applied for one basic Beijing office job in November 2025). Stable employment has given way to job flux. “I have family members who, since the early 2000s, never lost their jobs”, labour researcher Kevin Lin told

Red Flag

. “Last year, my cousin was laid off for the first time. Then he struggled to find another job, got laid off again, and is on to his third job.”

Unemployment is roughly twice the official figure of 5.2 percent, according to estimates by economist Li Daokui. “There are roughly 24 million long-term discouraged unemployed people, which is highly unfavourable for social stability”, the Tsinghua University academic told the China Macroeconomic Forum in July. The youth unemployment rate, officially hitting 17.9 percent that same month, has not included students since it soared past 25 percent in 2024, and hides a vast pool of underemployed youth working as little as one hour per week.

For the first time, the Communist Party’s most recent five-year plan includes no job-creation target. On the other hand, the government has a very clear target of 70 percent AI adoption across key industries by next year, inciting fears of layoffs among many IT workers. “I still can’t shake the feeling that I’m getting closer to being …

title: "When the Bubble Bursts": Naomi Klein & Astra Taylor on Reclaiming Democracy from AI Oligarchs
content:
We’re joined by Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor, co-authors of the book

End Times Fascism

, for a wide-ranging conversation on the multitrillion-dollar global investment in artificial intelligence and its reverberating effects around the world.


Klein recently spoke at the People’s AI Assembly, alongside other critics of the artificial intelligence industry, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and former chair of the Federal Trade Commission Lina Khan. “The resistance to AI is taking many forms, and it’s really a resistance to oligarch power, which is concentrated in the hands of these tech companies,” Klein tells

Democracy Now!

 “After 50 years of outsourcing and hollowing out of public functions of the state, the very last stage is the outsourcing of thinking, of intelligence itself.”


Taylor, a co-founder of the Debt Collective, warns that the “circular” debt financing of much of the AI economy is “a waste of resources that also endangers the public.” The AI buildout “is so intense, so frenetic and so redundant” that it risks causing a major economic crash akin to the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis, Taylor says. If that happens, she adds, “Naomi and I think we need to use this moment, just like during the Great Depression and the New Deal era, to demand a real renovation, transformation, of our public services.”

title: Tom Nomad - Toward an Army of Ghosts
content:
Author

: Tom Nomad

Title

: Toward an Army of Ghosts

Subtitle

: Immanence, Conflict and Crisis

Date

: 2017

Source

: PDF provided by publisher


 


 To Emma, the love of my life,

 you’re amazing and you always will be.


Introduction


 Almost four years ago, when

Master’s Tools

 was released, I had embarked on a distinct philosophical and political project, one that had grown out of the lessons from past experiences, and that did not have a determinate destination. This project was born as much out of frustration and failure as it was out of a certain conceptual interest and political desire. What was clear at the beginning of this project were the fundamental flaws in the categories we were using to make sense of action, and in our relationship to the space where action occurs. Paradoxical structures, fanciful notions, illusions, and utopian portrayals of our social and political milieu formed the basis of a political practice that was as much separated from the terrain of activity as were the liberals that we decried. Clearly we needed to at least throw out the latencies of the activist era, which we were discussing. But, for all the pages written about this—the problem of activism, the problems of conceptually-driven conflictual practice—all too often we seemed to be replicating the same categories in our attempts at transcendence. This current book is not some attempt to determine the way out of the morass of activism and ideology; it merely points out where some sparks may reside.

Master’s Tools

 is largely a discussion of immediate questions surrounding tactics; on some level this is a companion text. Some of the ideas will seem familiar to those who have read other writings of mine, but what my earlier writing has not focused on is the larger conceptual context at the base of my previously published works. This has led to misunderstanding by some, and problematic readings by others—some going as far as to retreat into liberal concepts of the rejection of militarism as a form of superficial rejection. I hope that this text clears some of the air, and illuminates a different point of perspective on these earlier works. Though there will be some things in common (the structure of the state, the relationship of logistics to the collection of actions that we term the police) the structure of the discourse here functions in a different mode and exists for a different purpose.


 These texts exist in relation to fundamentally different, yet intertwined, forms of life and tempos of existence. Previous texts were responses to an immediate question, one that was relevant when they were written. Specifically, they tried to articulate and address the failure of the tactics and methods that we were deploying. This mode of being was at a frenzied pace, with hectic risks, rewards, and activity. It was full of late night meetings, large distances traveled, and complicities formed: a life of immediacy. This formed a project to produce and distribute materials related to specific questions, first to a small group of people within direct proximity, which then leaked out into a wider, but still self-contained readership, and finally was compiled into

Master’s Tools

 and became one of the foundations for the journal,

Insurgencies

. It was to cut a line between the current approaches of the time, which were firmly rooted in activism, and address questions relevant to that space, while at the same time critiqueing that paradigm and pointing out some possibilities of escape.


 The text that you hold, on the other hand, reflects the time in between, a mode of life constructed around study, quiet music, and intimately engaged conversations, stepping back, looking beyond reactionary polemics on some immediate question, and forming foundations to think about the questions themselves. The second project, begun concurrently to the first and proceeding in parallel, was to articulate the grounding for

Master’s Tools

. Often relevant questions have emerged from those previously published writings, such as the rejection of utopianism, the rejection of activism, the rejection of political absolutism, morality, and the structure of absolute meaning. These questions are left open by much of the post-left literature written within the Western context. This book attempts to address a specific question—what are the implications of a distinctly materialist approach to the foundations of politics—without falling into the trap of …

title: „Die Zeitenwende“: 100 Milliarden (nur) für die Aufrüstung – die Zeitenwende 2.0: whatever it takes
content:
Dossier


„…

Um gegen Russland aufzurüsten, wird die Bundesregierung bislang unvorstellbare Summen für die Bundeswehr bereitstellen. Kanzler Scholz kündigte gestern an, der Militärhaushalt werde ab sofort auf mehr als zwei Prozent des Bruttoinlandsprodukts angehoben. Bei einer Wirtschaftleistung von 3,57 Billionen Euro sind das über 71,4 Milliarden Euro – beinahe 25 Milliarden mehr als im vergangenen Jahr (46,9 Milliarden Euro). Zudem stellt Berlin noch im aktuellen Bundeshaushalt ein „Sondervermögen“ von 100 Milliarden Euro bereit, das zur Aufrüstung der Bundeswehr eingesetzt werden soll. (…) Es sei klar, dass es deshalb zu Kürzungen an anderer Stelle kommen müsse, erklärt Finanzminister Christian Lindner

…“

Eigener Bericht vom 28.2.2022 bei Informationen zur Deutschen Außenpolitik


 (german-foreign-policy.com), siehe (sozialpolitische) Kommentare und Proteste:


Wie das Leistungsprinzip den Sozialstaat zu verändern droht 


„

Der Sozialstaat steht unter Druck: Kürzungen bei Gesundheit, Pflege und Inklusion folgen einer alten Logik – der Macht des Stärkeren. Woher kommt dieses Denken, und welche Gesellschaft entsteht, wenn Leistungsfähigkeit über Teilhabe entscheidet?


Menschen sollen mehr arbeiten. Alle müssen vermeintlich mitwirken, um die Wirtschaft voranzubringen. Zugleich sollen die Gelder, die einmal in Gesundheit, Pflege und Inklusion geflossen sind, künftig gekürzt werden. Diejenigen, die in der Gesellschaft als schwach gelten, sollen zurückstecken. Dahinter verbirgt sich eine alte Logik: die Macht des Stärkeren. Eine Macht, die heute, so scheint es, einige als selbstverständliches Recht ansehen.


Das Recht des Stärkeren: Eine historische Spurensuche


Dieses vermeintliche Recht hat Wurzeln in der Antike. Es findet sich bei Platon, führte später zu beispielloser Vernichtung. Es kommt in verschiedenen Formen immer wieder auf. Was ist das für eine Gesellschaft, in der die Starken, womit wir häufig meinen: die Gesunden, Angepassten, Unversehrten, überlegen sein sollen? Und vor allem: Wollen wir heute in solch einer Gesellschaft leben?


Wer die Debatten über die geplanten Kürzungen der Bundesregierung dieser Tage und Monate verfolgt, kann schnell folgendes Credo aus den Ankündigungen ableiten: Die Schwächsten der Gesellschaft müssen zurückstecken. Genauer: diejenigen, die in der Gesellschaft als Schwache gelten: arme, alte, kranke Menschen, Menschen mit Einschränkungen oder psychischen Herausforderungen. (…)


Wir sind nicht krank, die Gesellschaft ist krank oder macht krank, so formulieren es Psychiatriekritikerinnen und -kritiker.


„Wir sind nicht behindert, wir werden behindert“, lautet ein Leitspruch der Behindertenrechtsbewegung.


Beobachtet man also die gegenwärtigen Diskussionen über geplante Kürzungen, zeigt sich, dass die Barrieren – statt abgebaut – sogar höher werden, dass die Behinderung durch die Gesellschaft zunimmt. Gleichzeitig lassen sich immer mehr Menschen wegen psychischen Herausforderungen krankschreiben, leiden unter gesellschaftlichen Entwicklungen, Überarbeitung, Isolation. (…)


Die Nationalsozialisten wollten sogenannte „Ballastexistenzen“, wie sie Menschen mit Krankheiten, psychischen Auffälligkeiten und Behinderungen nannten, die nicht in ihrem Sinne arbeiten konnten, auslöschen.


Diejenigen, die auffällig waren, die sie als weniger leistungsfähig, als schwach ansahen, waren in den Augen der Nazis eine Last. Dabei ging man von klaren Kategorien aus, von einer Dichotomie der Kranken und Gesunden, wobei man die Erklärung für Krankheiten, Behinderungen und psychische Herausforderungen ebenso wie für Armut in vielen Fällen in „defekten“ Genen sah.


Unsere Gegenwart lässt sich weder mit der Antike noch mit dem Nationalsozialismus gleichsetzen. Die Unterschiede sind grundlegend. Und doch lohnt es sich zu fragen, welche Vorstellungen von Stärke und Schwäche heute immer noch wirksam sind.


In einem Gesellschaftsbild, das stark vom Wettbewerb geprägt ist, erscheint Erfolg oft als persönliche Leistung – und Scheitern als individuelles Versagen. (…)

author: Chris Walker
title: Senate Democrats Demand Trump Administration Reveal Full Costs of Iran War
content:
“Americans deserve to know how much of their money is being burned on Trump’s war,” Sen. Elizabeth Warren said.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Democratic members of the Senate Armed Services Committee are demanding that the Trump administration release official figures about the true economic costs of the war in Iran.

Lawmakers on that congressional committee were recently briefed about the war’s costs, but the administration has not made those figures public. Noting that the Congressional Budget Office estimated the war’s cost at $38 billion in September, Democrats are saying the White House should be forthright with the American people about updated numbers.

In an open letter sent to U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) commander Navy Admiral Brad Cooper, Democrats wrote that the “publicly disclosed costs of the war have already been tragic,” citing the fact that as many as 23 servicemembers have been killed and 861 have been wounded since the start of the conflict.

“Despite a lack of clarity and candor from [the Department of Defense], press reports of attacks, video footage, satellite images, and photos leaked to the media by active U.S. service members have painted a dire picture of U.S. bases and facilities damaged and destroyed by Iran,” the letter stated, adding that the war has also caused “significant damage to the U.S.’s critical infrastructure in the region.”

“The administration’s ongoing efforts to hide the true cost of this war are outrageous and unacceptable,” the Democrats’ letter stated. “DoD has repeatedly tried to cover up the truth about the number of service members hurt and killed since the war began and has not disclosed these deaths and injuries to the public in a timely manner.”

The letter-writers are calling for more transparency from the administration, and a response from CENTCOM by November 2.

In a post on X, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Massachusetts), a member of the Armed Services Committee, reiterated her and her colleagues’ call for more information.

“Americans deserve to know how much of their money is being burned on Trump’s war with Iran,” Warren said.

Estimates vary, but one examination of household expenses by Moody’s Analytics suggests that the average family’s costs have increased by $2,000 as a result of the war. Energy prices in particular have seen monumental increases, with regular grade gasoline costs going up by 45 percent since late February.

In addition to economic costs for the U.S., the war is having a tremendously negative impact on the region’s environment, with emissions from military activities contributing to the climate crisis, bombings worsening the effects of drought and water scarcity/access in the region, and pollution threatening air quality for much of Western Asia, an analysis from the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace shows. In terms of loss of life in Iran, between 3,592 and 11,410 people have been killed, and an estimated 26,500 (or more) are injured, because of the war.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: Lana Harb
title: Lebanon’s ‘pilot zone’ experiment: The case of Zawtar al-Gharbiyah
content:
Ihsan Yaghi’s house in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah is scorched from the inside. Piles of rubble fill the rooms she and her husband walk through to see what remains. What was not demolished by nearby Israeli strikes has been blackened by fire, with soot covering the interior walls. But Yaghi refuses to leave.


“Despite everything, this is still my land, and we have a very strong attachment to this land that we can’t let go of,” Yaghi tells Mada Masr.


Yaghi’s is one of roughly 100 families that have, since July, returned to Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, one of around 70 villages in southern Lebanon still under Israeli occupation, its residents displaced, its homes destroyed, its fields unreachable. The question of what should be done for the south, how to rebuild and how to return people to their land under continued occupation, has become one of the most pressing political questions in Lebanon. The answer currently on offer from the Lebanese government and its international partners is the “pilot zone.”


On July 21, the United States announced

the official commencement

 of pilot zone operations in three villages in southern Lebanon: Froun, Srifa and Zawtar al-Gharbiyah. The model emerged from the framework agreement — a US-mediated trilateral framework signed by Lebanon and Israel on June 26, under which the Lebanese military is to restore sovereign authority over all Lebanese territory pending Hezbollah’s disarmament. The implementation of pilot zones was to mark the agreement’s first practical step. The idea was that the Lebanese military would deploy to select villages in coordination with a limited Israeli withdrawal, allowing residents to return while reconstruction and services would be concentrated there. Those villages would serve as templates, proof that return and rebuilding are possible, and the model could then be replicated elsewhere in the south.


Mada Masr spoke to residents, municipal officials and others involved with the project to assess whether this is indeed a workable model for the south.


Two months in, it is falling short on nearly every measure residents say matters. People are returning to villages without water, electricity, schools or livelihoods, the prefabricated homes promised as a temporary fix have arrived at a fraction of the numbers requested, and there is no guarantee of safety so long as Israeli forces remain in position nearby and have not withdrawn.


Children walking by destroyed houses in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, July 26. Photo by Ammar Ammar.


The model also treats villages as isolated units, when in reality they depend on one another for schools, shops, hospitals and work, activists say. While experts on the South’s history of war and reconstruction say the current process marks a fundamental shift from previous rounds of war, for those in the south adopting a more radical position on resistance, another pathway must be found.


***


The pilot zone is a new model for the south. Political historian Nassib Chams tells Mada Masr that it emerged from a major shift in Lebanese politics: direct talks with Israel.


Such talks were not the case during the 2000 Israeli withdrawal, after 20 years of occupation, or after the 2006 war. That shift, he says, is what allowed the pilot zone project to come into being, and it gives Israel agency and authority over the return of southern Lebanese.


“This is the first time in Lebanese history that we see many Lebanese expressing that they want peace with Israel. So, while Israel was always stronger militarily, it is the first time there is this much political support for Israel,” he notes.


He adds that the project remains loosely defined, with the government yet to give residents a clear account of what the pilot zones entail.


“We may not know what is in it. We don’t know the details of what is happening in the negotiations. So far, we have not seen an Israeli withdrawal or anything. Israeli military operations are still continuing,” he says. “Are the people supposed to test if their villages are still habitable? It is unclear what they are trying to achieve when it is not even contingent on a full Israeli withdrawal,” he says.


Israeli forces in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, September 24. Photo by Ammar Ammar.


A resident of Zawtar al-Gharbiyah, speaking on condition of anonymity, tells Mada Masr that Froun and Srifa have no Israeli presence at all, while Zawtar al-Gharbiyah has a relatively limited presence of Israeli troops compared to its twin …

title: Eşref Saral'a yönelik silahlı saldırıyla ilgili 2 kişi gözaltına alındı
content:
Trabzon'un Of ilçesinde Eşref Saral'ın silahla vurulmasına ilişkin soruşturma kapsamında aranan iki kişi, İstanbul'un Çatalca ilçesinde gözaltına alındı.

AA'da yer alan habere göre, İstanbul Emniyet Müdürlüğü Organize Suçlarla Mücadele ve İstihbarat şube müdürlükleri ekipleri, Trabzon'da meydana gelen silahlı saldırıyı yapanların yakalanması için çalışma yürüttü. Trabzon Emniyet Müdürlüğünce şüphelilerin İstanbul'a kaçtığının belirlenmesi üzerine yapılan çalışmalarda, Of Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca "kasten öldürmeye teşebbüs" ve "suç işlemek amacıyla örgüt kurma" suçlamasıyla yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında arananların İstanbul'da bulunduğu tespit edildi. Çatalca'da belirlenen adrese düzenlenen operasyonda Y.E.S. (30) ve B.İ. (34) gözaltına alındı. Gözaltına alınanların ikametlerinde arama çalışmalarının sürdüğü öğrenildi.

Trabzon’un Of ilçesi Cumhuriyet Mahallesi’ndeki balıkçı barınakları mevkisinde olan silahlı saldırıda Eşref Saral, vücuduna isabet eden 5 kurşunla ağır yaralanmış ve hastaneye kaldırılmıştı. Son dönemde Amedspor’a verdiği destek mesajlarıyla gündeme gelen Saral’a yönelik saldırıyı, hakkında kırmızı bülten bulunan firari Yakup Kerem Saral üstlenmişti. Sosyal medya hesabından açıklama yapan Yakup Kerem Saral, saldırıyı “Saral ailesinin itibarını korumak” gerekçesiyle gerçekleştirdiğini öne sürmüştü. Saral, açıklamasında saldırıyı bir uyarı olarak nitelendirerek ikincisinin daha ağır olacağı tehdidinde bulunmuştu.

Daha önce Sedat Şahin’e yönelik suikast planıyla da gündeme gelen Yakup Kerem Saral’ın üstlendiği saldırı, MHP Genel Başkanı Devlet Bahçeli’nin girişimiyle Sarallar ve Şahinler grupları arasında sağlandığı duyurulan "barış" sürecinin ardından yaşanmıştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Sylvie Bunz
title: Nach Aufdeckungen: Rumäniens grausamste Hundetötungsstation schließt
content:
Update vom 21. Oktober 2026


PETA und seine Partnerorganisation sind schockiert über die behördliche Entscheidung, die Wiedereröffnung der Tierheime VetMedan und Daeni zu genehmigen. Seit Monaten kämpfen unsere NGO-Partner vor Ort gemeinsam mit PETA und anderen Tierschützenden sowie Organisationen mit aller Kraft dafür, dass diese Einrichtungen dauerhaft geschlossen bleiben.


Gemeinsam mit unseren Partnern prüfen wir nun erneut, ob es juristische Möglichkeiten gibt, gegen diese Entscheidungen vorzugehen und die Umsetzung der Beschlüsse auszusetzen. Solange mit Hunden erhebliche finanzielle Gewinne erzielt werden, stoßen Tierschutzbemühungen immer wieder auf massive Widerstände und es wird deutlich, wie stark das System ist, das an dem Leid der Hunde viel Geld verdient.


Update vom 22. Juni 2026


PETAs Partner im Einsatz gegen Rumäniens Hundetötungsstationen: Uzunu von Aspa Ivets für immer geschlossen


Nach Jahren voller Leid, Gewalt und systematischer Tötungen wurde das von einem Privatunternehmen geführte Tierheim Uzunu im Juni 2026 dauerhaft geschlossen. Die Entscheidung markiert einen Wendepunkt – für die Tiere, für die Tierschutzbewegung und für alle Menschen, die sich unermüdlich gegen diese Grausamkeiten eingesetzt haben. PETAs Partner in Rumänien, der Verein Eduxanima, hat sich zusammen mit weiteren lokalen und internationalen Vereinen dafür seit Monaten intensiv eingesetzt.


Das Tierheim Uzunu im Kreis Giurgiu war über Jahre hinweg ein Ort des Schreckens: Hunde wurden auf den Straßen eingefangen, in der Tötungsstation unter widrigsten Bedingungen eingesperrt und grausam getötet. Die jüngsten Pathologieberichte bestätigen, was Tierschützer:innen seit Langem vermutet haben: Viele der Tiere starben durch Vergasung – ein qualvoller Tod.


Hintergrund: Aufdeckungen über massives Tierleid


Erst als die Polizei des Kreises Prahova im März 2026 eingriff, kam Bewegung in den Fall. Die Ermittlungen führten zur Entdeckung von über 105 Hundekadavern, die trotz eines Tötungsverbots im Kühlcontainer des Lagers aufbewahrt worden waren. Die anschließenden Untersuchungen der toten Hunde belegten eindeutig, dass die Tiere an schwerer Methämoglobinämie und Hypoxie starben – ein klarer Hinweis auf Vergasung.


Auf Grundlage dieser Ergebnisse ordnete die Veterinärbehörde schließlich die endgültige Schließung der Einrichtung an.


Das derzeitige massive Tierschutzproblem ist, dass an diesem Ort weiterhin rund 240 Hunde vor sich hin vegetieren und kaum versorgt werden. Nur zwei Mitarbeiter kümmern sich um die Hunde, die an diesem Ort an Krankheiten leiden, sich gegenseitig verletzten und sterben. Es gibt weder medizinische Hilfe noch Unterstützung für die Vierbeiner. Unser Partner vor Ort setzt sich für die Hunde ein und fordert von den zuständigen Behörden, dass diese dringend und sofort die Verantwortung übernehmen müssen. Die Behörden und die Polizei sind nach der offiziellen Schließung für die Hunde verantwortlich.


Tierfreundliche und nachhaltige Lösungen sind erforderlich


Einrichtungen wie Uzunu existieren, weil Gemeinden weiterhin Verträge mit kriminellen Firmen abschließen, die Hunde einfangen und töten – finanziert mit öffentlichen Geldern, ohne nachhaltige Wirkung. Die einzige wirksame Lösung gegen Überpopulation bleibt: Kastration, Aufklärung und Bildung. Seit vielen Jahren hat unser Partner ein entsprechendes Konzept, welches immer wieder Gemeinden und Behörden vorgelegt wird und mit dem Rumänien innerhalb von zehn Jahren – statistisch berechnet – nahezu keine heimatlosen Hunde mehr hätte.


Dieses Konzept fußt auf ethischen Maßnahmen und weist geringere Ausgaben auf. Es ist an der Zeit, dass dieses Konzept Beachtung findet und das „System Hund“ sich endlich zum Positiven verändert. Die Schließung von Uzunu zeigt, dass Veränderung möglich ist, wenn Behörden handeln und die Öffentlichkeit hinschaut.


Hundetötungsstation Rumänien: So arbeitet PETA weiter


Nachdem wir von PETA Deutschland uns mit einem nachdrucksvollen Brief an die zuständigen Politiker, die Polizei und die oberste Veterinärbehörde gewandt haben, ist klar: Der Fall ist noch nicht abgeschlossen. Wir werten aktuell die Antworten mit allen Informationen aus, um weiter in den Austausch mit den Behörden zu gehen. Wir erhöhen den Druck und bleiben weiter an dem Fall Uzunu dran und kämpfen für die verbleibenden Hunde und deren Versorgung.

author: Benji
title: Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies
content:
Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies

Tiere leiden vor dem Schlachten Höllenqualen bei CO₂-Betäubung

ARIWA veröffentlicht jetzt erstmals umfangreiche Aufnahmen aus einem Schlachthof von Tönnies. Schlachthöfe gehören zu den schwierigsten Herausforderungen für Undercover-Aufnahmen, da sie extrem gut gesichert sind. Die Betreiber setzen alles daran, dass das, was dort geschieht, nicht an die Öffentlichkeit gelangt.


19.10.2026, Deutschland


 NDR berichtet mit Videomaterial von ARIWA.


Er ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie: Tönnies. Als Marktführer produziert er 30 Prozent des gesamten deutschen Schweinefleischs. Allein 2023 meldete der Konzern einen Jahresumsatz von über 7 Milliarden Euro. Dafür tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen


Schweine. 


Das uns vorliegende Material zeigt, wie Mitarbeiter*innen die Tiere beim Zutrieb schlagen und sie unter automatischen Toren eingeklemmt werden. Es zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf in der CO₂-Anlage mit Tieren, die in Gondeln vor Angst schreien und versuchen zu fliehen. Und es zeigt zahlreiche Verstöße gegen die gesetzlichen Vorschriften vor und während der Schlachtung.


Von der Ankunft bis zum Tod:

Erste Undercover-Aufnahmen aus Tönnies Schlachthof


Das vorliegende Material dokumentiert erstmals unabhängig den gesamten Ablauf der Schlachtung von der Ankunft der Tiere im Schlachthof bis zur Tötung. Die Aufnahmen zeigen, wie leidvoll die letzten Stunden im Leben der Tiere sind. Das liegt auch an einer Maschine im Schlachthof, die grausamer nicht sein könnte: Die sogenannte CO₂-Betäubungsanlage.


Die Betäubung vor dem Schlachten ist gesetzlich vorgeschrieben. Die Tiere sollen so vor Schmerzen und Stress geschützt werden. Auch zur Betäubung selbst gibt es eindeutige Vorgaben: Paragraf 12 der Tierschutz-Schlachtverordnung legt fest, dass Tiere “schnell und unter Vermeidung von Schmerzen oder Leiden in einen (…) Zustand der Wahrnehmungs- und Empfindungslosigkeit” versetzt werden müssen. Der Betäubungsvorgang darf also keine Schmerzen oder Leid auslösen und muss bis zum Tod des Tieres anhalten. Doch die Aufnahmen zeigen eindeutig, dass die Betäubung mit CO₂ gegen diese Vorschrift verstößt!


Ankunft im Schlachthof


Am frühen Morgen kommen die ersten LKWs auf dem Schlachthof an. An den aufgenommenen Tagen werden mindestens fünftausend Schweine pro Tag hier angeliefert und getötet. Tönnies verfügt über ein riesiges Netz von Zulieferbetrieben in ganz Deutschland.


Nach ihrer Ankunft werden die Tiere in enge Wartebuchten gebracht. Hier läuft sanfte Musik, sie soll die Tiere entspannen. Es wirkt makaber. Neunzig Minuten lang sollen sich die vom Transport und Ausladen gestressten Schweine hier beruhigen, dabei ist zu erkennen, wie ängstlich sie sind.


Doch das wahre Grauen kommt erst noch. Nach anderthalb Stunden öffnet sich ein Tor. Ein Mitarbeiter beginnt, die Tiere in einen Treibgang zu scheuchen. Dabei kommt Gewalt zum Einsatz: Wenn die Schweine panisch versuchen zu fliehen, schlägt der Mitarbeiter mit der Treibstange zu, auch ins Gesicht. Die Schweine werden nach und nach in Sechsergruppen aufgeteilt. Als nächstes geht es für sie in die Betäubungsanlage.


Per Gondel in den Erstickungskampf


Die Schweine sind jetzt in einem engen Abteil, aus dem es kein Zurück gibt. Ein Mitarbeiter treibt die Gruppen nacheinander in die Gondelkäfige, mit denen es in wenigen Augenblicken gut 9 Meter nach unten in eine mit CO₂ gefüllte Grube geht. Manche Tiere werden von den schweren hydraulischen Trenngittern eingeklemmt und können sich nicht alleine befreien. Sie schreien vor Schmerz.


Sobald die erste Gruppe von Schweinen in ihre Gondel getrieben wurde, schließt sich der Käfig aus dicken Metallstangen. Kurze Zeit später setzt sich die Gondel in Bewegung. Die versteckte Kamera fährt mit. Innerhalb weniger Sekunden reagieren viele Schweine mit Panik. Viele schreien, schnappen nach Luft, werfen sich gegen die Gitterstäbe und steigen aufeinander. Die Fluchtversuche können so heftig sein, dass manche Tiere sich verletzen und Blutspuren an der Anlage zurücklassen.


Je tiefer die Tiere in den Schacht fahren, desto heftiger werden ihre Fluchtversuche. Die CO₂-Konzentration beträgt nach wenigen Metern schon 80 Prozent. Zeitgleich wird oben die nächste Gruppe in die Gondeln getrieben. Sie können die Angstschreie ihrer Artgenossen aus den Gondeln unter ihnen hören.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Animal Rights Advocates Call for Referendum on Snare Traps
content:
ANIMAL RIGHTS ADVOCATES are currently campaigning for a referendum to be held on the use of wild boar snares.

In particular, animal rights advocates have long criticized wild boar snares as overly cruel. Such traps use spring-loaded mechanisms to tighten around animals’ limbs when triggered.

Nevertheless, such traps have also been criticized for ensnaring other species, as they do not distinguish. Endangered species such as Formosan black bears and leopard cats had also been killed by such traps, as have cats and dogs, sometimes resulting in their losing limbs if they survive.

Though claims had been made that Indigenous hunters used such traps as part of traditional hunting rights, animal rights groups have generally cited that this was rarely the case, in that Indigenous hunters generally do not use such traps. By contrast, such animal rights advocates state that Indigenous hunters more commonly use traps made from wood, bamboo and vines, and other natural materials. In the past, the Central Election Commission turned down calls for a referendum on the use of wild boar snares on the basis that the referendum was unclear as to whether it pertained to traps used by Indigenous hunters.

Otherwise, such traps are sometimes used by farmers as a means of preventing damage to their crops. Animal rights advocates have called on the government to provide electric fencing, protective netting, or other means for farmers to protect their livestock and crops.

The proposals called for by animal rights advocates are relevant to the use, display, and sale of wild boar snares, as well as their import and export. It is thought that China is a major source of some of the wild boar snares used in Taiwan.

It is unclear as to whether the Central Election Commission will approve the referendum currently called for by animal rights advocates. At the same time, without a major political party endorsing it as an issue, such a referendum is unlikely to gain traction. It is to be seen if either the DPP or KMT, or perhaps even both parties, throw their weight behind the proposal.

One notes that there have been cases of political bipartisanship between both major parties on the issue of animal rights in past years, as seen with politicians of both parties supporting enshrining animal rights in the constitution. Even so, such politicians ultimately did not prove serious about such promises outside of election campaigning, as a result of which neither the KMT nor DPP acted on claims in past election cycles that animal rights would see constitutional protection.

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als weibliches Rind in der Milchindustrie zu leben
content:
Die Milchindustrie ist ein grausamer Kreislauf des Leids und endet mit einem gewaltvollen Tod.


Wie fühlt es sich an, in dieses System hineingeboren zu werden, ohne die Möglichkeit, dem zu entkommen?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Auch du sollst Kinder gebären, immer wieder, damit du Milch produzierst. Milch, die dann von Menschen, statt von deinem Kalb konsumiert werden kann.


Du wirst fixiert, während jemand das Besamungsgerät in deine Vagina sowie seinen Arm in deinen Anus einführt. Wenn die Zwangsbefruchtung nicht beim ersten Mal zur Trächtigkeit führt – was oft der Fall ist –, wird dieser Vorgang mehrfach wiederholt.


Neun Monate – wie bei uns Menschen – wächst dein Kalb in dir heran. Du spürst eine Verbindung, merkst, wie es sich bewegt und immer größer wird. Je schwerer du selbst wirst, umso stärker werden deine Gelenkprobleme. Die rutschigen und harten Spaltenböden, auf denen du fast dein ganzes Leben verbringst, führen oft zu Verletzungen.


Dann bringst du dein Kalb zur Welt. Um dich herum riecht es extrem nach Kot und Ammoniak, von den Ausscheidungen der Tiere.


Endlich ist es da, noch ganz nass und schwach. Du leckst ihm über das Fell, um es zu wärmen. Es sucht deine Nähe und will an deinem Euter die für ihn so wichtige Erstmilch trinken. Sie stärkt sein noch schwaches Immunsystem und gibt ihm Kraft. Doch dann kommen die Arbeiter*innen.


Sie zerren dein noch ganz wackelig stehendes Kalb weg von dir. Es ruft nach dir. Du versuchst, bei ihm zu bleiben, aber du hast keine Chance. Die Menschen haben es weggebracht – du wirst es wahrscheinlich nie wiedersehen und nach nur zwei Monaten direkt wieder gewaltvoll befruchtet.


Du wirst nach der Geburt monatelang mehrmals täglich in den Melkstand getrieben – und die meiste Zeit davon bist du bereits wieder schwanger. Dein Körper muss gleichzeitig ein neues Kalb versorgen, das in dir heranwächst, und täglich über 22 Liter Milch produzieren. Dein Euter und deine Zitzen schmerzen. Aufgrund der extremen Überzüchtung produzierst du viermal so viel Milch, wie du es natürlicherweise für dein Kind tun würdest.


Die Prozeduren und Haltungsbedingungen zehren stark an deinem Körper. Dein Euter ist entzündet und schmerzt bei jeder Berührung. Andere Tiere humpeln, weil ihnen jeder Schritt wehtut. Viele sind schwach und ausgelaugt.


Wenn du nicht schon vorher stirbst oder getötet wirst, weil dein Körper nicht mehr kann, dann wirst du voraussichtlich nach nur fünf Jahren getötet – obwohl du unter natürlichen Bedingungen 25 Jahre alt werden könntest.


Dann kommt der Tag, an dem du als nicht mehr profitabel giltst. Du wirst aus dem Stall getrieben – das erste Mal nach Jahren verlässt du ihn, aber das ist kein Grund zur Freude.


Zusammen mit anderen erschöpften „ausgedienten Milchkühen“ wirst du auf einen Transporter verladen. Du hast Mühe, über die Rampe zu gehen. Deine Gelenke schmerzen vom jahrelangen Stehen auf Spaltenböden. Im engen Transporter stehst du dicht an dicht mit den anderen Tieren, der Lkw wackelt. Manche fallen hin und werden versehentlich getreten. Eure Fahrt in den Schlachthof dauert mehrere Stunden, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung, ohne Pause.


Angekommen erwartet dich ein brutaler Tod. Überall riecht es nach Blut, du bekommst Panik, aber es gibt keinen Ausweg. Dann ein Bolzenschuss in deinen Kopf. Wenn die Betäubung korrekt durchgeführt wurde und wirkt, brichst du zusammen. Wenn nicht, kann es sein, dass du bei Bewusstsein und unter extremen Schmerzen erlebst, wie dir deine Kehle aufgeschnitten wird und du verblutest.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Mutterrinder in der Milchindustrie erleiden müssen.


Der wahre Preis von Milch


Ein Ermittler von Animal Equality hat mehrere Monate undercover in einem deutschen Milchgewinnungsbetrieb gearbeitet und den Alltag der Tiere dokumentiert. Was unsere Undercover-Recherche zeigt, ist der wahre Preis von Milch: Ausbeutung, Gewalt, Schmerz, Leid und Tod.


Auf unserer Webseite erfährst du mehr und kannst die Stellungnahme des Betriebs nachlesen:


Zur Undercover-Recherche


Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht!


Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel. Im Supermarkt findest du zahlreiche Alternativen zu Milch, wie:


Hafermilch – mild, cremig, perfekt für Kaffee und Müsli (oft die günstigste Option!)


Sojamilch – proteinreich, ideal zum Kochen und Backen


Mandelmilch – leicht nussig, besonders lecker in Smoothies


Reismilch – süßlich und gut verträglich …

author: admin
title: Solidarität mit nichtmenschlichen Tieren im Klimakollaps
content:
Am 2. November ist Friederike Schmitz zu Gast in Leipzig. Ihr Vortrag beschäftigt sich mit der Frage von Solidarität mit nichtmenschlichen Tieren im Klimakollaps.

Plaque, Industriestraße 101, Leipzig

Orga: tierbefreier*innen Leipzig

Die Erderhitzung schreitet voran und wir müssen damit rechnen, dass Wetterextreme und Katastrophen unsere Gesellschaften massiv unter Druck setzen werden. Es ist daher realistisch, von Kollapsszenarien auszugehen – das bedeutet nicht zwingend ein einmaliges Ereignis, das plötzlich alles verändert. Es kann auch bedeuten, dass etablierte Systeme und Sicherheiten zunehmend instabil und unverlässlich werden.>

Die Kollapsbewegung fordert, dass wir uns gemeinsam darauf vorbereiten und solidarische Strukturen aufbauen, denn wer gegen Umweltzerstörung und Faschismus kämpft, kann sich auf den Staat nicht verlassen. Doch inwieweit sind nichtmenschliche Tiere dabei eingeschlossen? Und wie könnte es aussehen, wenn die Solidarität nicht an der Speziesgrenze haltmacht? Der Vortrag liefert einen Einstieg in diese Fragen und lädt zu Austausch und Diskussion ein.

Friederike Schmitz ist eine deutsche Philosophin und Publizistin mit dem Schwerpunkt Ethik und Politik der Mensch-Tier-Beziehung. Zu ihrem Schwerpunkt gehört die Klimagerechte Transformation von Landwirtschaft und Ernährung. In dem Podcast “Was zu retten ist?” thematisiert sie zusammen mit Annemarie Botzki (Campaignerin und Aktivistin) Klima, Kollaps und Ernährung.

author: L214
title: Végétalisation des menus des cantines scolaires : l’état des lieux de L214
content:
Au lendemain de la rentrée scolaire 2026, L214 dresse l’état des lieux de la végétalisation des menus des cantines scolaires dans 40 villes de France. Ce bilan, le premier depuis la prise de fonction des nouveaux élus à l’issue des élections municipales de mars 2026, révèle des situations contrastées : là où certaines villes se contentent du minimum imposé par la loi, d’autres font preuve de plus d’ambition, indépendamment de leur couleur politique.

La végétalisation des menus dans les cantines scolaires constitue un levier puissant et efficace à disposition des maires pour contribuer à réduire le nombre d’animaux tués pour l’alimentation en France. C’est pourquoi L214 propose trois mesures de végétalisation dans sa charte d’engagement du Sauvetage du siècle à destination des maires : instaurer une option végétarienne quotidienne, deux journées végétariennes hebdomadaires et un plat végétalien hebdomadaire.

Ce début d’année scolaire révèle de fortes disparités d’une ville à l’autre sur la mise en place de deux journées végétariennes par semaine. Sur les 40 villes de plus de 100 000 habitants étudiées par L214 :

14 villes proposent deux journées végétariennes par semaine ou plus,

12 villes proposent 5 à 7 journées végétariennes par mois,

14 villes se contentent d’une journée végétarienne par semaine, le minimum légal imposé par la loi EGalim.

Concernant la mise en place d’une option végétarienne quotidienne, le tableau est là aussi très contrasté : 11 villes proposent déjà cette option, alors que 24 villes proposent une option « sans viande » ou « sans porc » pouvant contenir du poisson, une alternative qui n’est donc pas végétarienne. Cinq villes ne proposent aucune alternative végétarienne quotidienne.

Certaines villes comme Bordeaux, Grenoble, Lyon, Montpellier et Paris font figure de bonnes élèves en cumulant d’ores et déjà une option végétarienne quotidienne et deux journées végétariennes hebdomadaires. D’autres villes vont même au-delà des mesures portées par L214, à l’image de Saint-Denis, qui propose 3 journées végétariennes chaque semaine dans ses cantines, ou de Montpellier, qui propose deux plats végétaliens chaque mois.

À l’inverse, Boulogne-Billancourt, Limoges et Le Mans notamment se limitent à une journée végétarienne par semaine, le minimum prévu par la loi.

→ Découvrir la charte d’engagement du Sauvetage du siècle

Cet état des lieux montre que la volonté de végétaliser les menus dans les cantines scolaires n’est pas portée par un seul parti politique. Parmi les cinq villes qui cumulent une option végétarienne quotidienne et deux journées végétariennes hebdomadaires, Bordeaux est dirigée par une majorité du centre, Grenoble et Lyon par des majorités écologistes, et Montpellier et Paris par des majorités de gauche.

Plusieurs villes affiliées à droite renforcent elles aussi la végétalisation de leurs cantines. Aix-en-Provence propose désormais deux journées végétariennes une semaine sur deux, et Metz en propose 5 à 7 par mois.

Pour Erwin Goeller, chargé d’affaires publiques de L214 : « La végétalisation des menus dans les cantines scolaires est un choix politique concret à la portée de chaque maire. L’enjeu a été pris au sérieux par plusieurs municipalités, mais les efforts restent très disparates selon les villes. Nous appelons les nouveaux élus à se saisir pleinement de ce sujet pour contribuer, à leur échelle, à réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués pour l’alimentation en France ! »

author: Animal Rising Press
title: Guilty Verdict For King’s Sheep Rescuers In Theft Trial
content:
After a four-day trial at Norwich Crown Court, Rose Patterson, Sarah Foy, and Rosa Sharkey have all been found guilty of theft after the rescue of three lambs from King Charles III’s Sandringham Estate in May 2023. Sentencing to follow today.

Despite the verdict, Animal Rising claims that the rescue and subsequent trial have helped to put a spotlight on the reality behind animal farming in the UK, with over 10 million sheep being slaughtered yearly [1].

The controversial rescue made front-page news across the UK and headlines around the world [2]. It captured the attention of the British public, questioning how we relate to animals in the food system and if it’s a rescue or a theft to take them from farms.

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, alongside Rosa Sharkey and Sarah Foy, rescued the lambs - Sammy, Sunny and Sooty - before informing police the following day. The women held signs outside Windsor Castle reading “I rescued the King’s sheep” before reporting what they had done to police. They each face up to 7 years' imprisonment.

Earlier this year, Patterson was found not guilty by a jury over another Animal Rising open rescue, after helping to rescue beagle puppies from MBR Acres, a facility breeding animals for testing [3].

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, one of the three defendants found guilty today, said:

Sammy, Sunny and Sooty remain safe and are now fully grown.

The trial followed a series of open-rescue trials relating to Animal Rising’s rescue of beagles from MBR Acres. In January this year, Animal Rising made history by securing the UK’s first-ever not-guilty verdict in an open-rescue case [4]. The lambs were rescued from Appleton Farm, which forms part of the Sandringham estate.

Defendants Patterson and Foy are available for comment or broadcast interview upon request.

For further information, comment, or to arrange an interview, please email press@animalrising.org or call +44 1225 29 6691

High-Quality Pictures and Videos: https://show.pics.io/animal-rising-breaking-news

All images and videos in this file, on our social media, and website can be used with credit to Animal Rising under ‘fair use’ for the purposes of reporting.

[2] https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12431619/Animal-Rising-protesters-charged-stealing-Kings-sheep-royal-Sandringham-Estate-driving-away-animals.html

https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12126009/Will-stop-eco-clowns-Just-Stop-Oil-throw-orange-powder-Animal-Rising-kidnap-lambs.html

Rose Patterson, 37, is the Director of Animal Rising. An advocate for animals since 2012, she holds an MSc in Animal Welfare Science, Ethics, and Law and previously worked with World Animal Protection before joining Animal Rising in 2020.

Sarah Foy, 26, has been involved in a range of campaigns advocating for a just and sustainable food system that works for animals, farmers, and the planet. She brings a practical, hands-on approach to her advocacy, with real-world experience caring for rescued farm animals at sanctuaries and protesting alongside farmers.

Rosa Sharkey, 26, is a food charity worker. She is passionately committed to reducing the impact of our food system on the climate crisis, community action, and animal rights.

Animal Rising is a nonviolent campaign group working to fundamentally transform our relationship with animals and nature, and build a more sustainable future for animals, people and the planet. Animal Rising is calling on the Government to end factory farming by 2040 and support a transition to a sustainable plant-based food system.

The group has used a variety of civil disobedience and nonviolent direct action tactics, notably blockading McDonald's distribution centres in May 2021, blockading dairy industry sites in September 2022, disrupting the 2023 Grand National, rescuing lambs belonging to King Charles III in May 2023, and carrying out the UK’s largest undercover farm investigation in 2024.

author: webadmin
title: Smokescreen Saturday Exposed: Chris Packham Blasts The Quorn Hunt Over Sickening Fox Cruelty That Blows Apart Trail Hunting’s Biggest Lie
content:
When we showed wildlife campaigner Chris Packham the sickening footage of the Quorn Hunt, his response was damning:


“Another bloody year, another bloodied body, another animal tortured and torn to pieces to gratify the bloodlust of savages. Where is the damned consultation and where is the damned ban?”


Chris Packham condemns the Quorn Hunt footage.


The footage lays bare the brutal reality of cub hunting – the practice of using foxes to train young hounds to hunt and kill.


WARNING: DISTURBING FOOTAGE


Cub hunting is not some isolated activity. It is the preparation for the hunting season ahead. Throughout the autumn, young hounds are taught what to chase, what to kill and how to respond to the huntsman’s commands. What they learn – or fail to learn – during these crucial weeks sets the tone for the entire season.


This is what makes the Quorn Hunt footage so damning. It shows hounds being deliberately encouraged to seize and tear at a fox, with hunt staff repeatedly intervening to reinforce that behaviour.


On the eve of National Trail Hunting Day aka Smokescreen Saturday – as the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) and the Countryside Alliance prepared to showcase so-called ‘trail hunting’, the Quorn Hunt provided a horrifying glimpse of the reality behind the myth of trail laying.


On Friday 16 October, 2026 Northants Hunt Saboteurs visited The Quorn Hunt’s kennel meet at Kirby Bellars, near Melton Mowbray, Leicestershire.


The Quorn has a long history of royal connections. King Charles regularly rode with the hunt when he was Prince of Wales. His association with the Quorn came to an end following the emergence of footage showing

hunt members pulling a fox cub from its den

 and throwing them to the hounds to be torn apart.


The footage begins with the saboteurs’ drone approaching a group of barns stacked with bales. Mounted riders are positioned around the outside of the covert – a classic cub hunting tactic designed to frighten fleeing foxes back into cover, where the hounds can kill them.


Riders surround the covert which forces the fox back towards the barns.


As the drone circles to the far side of the barns, a group of hounds comes into view. A quad bike can be seen approaching, alongside another rider. More hounds appear on the track, along with a riderless horse.


Two terriermen jump off the quad bike and run towards the hounds, which have gathered in a narrow passageway between two barns.


Trapped. The fox is between the two barns.


What the drone captures next is utterly horrific – and exposes the brutal reality behind the hunting industry’s claims about scent trails.


The huntsman is already on foot, surrounded by excited hounds. He is swinging something towards them, encouraging them to grab hold. As the footage unfolds, it becomes clear that he is swinging a fox.


First the huntsman is alone shaking the fox to excite the hounds.


The hounds are repeatedly encouraged to seize the fox. Eventually, several begin to grab hold, and the huntsman encourages them further, pulling and tugging against them as though playing a game.


The huntsman blows on his horn over the hounds reinforcing the sound of the horn call with the kill.


When the hounds finally take the fox from him, he bends over them as they tear at it and then blows his hunting horn – most likely sounding the traditional call for a kill, reinforcing the hounds’ association between the horn and their quarry.


He then gives one of the terriermen a thumbs-up.


Thumbs-up.


When the hounds begin to lose interest again, the terrierman picks up the fox’s body and repeatedly shakes it in front of them, encouraging them to take hold once more. He appears to push the fox towards the hounds jaws.


The terrierman also has a go with the fox – shaking the body into the hounds jaws.


When the dogs finally grip it, he pulls against them in a grotesque tug-of-war. Once the hounds take the fox from the terrierman, the huntsman again blows his horn over them.


As more hounds join in, the terrierman pats one of the dogs. But as he does so he appears to hear the drone and looks up.


The terrierman suddenly notices the drone. Too late.


Suddenly everything changes.


The fox’s body is hurriedly retrieved from the hounds, and the two terriermen scramble to stuff it beneath the hay bales.


The men stuff the body under the haybale with their feet and put their hoods up


The huntsman immediately exits towards his horse, while the …
