author: Unknown
title: Oil exploration expands across Kurdish regions
content:
Oil drilling continues uninterrupted across Kurdish regions. Intensive drilling operations in Gabar, Cudî, Kato and Besta continue to displace local communities, devastate natural habitats, and deplete and pollute water resources. A similar situation is emerging in Batman (Êlih) and Diyarbakır (Amed), where shale oil drilling is expected to begin within the next one or two months. The Ecology Commission of the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) Headquarters and the ÖHD Şırnak (Şirnex) Branch conducted a field investigation into the ongoing ecological destruction on Mount Gabar. The delegation announced that its findings would be compiled into a report and shared with the public. According to a report published by Mezopotamya Agency (MA), the ÖHD delegation examined tree felling and activities carried out under the pretext of oil exploration, drawing attention to pollution and environmental destruction.


The Tigris River is being poisoned


Hülya Yıldırım, a member of the ÖHD Headquarters Ecology Commission, spoke to

Yeni Yaşam

 about the investigation, stressing that the ecological destruction in Gabar could not be considered separately from the wider devastation of nature across the region. Yıldırım said, “In Gabar, Besta, Cudî and many other places, we are witnessing tree felling, forest fires, mining activities and toxic thermal power plants, all of which are used as both instruments and consequences of war. Today, there is an oil well on every corner of Gabar and an oil production facility at every turn. As a result, Gabar has been blasted apart with dynamite. The Tigris River is being polluted by oil leaks and petroleum waste.”


Life is treated as a resource


Hülya Yıldırım said that oil operations threatened workers' health, environmental and public health, as well as agriculture and livestock farming. She noted that residents were still waiting to return to their villages, which had been burned and evacuated in the 1990s, but that these operations were creating further obstacles to their return. Yıldırım stressed that activities causing ecological destruction were not being carried out in accordance with legal requirements. Yıldırım said, “These areas, these mountains, this land and this river are all seen merely as resources. We will continue to oppose this mentality and the permit procedures being carried out without even complying with the existing legal framework. We will intensify our struggle and continue to share our findings with the public.”


24 shale oil wells planned


Energy and Natural Resources Minister Alparslan Bayraktar described the shale oil exploration launched in Diyarbakır as a game-changing development for Turkey. His announcement that the project would also extend to Batman raises concerns about the future of the region. Bayraktar said that new discoveries had been made in Adıyaman, where oil production had fallen below 10,000 barrels per day. He stated that steps had been taken to increase existing production by approximately 50 percent, bringing it to around 15,000 barrels per day. He added that daily production in Adıyaman was expected to reach between 14,000 and 15,000 barrels by the end of this year. Bayraktar announced that shale gas and shale oil exploration had begun in Batman and Diyarbakır using unconventional extraction methods, including hydraulic fracturing, commonly known as fracking. He said that the project, which involves horizontal drilling, was expected to begin producing results towards the end of the year. The minister added that horizontal drilling operations were scheduled to be completed in 2027, while a programme involving 24 wells would continue until 2028.


Shale oil exploration spreads across the region


Agricultural land, pastures and water resources across Şırnak, Batman and Diyarbakır are increasingly being sacrificed to oil and shale oil extraction. It had previously been announced that a shale oil well had been drilled in Bismil. The US-based company TransAtlantic Petroleum and another US company, Continental Resources, which operates alongside it in the project, reportedly injected thousands of tonnes of water mixed with chemicals underground, leading to the first oil discovery. The drilling operations cover an area of 7 million 650 thousand decares of natural habitats, pastures and agricultural land, including Bismil and Silvan (Farqîn). The first oil was reportedly reached through horizontal drilling at a depth of four kilometres. Plans …

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Burnham Approves New North Sea Gas Drilling in ‘Act of Climate Vandalism’
content:
Andy Burnham’s government has given fossil fuel giants Shell and Equinor permission to drill the undeveloped Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea.


Energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh, who publicly opposed new drilling before taking on the role, is set to make the announcement from Aberdeen on Wednesday morning alongside chancellor John Healey. 


In 2022 Fahnbulleh wrote on X: “To have a shot at staying within 1.5C global warming, we can’t have any new oil or gas fields. 


“Banks know this, but some are pumping billions into new projects. It’s irresponsible and shortsighted to be funding new fossil fuels when we need to be getting to net zero fast.”


Before becoming prime minister, Burnham endorsed calls for a fossil fuel non-proliferation treaty. “It’s not just a plan, it’s a lifeline,” he

said last year

. “It’s a call to end coal, oil, and gas, hold polluters accountable.” 


Fahnbulleh told BBC Radio Scotland on Wednesday that drilling Jackdaw “won’t lower energy bills this winter”. Numerous energy experts have said extracting the gas will not lower bills at all. “The UK is not an isolated energy island where new supply has the effect of decreasing prices,” professor Gavin Bridge, fellow of the Durham Energy Institute,

told the Independent

 in April. 


Advocacy group

Greenpeace argues

 that, based on calculations for climate harm used by the government, burning the gas from Jackdaw will cause £16.1bn in “global damage” and cause more than 8,000 heat-related deaths.


Ross Greer, co-leader of the Scottish Greens, said: “Labour’s decision to approve Jackdaw is climate vandalism. Andy Burnham’s government had the opportunity to reject the greed of oil and gas companies… Instead, this Labour prime minister has caved in to the fossil fuel lobby and continued to devastate our climate. It is a devastating betrayal of our children’s future.”


Zack Polanski, leader of the Green party of England and Wales, said: “Labour has abandoned all credibility in the fight against climate change. This is a victory for Shell over the people.”


US president Donald Trump said in July that Burnham had told him he would “open up North Sea oil”.


The government is yet to issue a decision about Rosebank, an oil field also in the North Sea owned by Shell, Equinor and a firm called Ithaca Energy, which is part-owned by Israeli holding company Delek Group.

author: Vivian La
title: In Michigan, 3 tribes are on a mission to bring back a fish that disappeared 100 years ago
content:
Even when they’re young, the characteristic iridescent hues of the Arctic grayling are noticeable at the right angle.


On a brisk morning in September, fish and wildlife biologist Sean Leask counted and measured hundreds of these fish, which were raised at the Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians’ streamside rearing facility, located just outside Traverse City in northern Michigan. 


“Some of these might be catchable by the end of next year,” Leask said. “I don’t know what their growth will look like in the wild.”


That’s because Arctic grayling haven’t been seen in Michigan waters for almost a century. By the 1930s, industrial activity like logging and overfishing, along with competition from non-native fish, had decimated their numbers. But three northern Michigan tribes and the state are trying to change that by reintroducing the fish to local waters. 


“Our taking care of them and helping them to reestablish their population helps us to reestablish ourselves, our culture, and our traditions,” said Tina Frankenberger, the Grand Traverse Band’s tribal environmental resiliency lead.


Their work joins broader efforts by tribes around the country to restore native species — from

salmon

 to

oysters

 to

condors

 — that are culturally and economically important, while also strengthening the ecosystems that these species depend on against threats like climate change.


One year into raising and releasing grayling to northern Michigan waterways, biologists with the Michigan tribes are grappling with questions about whether the fish are surviving and how to adapt their efforts to extreme weather. No released grayling have been seen in the wild. Flood conditions and the small number of fish they began with are complicating survey work.


But the tribes remain optimistic that their restoration efforts will improve as they collect more data in the coming years. Biologists think it will be around six to eight years before they can tell if grayling reintroduction has been successful.


“This is an experiment,” said Dan Mays, inland policy biologist for the Grand Traverse Band. “We’re trying our best.”


Young Arctic grayling swim in holding tanks at a Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians streamside rearing facility near Traverse City.


Vivian La / IPR News


In the summer and early fall, the Grand Traverse Band raised around 8,000 young grayling and released them into the Boardman-Ottaway River. They’re one of three northern Michigan tribes that

received grayling eggs from a state hatchery

 in 2025, along with the Little River Band of Ottawa Indians and the Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians. This was the culmination of years of planning plus millions of dollars in combined

state

,

federal

, and

private

 funding to restore ecosystems. The eggs for Michigan’s reintroduction efforts were sourced from the Chena River in Alaska, a state where Arctic grayling are plentiful and more genetically diverse than the only remaining population in the Lower 48, in

Montana’s Big Hole River

.


Mays is already feeling more optimistic about the number and the size of the grayling that the Grand Traverse Band raised compared to last year, when a power outage at the tribe’s rearing facility killed a majority of the grayling.


“Overall, four times as many grayling,” he said. “We’re also stocking a higher proportion of bigger grayling this year. Greater size, greater survival.”


Raising the grayling is one challenge. Tracking the fish to see whether they’ve survived is another. None of the three northern Michigan tribes have recaptured a grayling yet.


“It’s like looking for a needle in a haystack, and the haystack is the size of a river,” said Alex Ontkos, an inland fisheries biologist with the Little River Band of Ottawa Indians. Earlier this year, this tribe stocked 391,000 grayling eggs using in-stream incubators on the Manistee River near Kalkaska. Not all of those eggs hatched, with viability rates estimated around 50 to 60 percent, Ontkos said.


Unlike the Grand Traverse Band, the Little River Band let larvae hatch directly into the incubators, grow into tiny fry, then leave the incubator. While biologists observed tens of thousands of fry leaving the incubators, they have yet to see or recapture a grayling. 


“I don’t think that that’s because they’re not out there,” Ontkos said. “It’s just a matter of being in the right place at the right time.” The team with the Little River …

author: Peter Boyle
title: Why the billionaire class has to go
content:
One of the saddest aspects about the global wave of right-wing populism is how many people are in awe of the billionaires who are literally destroying our future.

Back in the age of feudal despots, lavish palaces, pomp and ceremony, the superstitious belief in the “divine right” of the rulers to rule helped keep the masses in line.

While many of those old superstitions have worn thin, they have been replaced by the myth that the mega rich are where they are because they have brilliant minds, or have worked their way to the top.

But this myth is also wearing thinner — thanks to United States President Donald Trump’s narcissistic outbursts and the obscene growth in the wealth of the mega rich.

All that remains in the billionaire’s ideological armoury is their capacity to fund the spread of more racism, misogyny, hate and bigotry.

Hence Trump’s toxic bullying and the blatant white supremacy propagated by Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, through his social media platform X (formerly Twitter).

The sheer amount of wealth the billionaire class has accumulated refutes the lie that it was earned through hard work. Oxfam estimates their combined wealth at $18.3 trillion.

This year, Musk became the first trillionaire.

If a worker somehow managed to save $50,000 a year, it would take 20 million years to get to a trillion dollars.

Great wealth only comes from exploiting others and plundering nature. The wealth of every billionaire has grown exponentially because it is used to make more and more people work for their profits.

The hidden power of the billionaire class is the collective labour and creativity of billions of working people. If all these people stopped working to make those billionaires profit, that wealth would not grow by a cent.

The combined wealth of the billionaire class rose by $2.5 trillion last year — enough to eradicate extreme poverty 26 times over.

Instead of eradicating poverty, billionaire rule is actually sending more people into poverty.

According to the United Nations Development Program’s (UNDP) 2026 update of its global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), 1.2 billion people (18.9%) of the 6.3 billion people in 108 countries surveyed are now living in “acute multidimensional poverty”.

MPI measures health, education and standard of living, instead of just income levels.

But even by the World Bank’s narrower measurement of poverty based on income, globally, 826 million people (10%) still live in extreme poverty.

Poverty eradication has stalled because billionaire rule continues to impose neoliberal policies of privatisation, austerity and impossible debt repayments on the poorest countries in the world. At the same time, it is degrading and destroying the environment that people depend on for survival.

On top of that, the billionaire class has imposed permanent war on a large part of the Global South to preserve its privileges and the political and military hegemony of the powerful states that protect its interests.

Four out of five people living in extreme poverty are in ecologically devastated sub-Saharan Africa, or in other fragile and conflict-affected countries.

The world lost more than 7 million hectares of forest to deforestation last year and a further 65.4 million hectares of forest “lost ecological integrity because of human activities”, according to the Forest Declaration Assessment 2026, prepared by a coalition of civil society organisations and researchers.

The out-of-control wildfires in Indonesia, which have blanketed Southeast Asia with toxic smoke for months, burnt a further 1.92 million hectares of rainforest by the end of last month, according to satellite data.

According to Planetary Boundaries Science Lab at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research’s latest annual Planetary Health Check, authored by more than 60 scientists, seven of the nine “planetary boundaries” have been transgressed.

Planetary boundaries are interconnected Earth-system processes that must remain within safe limits to preserve the planet’s stability and resilience. The seven transgressed boundaries are: Climate change; change in biosphere integrity; land system change; freshwater change; modification of biogeochemical flows; introduction of novel entities; and ocean acidification.

author: Unknown
title: Max Oelschlaeger - The Wilderness Condition
content:
Author

: Max Oelschlaeger

Title

: The Wilderness Condition

Subtitle

: Essays on Environment and Civilization

Date

: Jun 1, 1992

Source

: <

press.princeton.edu

> & <

www.archive.org

>


 


 In this age of heightened sensitivity to environmental problems, the popular press inundates us with the issues of the moment. We hear of the immediate threats to our groundwater supply, to the rain forest, to the ozone. Yet nowhere do we find coverage of the fundamental issues of environmentalism, those elements such as philosophy and history that, though less dramatic, constitute the foundation from which we can reverse ecological breakdown.


 This vital collection of essays by some of the environmental movement’s preeminent thinkers addresses these deeper, neglected issues. Written from a broad range of perspectives, the authors explore the dynamic tension between wild nature and civilization, offering insights into why the relationship has become so conflicted and suggesting creative means for reconciliation.


 Introducing the concept of the wilderness condition, the essays probe the effects of history, psychology, culture, and philosophy on the environment. Included is commentary from Gary Snyder, award-winning author of

Turtle Island,

 who discusses how our prevailing assumptions about “nature” and “wilderness” impede conservation. Paul Shepard, author of

Man in the Landscape,

 presents his compelling, controversial theory that the seeds of our current ecological crisis were planted in the New Stone Age. And George Sessions explains how the two major schools of thought in the environmental movement differ on its most basic issues, again thwarting opportunities for change.


 Other essays discuss how Western philosophy has erroneously divorced humankind from nature; why Sierra Club founder John Muir’s early writings remain eminently relevant; and how elements of Eastern philosophy may hold the key to sucessful change.


 The contributors eloquently demonstrate why we can no longer take nature for granted, or assume that its existence is somehow second to humankind’s. They argue convincingly that no amount of technology will ever displace our primal connection to nature. But rather than simply deploring the prevailing attitudes toward our imperiled environment, the essayists offer fresh, realistic, and inspiring ideas for alleviating the crisis.


 Three themes unify the collection: the essayists, though they represent different traditions, share an evolutionary perspective that confirms why humankind and nature are by necessity interdependent; sensitive to language, the writers reveal how the words we choose when we consider environmental issues reflect our sometimes naive understanding of them; and most important, the essayists share the conviction that al! is not lost—and that we can initiate a worldwide trend toward recognizing the environment as a vital entity in its own right, thereby preserving its integrity.


 


 MAX OELSCHLAEGER teaches philosophy of ecology, environmental ethics, and wilderness studies at the University of North Texas. He is author of the influential and critically acclaimed The

Idea of Wilderness,

 which explores Western culture’s persistent attempts to separate humankind from the natural world.


 


 The Sierra Club, founded in 1892 by John Muir, has devoted itself to the study and protection of the earth’s scenic and ecological resources — mountains, wetlands, woodlands, wild shores and rivers, deserts and plains. The publishing program of the Sierra Club offers books to the public as a nonprofit educational service in the hope that they may enlarge the public’s understanding of the Club’s basic concerns. The point of view expressed in each book, however, does not necessarily represent that of the Club. The Sierra Club has some sixty chapters coast to coast, in Canada, Hawaii, and Alaska. For information about how you may participate in its programs to preserve wilderness and the quality of life, please address inquiries to Sierra Club, 730 Polk Street, San Francisco, CA 94109.


 


For A. E. Koenig, in memoriam


Introduction: The Wilderness Condition Today


 by Max Oelschlaeger


 During 1989 the popular press rediscovered the environment. After almost a decade of neglect, during which time disasters such as “Bhopal” and “Chernobyl” or the misadventures of various Reagan appointments such as James Watt dominated environmental news coverage, less dramatic but …

author: Kiara Green
title: Beyond Indigenous Peoples Day: The Fight to Protect Indigenous Communities
content:
The second Monday in October is federally recognized as Christopher Columbus Day, commemorating the arrival of colonizer Christopher Columbus to the Americas. It’s undeniable that Indigenous communities lived in America long before Columbus docked his ship. Why, then, is he celebrated as the man who “discovered” America?

For years, public debate has challenged this Eurocentric narrative. In response, several states have recognised the second Monday in October as Indigenous Peoples Day. The day celebrates the resilience and the vibrant cultures of Indigenous communities in America.

Despite the lack of federal recognition, Indigenous Peoples Day continues to be celebrated while bringing attention to issues that Indigenous communities face. The day has been used to advocate for the removal of Columbus memorials, the returning of Indigenous lands, and awareness about Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women (MMIW).

The Trump administration has rejected this broader recognition. In 2025, Trump declared he was “bringing Columbus Day back from the ashes,” reinforcing the federal emphasis on celebrating Columbus rather than recognizing Indigenous peoples.

Meanwhile, proposed federal funding cuts of $2.3 billion from the administration continue to impact Tribal programs especially violence related programs and services that support survivors. These reductions could undermine essential services, including programs that address violence and support survivors.

The consequences are especially serious given the rates of violence facing Indigenous communities. On September 15, the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Federal Government Surveillance held a hearing titled “Missing and Murdered Indigenous People: Strengthening Public Safety in Tribal Communities.” Lawmakers and witnesses discussed how the federal government can help ensure the safety of Indigenous communities as they face some of the highest homicide and missing persons rates in the country.

According to the CDC, homicide was the fourth leading cause of death for American Indian and Alaska Natives men and sixth-leading cause for women ages one to 44 in 2023. Tribal communities rely on violence prevention programs and other services to address these disparities. Funding cuts threaten their ability to sustain this work.

During the September hearing, witnesses urged members to increase the funding for tribal communities to sustain these instrumental programs. Trent Shores, former U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Oklahoma, stressed that “Resources need to reach the people and stay there.” Myron Lizer, Former Vice President of Navajo Nation, similarly warned that “we have built programs but not continuous systems,” highlighting the gap between establishing initiatives and providing the sustained resources communities need.

Legislation like Savanna’s Act and the Not Invisible Act have started to address missing and murdered Native Americans by strengthening relations between federal and tribal law enforcement. However, significant gaps remain in preventing violence, investigating cases and supporting survivors.

As Indigenous communities continue to face high levels of homicide and missing person rates, Congress must continue to act and pass the Trace Act for a concise database. Honoring Indigenous resilience goes beyond annual recognition but a continued effort to guarantee sustained resources and legislative action that protect these communities from ongoing violence and funding cuts.

author: Kay Pacha / Equipo Pueblos Originarios del SERPAJ
title: La basura es una amenaza a la comunidad Nahuelpan
content:
Pareciera que las amenazas de desalojos no bastan, porque se les agregan otras que obligan a las comunidades a establecer una estrategia de resistencia y lucha. Es el caso de la Comunidad Mapuche Tehuelche Nahuelpan, quien desde el año 2009 viene enfrentando la decisión del Municipio de Esquel que instaló una planta de tratamiento de residuos urbanos en un lote vecino al territorio de la comunidad, sin realizar ninguna consulta como corresponde.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/La-basura-es-una-amenaza.mp3


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/La-basura-es-una-amenaza.mp3


Descargar archivo


En ese entonces se hicieron muchas notas y diversas presentaciones que nunca fueron respondidas. En el año 2024 los comuneros cerraron el paso de los camiones de residuos durante una semana, entonces hubo un compromiso con el Ministerio de Ambiente y la Municipalidad de Esquel que dieron  su palabra de retirar ese basurero, cosa que nunca pasó.


Fue entonces cuando comienza una instancia legal, ya que el Municipio administra los residuos del Parque Nacional Los Alerces, Trevelin y zonas aledañas a Esquel.


En esa oportunidad, se tomaron muestras, que determinaron un alto grado de contaminación del suelo con niquel y cobalto e hidrocarburos en el agua. Hubo varias denuncias penales, que fueron desestimadas por falta de pruebas y actualmente la situación se va agravando, ya que hay proyectado la instalación de un crematorio y otro de manipulación de residuos patológicos y residuos lubricantes, industriales y combustibles automotrices.


Cabe recordar que esta comunidad tiene una historia de lucha, ya que allá por 1908 se les reconoció una reserva de 19000 hectáreas, pero en 1937 un decreto de facto anuló esa medida y derivó en un desalojo violento y la división de los terrenos entre terratenientes y particulares. Si bien en 1948 se les restituyó una porción menor, los reclamos de tierras ancestrales continuaron.


Por eso decimos que hay comunidades que a raíz de las diferentes amenazas que vienen sufriendo, deben organizarse para trazar estrategias de resistencia y lucha y esta comunidad es una de ellas.


Entonces, para tener más claridad y conocimiento de la situación, vamos a escuchar a Grabriel Nahuelquir, referente de la Comunidad Mapuche Tehuelche Nahuelpan y a Sonia Ivanoff, abogada y apoderada de la comunidad.


El Micro Kay Pacha se realiza con el apoyo de la organización Otto per Mille-Chiessa Valdense.

La basura es una amenaza a la comunidad Nahuelpan

author: Rachel Sherrington and Hazel Healy
title: How Big Pharma Tried to Weaken the Rules of the UN’s Nature Fund
content:
As the COP17 nature summit gets underway in Armenia, evidence has emerged of lobbying by a leading international pharmaceuticals group to weaken the terms of a flagship fund for nature.


Documents analysed by DeSmog show that the International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations (IFPMA)

called

 for a “radical rethink” of the rationale for the

landmark

 Cali Fund – the first mechanism built to take voluntary payments from large companies that profit from genetic sequence data.


The IFPMA states that the “modalities of the decision” to establish the Fund – which was ratified by 196 countries in 2024 at the COP16 summit of the UN Convention on Biological Diversity in Colombia – should be “significantly reviewed, revised and clarified”.


In the consultation submission, the trade group – which

represents

 the pharmaceutical sector at the UN – also challenged the indicative rates at which companies were invited to contribute to the Fund, agreed at COP16 as 0.1 percent of revenue or 1 percent of profit.

The IFPMA labelled these indicative rates as “premature”, set “without any rational analysis”, and “commercially unrealistic”, suggesting instead that companies be allowed to contribute to the voluntary fund at a level of their choosing. 


Other demands from the IFPMA included a guarantee that any contribution would explicitly substitute payments for digital sequence information required under national or international laws.

Despite contributions to the Cali Fund already being voluntary, following a fierce

lobbying push

 at the last summit, the IFPMA also seeks a guarantee they will remain so, stating that “there are elements in the decision that do not go far enough in creating a truly voluntary mechanism”.


Responses from other sectors, such as biotechnology and cosmetics – which are listed alongside pharma and artificial intelligence firms in the treaty text as industries that should contribute – echo some of the IFPMA’s objections, and appear to be reluctant to support the Fund as it is currently conceived. 


The UK Bioindustry Association (UK BIA), which

has

 600 biotech and life sciences companies among its members,

says

 the CBD’s expectations for what the Fund can raise are currently set “unrealistically high”, in its consultation response dated March 2025. 


UK BIA states that “for the Fund to succeed in the long term”, questions over its design and operationalisation must be addressed, and “clear incentives” created. 


The revelations come as negotiators gather for the UN biodiversity summit in Armenia this week, with just $10,000

pledged

 by companies to the Cali Fund. 


It falls far short of the $1 billion to $10 billion that the UN had

hoped

 the Fund could draw in every year, half of which is mandated to flow directly to the Indigenous and local communities that steward biodiversity.


“The tiny amounts contributed to the Cali Fund so far, combined with continued delays from industry, send a clear signal: voluntary contributions are simply not delivering,” An Lambrechts, a biodiversity politics expert at Greenpeace International, told DeSmog. 


The latest UN report shows that the world is

off track on

author: labor4pal
title: Dezionizing the University of California
content:
Sean Malloy and Ethnic Studies Council at UC

In September 2025, I wrote a guest post for Chris Newfield’s blog that highlighted the complicity of UC leadership and the Academic Senate in federal attacks on the university under the guise of combating antisemitism. In a follow-up guest post in May 2026, I identified Zionism as the driving force behind many of the external and internal threats to the UC and its faculty, staff, and students. Building on those earlier writings, I want to explore at some length what it would mean to “dezionize” the University of California. Anti-Zionism is not new and has existed since the creation of the Zionist political movement. Given the stakes of the current moment, however, it is not enough to be simply anti-Zionist in orientation. It is past time that we consider the real, material steps that we must take to both sever the UC’s connections to Zionism and address the current and past harms created by those connections.

Dezionization entails not only ending the UC’s complicity in the genocidal actions of the Israeli state (which would include divestment and the end of formal research and teaching collaborations with Israeli-linked entities), but also confronting the role of Zionist organizations, donors, Regents, and administrators in repression targeted at members of the university community. Since 2023, students, faculty, and staff have been the subject of individual discipline and surveillance while entire university policies have been written or re-written to institutionalize compulsory Zionism and stifle those who would speak out on behalf of Palestinian life. Confronting and redressing these individual and structural harms is a crucial element of any meaningful dezionization effort. And while addressing the issues of post-10/7 complicity and repression are important immediate goals, dezionization also requires an honest accounting of the historical role of Zionism at the UC. Building on the flawed but necessary efforts of universities to acknowledge their historical connections to slavery and indigenous genocide and disposession, dezionization must also involve acknowledging and at least attempting to redress past harms resulting from the UC’s long entanglement with Zionism.

Thanks for reading Ethnic Studies Council @ UC! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.Subscribe

Dezionization does not require that individual staff, faculty, or students renounce their own personal beliefs. It does insist that the UC as an institution should neither advance nor be beholden to a political project that has fueled genocide in historic Palestine and repression on our own campuses.

Dezionization is neither an easy task nor will it solve all of the problems currently confronting the UC. Ultimately, however, the current status quo is both immoral and untenable and those who care about the university’s future are going to need to commit to a series of radical changes which include, but are not limited to, confronting the corrosive effects of Zionism. If pursued correctly, the process of dezionization will itself contribute to making the university more democratic, anti-racist, and accountable to all. And while I have focused on the UC in this essay because it is where I have worked and organized for 21 years, my goal in writing this is to spark conversation about how we might move forward with dezionization in all the institutions in which we are entangled, wherever those might be.

Before considering what dezionization might look like in practice, it is important to directly confront the question of what Zionism is — and what it is not. Contemporary defenders of Israel have mounted an aggressive campaign asserting that Zionism is an integral part of Jewish religious andethnic identity. In a 2022 complaint filed against the UC Berkeley law school with the Department of Education targeting several student organizations who refused to platform Zionist speakers, attorneys Gabriel Groisman and Arsen Ostrovsky asserted that “A rejection of Zionism. . . is an act of antisemitism and direct assault upon the very core ethnic and racial identity of Jewish students.” Kenneth Marcus, a former George W. title: Söke Ekmek ve Gül açıklaması: Her çocuğa okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı yemek istiyoruz
content:
Aydın - Söke'de Belediye Meydanı’nda Söke Ekmek ve Gül "Bir Öğün Ücretsiz Sağlıklı Yemek Güvenli Okul Güvenli Ulaşım İstiyoruz” diyerek basın açıklaması yaptı.

Söke Ekmek ve Gül’ün çağrısıyla yapılan açıklamaya veliler, Söke Kadın Dayanışma Derneği ve Söke Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri de destek verdi. "Bir öğün ücretsiz sağlıklı yemek güvenli okul güvenli ulaşım istiyoruz” pankartının açıldığı basın açıklamasıni Söke Ekmek ve Gül adına öğrenci velisi Huri Abrinç okudu.

Çocukların okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı ve dengeli yemek yiyebilmesi için yıllardır ülkenin dört bir yanında ve Söke’de aralıksız mücadele ettiklerini belirten Abrinç; “Söke Ekmek ve Gül olarak imza kampanyaları düzenledik, stantlar açtık, çocukların beslenme hakkını kararlılıkla savunduk. 2022 yılında Ekmek ve Gül tarafından başlatılan, 2023’te Kocaeli Ekmek ve Gül Kadın Dayanışma Derneği’nin çalışmalarıyla büyüyen, Esenyalı Kadın Dayanışma Derneği üyesi bir kadının hukuki mücadelesine kadar uzanan bu talep; bugün Türkiye’nin her köşesindeki kadınların, velilerin, öğretmenlerin ve eğitim emekçilerinin ortak talebidir. Toplanan binlerce imza, yapılan basın açıklamaları ve dayanışma ağları bu ihtiyacın ne kadar hayati, acil ve vazgeçilmez olduğunu defalarca kanıtlamıştır.

Çünkü biliyoruz ki derinleşen ekonomik kriz ortamında çocukların okula aç gittiği, ailelerin beslenme çantalarını doldurmakta zorlandığı, temel gıda ürünlerinin dahi lüks hâline geldiği bir ülkede; sağlıklı beslenme bir lütuf veya yardım değil, en temel insan hakkıdır. Çocuklar açken eğitimde fırsat eşitliğinden ya da nitelikli bir eğitimden söz edilemez” dedi.

Yürütülen bu haklı mücadeleler ve yükselen kamuoyu baskısı sonucunda Millî Eğitim Bakanlığının 5-19 Ekim tarihleri arasında ücretsiz okul yemeğine ilişkin velilerin görüşlerini almak amacıyla bir anket süreci yürüttüğünü hatırlatan Abrinç: “Yıllardır dile getirilen bu yakıcı ihtiyacı anlamak için çocukların açlığının bu kadar derinleşmesini bekleyen Bakanlığa soruyoruz: Velilerin ve kadınların sesi neden bugüne kadar duyulmadı” sorusunu sordu.

Bakanlığın adım atması önemli olsa da, yürütülen anketin kapsamı, erişilebilirliği ve yöntemi ciddi soru işaretleri doğurduğunu vurgulayan Abrinç anketle ilgili eksiklikleri sıraladı:

İnternet üzerinden yürütülen ankete pek çok veli eşit biçimde katılamamıştır. Veliler ankete ulaşmaya çalıştıklarında "yetkiniz yok" uyarılarıyla, sistemde yaşanan teknik sorunlarla karşılaşmış; internet ve telefon imkânı bulunmayan ya da dijital araçları kullanmakta zorlanan aileler süreçten tamamen izole edilmiştir. Ayrıca anket hakkında velilere yeterli bilgilendirme yapılmamıştır.

Edindiğimiz bilgilere göre ilkokul öğrencileri anket kapsamı dışında tutulmuş, süreç yalnızca ortaokul ve lise düzeyine sıkıştırılmıştır. Oysa en temel gelişim çağındaki ilkokul ve okul öncesi çocukların beslenme hakkı nasıl göz ardı edilebilir?

Servis imkânlarının kaldırılması veya kısıtlanmasıyla mağdur edilen taşımalı eğitim kapsamındaki aileler, bu anket hakkında da yeterince bilgilendirilmemiştir. Çocukların ulaşım ve beslenme ihtiyaçları birlikte değerlendirilmelidir.”

“İnternete erişemeyen, yetki engeline takılan ya da anket kapsamına alınmayan çocukların sağlıklı beslenmeye ihtiyacı yok mu? Çocukların en temel hakkı, teknik aksaklıklarla dolu bir anketin sonucuna ya da hangi eğitim kademesinde olduğuna indirgenebilir mi?” sorularını soran Abrinç, “Bir ankete katılamamış olmak, ücretsiz yemek ihtiyacının olmadığı anlamına gelmez! Çocukların açlığı anket sorularıyla giderilemez; beslenme sorumluluğu yalnızca ailelerin ve kadınların omuzlarına yıkılamaz” ifadelerini kullandı

Mıllî Eğitim Bakanlığına ve yetkililere çağrı yapan Abrinç şu talepleri sıraladı

Eşit ve Koşulsuz Hak: Okul öncesinden liseye kadar, kamu okullarındaki tüm öğrencilere ayrım yapılmaksızın her gün bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı ve dengeli yemek derhal sağlanmalıdır.

Anket Sonucu Beklenmemelidir: Ücretsiz okul yemeği bir anketin sonucuna bağlanmadan, bütçe bahanelerinin arkasına sığınmadan kalıcı bir kamu hizmeti olarak uygulamaya konulmalıdır.

Şeffaflık ve Hesap Verilebilirlik: Yapılan anketin kaç veliye ulaştığı, hangi kademeleri kapsadığı ve sonuçların nasıl değerlendirildiği kamuoyuyla açık ve şeffaf bir şekilde paylaşılmalıdır.

Erişilebilir Katılım Yöntemleri: Dijital araçları kullanamayan veya erişim sorunu yaşayan veliler için yüz yüze görüşmeler, basılı formlar ve okullar aracılığıyla katılım kanalları oluşturulmalıdır.

author: Ayurdhi Dhar, PhD
title: Being Mindful of Agony: How to Incorporate the Sublime in Our Daily Life—An Interview with Will Adams
content:
H

ow does a wounded world wound us in return? Can we be mindful and offer intimate attention to pain and trauma? We answer these and other questions with Will Adams who is an Associate Professor and Chair of the Department of Psychology at Duquesne University in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. He holds a PhD in Clinical Psychology from Duquesne and completed his clinical psychology internship at McLean Hospital, affiliated with Harvard Medical School.


Dr. Adams is the author of

A Wild and Sacred Call: Nature-Psyche-Spirit

, published by SUNY Press, a book that explores the deep connections between human psychology, the natural world, and spirituality. His work brings together phenomenology, relational psychoanalysis, Gestalt therapy, transpersonal psychology, and contemplative traditions, particularly Zen Buddhism and Christian mysticism.


His scholarship invites us to reconsider the relationship between self and world, mind and nature, and psychological healing and spiritual life. In this very personal interview, we’ll be speaking with him about how a lifetime of contemplative practice came to his rescue during the most traumatic time in his life, the possibilities of a relational understanding of human and more-than-human experience, and what psychology might learn from contemplative traditions and our relationship with the natural world.


The transcript below has been edited for length and clarity. Listen to the audio of the interview here.


Ayurdhi Dhar: Dr. Adams, you’ve learned from multiple traditions—Christian mysticism, Buddhism, and phenomenology, which is the study of lived experience. How did all of these come together?


Will Adams:

 First, I want to say that I appreciate this opportunity to have this conversation. I want to thank you and thank Mad in America for touching folks in a deep way, especially many folks that have been marginalized and wounded.


This was during my undergraduate years at University of North Carolina which got me interested in humanistic and existential psychology. I had powerful experiences with a roommate in college and then later volunteering at a state psychiatric hospital. I started reading people like Martin Buber and R. D. Laing, and I found my way to a wonderful master’s program at University of West Georgia. You and I both are alums from that program. That program changed my life.


I went to London to study with R. D. Laing. Then I came to Duquesne as a PhD student and immersed myself in not just phenomenology, but the larger human science psychology tradition. I became interested in meditation. I practiced Vipassana meditation for 11 years, and then a wonderful Zen teacher fell into my life, Bruce Harris; I’ve been practicing with him for 26 years now.


I’m practicing psychotherapy and bringing these sensibilities into the therapy. Later I realized that with all the ecological destruction and desecration, with our human plundering of the natural world, the more-than-human natural world, that psychology has something to say about this, because it’s not only a biological problem—habitat destruction, mass extinction, climate change. It’s a malady of consciousness and culture, and psychology has something to say about consciousness and culture. All of this sparked me to do work in eco-psychology.


Dhar: You spoke about suffering; a lot of our readers are privy to what suffering is. They’re often people with lived experience of terrible psychological distress and also of horrid institutional responses that we have to that distress. You mentioned working at the state psychiatric hospital, and how that was an important experience for you. Could you share your experience at the Halloween carnival at the institution?


Adams:

 That experience, and also the one with my college roommate were life-changing. We were roommates and dear friends. He was realizing that he was gay, and this was at a time when it was much more dangerous to express than today. We had long, intimate conversations about his excitement, his suffering, his confusion, and his inspiration. This is before I studied psychology, but through those conversations, his trust and generosity, and his opening to me, I realized that really being with another person, and listening intimately and openly is transformative.


That was right at the time I volunteered at the state psychiatric hospital. It was a bleak place, not quite as extreme as the depiction in

One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest

, but similar. I was …

author: Kodao Productions
title: The Political Economy of Healthcare and the PhilHealth Dilemma: Social Insurance or Socialized Medicine?
content:
By

Prof. Sarah Raymundo


Angelo V. Suarez

’s sharp intervention in response to Cielo Magno’s senatorial campaign line brings a vital structural issue into the public sphere. Credit must be given to Magno: her platform draws directly from a concrete social issue plaguing the vast majority of Filipinos—a crisis of public health and economic vulnerability that demands urgent collective attention. Unlike the posture of mainstream politicians running on empty campaigns, abstract pledges of service, and hollow soundbites, Magno brings a substantive issue to the table that gives the citizenry something real to evaluate and debate.


It is precisely this substance that prompted Suarez—a poet, creative industry worker, and staunch peasant advocate for the Unyon ng mga Manggagawa sa Agrikultura (UMA)—to respond, participate, and rally his friends and comrades around this critical issue. While one might be tempted to label this response as a “new politics” brought forward by figures from late Generation X and early Millennial cohorts, its core is rooted in a fundamental class politics challenging mainstream governance in the Philippines. This intervention offers an opportunity to build on our collective arsenal of knowledge and critique regarding the current Philippine health system. It aims to foster a well-informed, critical citizenry whose stakes in national elections must be elevated to what the working people truly deserve. What is at stake in this counter-critique is the necessity of deepening public deliberation on genuine reforms—and examining how these immediate struggles can advance more systemic, transformative aspirations for society.


Dissecting the Policy Platform and the Critique


In her published academic research—such as her study on pharmaceutical competition for the Philippine Competition Commission—Magno approaches the issue of expensive medicines through neoclassical market regulation. She does not advocate for breaking away from foreign drug monopolies or building a state-owned pharmaceutical industry. Instead, she identifies high medicine prices as a symptom of insufficient market competition, brand bias, and distorted prescribing behaviors. Her proposed remedy relies on market regulation: using antitrust oversight to encourage generic competition, alongside using PhilHealth as a bulk purchaser to negotiate lower prices from private pharmaceutical suppliers and absorb outpatient drug costs.


Angelo Suarez’s critique dismantles this reformist premise at its structural foundation. Suarez’s actual text makes four direct arguments:


First, policy directions that prioritize a “stronger” PhilHealth obstruct the creation of a strong public health system. Second, PhilHealth fosters and entrenches an insurance system that welcomes and relies upon the private health sector. Third, the state must directly fund the supply side by hiring health workers with security of tenure and reasonable wages, building accessible facilities staffed by well-trained personnel, and establishing a nationalized pharmaceutical industry grounded in a program of national industrialization. Fourth, health services can and should be made entirely free, funded directly out of general state taxes without resorting to PhilHealth as an insurance middleman.


While Suarez articulates these core demands, this analysis extends his critique by placing it within the broader frameworks of international political economy, World Bank policy history, and Samir Amin’s theory of imperialist value transfer. Suarez identifies the political demands; this intervention maps the structural mechanisms behind them.


The core dispute between Magno’s platform and Suarez’s counter-position is not over whether Filipinos deserve access to medical care, but over the mechanism through which that care is delivered.


Magno advocates for demand-side financing, where the state acts as an insurer buying health services and imported medicines on behalf of citizens within a market economy. Suarez advocates for supply-side direct provision, where the state directly owns, operates, and funds the physical, human, and industrial infrastructure of health as an unmediated public good. #


 


The post

The Political Economy of Healthcare and the PhilHealth Dilemma: Social Insurance or Socialized Medicine?

 appeared first on

Kodao Productions

title: Immer nur Behindertenwerkstätten: Warum verdienen Menschen mit Behinderung so wenig? Und wo bleibt die Inklusion?

In der Pandemie sind beinahe unbemerkt Löhne in Behindertenwerkstätten gekürzt worden. Schon vorher ließ sich von den Geld kaum leben. (…) Der Lohn der Beschäftigten in Behinderten-Werkstätten setzt sich in Deutschland aus mehreren Teilen zusammen: Ein sogenanntes Arbeitsförderungsgeld von 52 Euro wird aus Töpfen des Landes gezahlt. Dazu kommt ein Grundlohn von 89 Euro und ein individuell festgelegter Steigerungsbetrag. Diese beiden Posten müssen die Werkstätten selbst erwirtschaften. Als die Corona-Pandemie Deutschland erreichte, schlossen die Betreiber ihre Werkstätten für Menschen mit Behinderung. In der Folge konnten viele Aufträge nicht mehr erfüllt werden. Der Steigerungslohn entfiel. (…) 19 Prozent der Werkstätten, die an der Umfrage teil nahmen, gaben an, Löhne gekürzt zu haben. Weitere 18 Prozent gaben an, dass Kürzungen absehbar sind. Insgesamt hat sich in der Umfrage gezeigt, dass die Auswirkungen der Krise verzögert in den Werkstätten ankommen

Jürgen Linnemann arbeitet 24,3 Stunden pro Woche und erhält nur einen Stundenlohn von rund 2 Euro. Im Monat macht das knapp 200 Euro. Der 57-Jährige ist Teil eines Teams, das Dokumente digitalisiert. Bevor die Papiere gescannt werden, entfernt Linnemann die Tackerklammern. Für seine Tätigkeit im Werkstattrat – einer Art Betriebsrat – hat er bereits das Bundesverdienstkreuz erhalten.

title: Sağlık Bakanlığı: Eşitsizlikleri devam ettirmekte kararlıyız!
content:
Sağlık Bakanlığı İstatistik Yıllığı (SBİY) 2025 Haber Bülteni, 30 Eylül 2025, çarşamba günü, saat 17:00’de 

(!)

 yayımlandı. İlki 12 yıl önce, 2014 yılında yine eylül ayının son günü SBİY 2013 Haber Bülteni olarak yayımlanmıştı. Bülten, istatistik yıllığından yaklaşık üç, dört ay önce daha az sayıdaki veri grubunu kapsayacak şekilde yayımlanıyor. Bununla birlikte, ölümlülük, aşılama ve hizmet kullanımıyla ilgili bir önceki yılın verilerine 9-10 ay sonra da olsa ulaşabilmiş oluyoruz. Ve Türkiye’nin dokuz ilinin bulunduğu coğrafyada yaşayanların, AKP’li yılların bundan önceki 16 yılında olduğu gibi, 17nci yılında da değişmeyen bir biçimde sağlık ve sosyoekonomik eşitsizlere mahkûm edilmiş olduğunu görüyoruz. Bu haftaki yazıda söz konusu durumu ve AKP’li Sağlık Bakanlığı’nın verileri kendine saklamak gibi bir özelliğini kendilerinin sunduğu kaynaklar üzerinden ele alacağım.


ERİŞ BİLALOĞLU YAZDI


Yeni Bir Sıfırlama Çabası mı: Türkiye’de Bebek Ölüm Hızı


29 Ocak 2015


AKP’li bakanlık verileri kendine saklıyor


AKP tarafından 2002 yılında kurulan 58. Hükümet’e kadar sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili veriler yıllardır istatistik yıllıklarıyla düzenli olarak kamuoyuyla paylaşılıyordu. Ancak

58. Hükümet ve o kabinenin Sağlık Bakanı Recep Akdağ ile birlikte, sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili veriler kamuoyundan 2011 yılına kadar saklandı,

paylaşılmadı. Dünya Sağlık Örgütü başta olmak üzere, Türkiye’nin üyesi olduğu uluslararası kuruluşların talebi üzerine, bir AKP Hükümeti ve Sağlık Bakanı olarak ilk defa 2011 yılında, 2008 yılına ait veriler “Sağlık Bakanlığı Sağlık İstatistikleri Yıllığı 2008” başlığında Bakan Akdağ’ın önsözüyle yayımlandı. O nedenle Türkiye’nin 2003-2007 yıllarına ait sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili verileri diğer yıllar gibi düzenli bir biçimde bugüne kadar paylaşılmadı.


Sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili istatistikler, 2011 yılından sonra, Sağlık Bakanlığı ve Türkiye İstatistik Kurumu (TÜİK) tarafından düzenli olarak yayımlanıyor. TÜİK, özelikle doğurganlık ve ölümlülükle ilgili verileri Merkezi Nüfus İdaresi Sistemi (MERNİS) üzerinden iller düzeyinde, sağlık harcamalarıyla ilgili verileri Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı ile Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (SGK) ve yerel yönetimlerden ve “Hanehalkı Bütçe Anketi” çalışması üzerinden, hastalıklarla ilgili verileri de “Türkiye Sağlık Araştırması” üzerinden sağlıyor. Sağlık Bakanlığı da bu verileri kullanıp yaptığı hesaplamaları ve sağlık kurumları, sağlık emekçileri, ilaç, sağlık hizmetleri kullanımı vb. verileri Türkiye’nin makro düzeyde ekonomik ve sosyo-ekonomik yapıya göre gruplandığı 12 bölge, İstatistiki Bölge Bilgileri Sınıflaması-1 (İBBS-1), üzerinden paylaşıyor. Bununla birlikte, 

Sağlık Bakanlığı kaynakları üzerinden 81 ilden herhangi birinin sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleri verilerini, durumunu öğrenebilmek mümkün olamıyor.

Çünkü Sağlık Bakanlığı illerin verilerini yayımlamayı uzun zamandır tercih etmiyor.

Bebek ölüm hızı önemli bir toplumsal sağlık düzeyi göstergesidir


Toplumların sağlık düzeyinin değerlendirilmesi ve izlenebilmesi amacıyla “bebek ölüm hızı”, “beş yaş altı ölüm hızı” ve “doğumda beklenen yaşam süresi” uluslararası alanda sıklıkla kullanılan, kabul görmüş üç değişkendir. Bunlar aynı zamanda, ülkelerin gelişmişlik düzeyi göstergeleri arasında da yer almaktadır. Çünkü, bu üç gösterge bir ülkede, bölgede, ilde vb. öncelikle beslenme, barınma, alt yapı ve eğitim başta olmak üzere, sosyoekonomik koşulların durumu ve sağlık hizmetlerinin ulaşılabilir olup olmamasıyla sağlık hizmetlerinin niteliğinden doğrudan etkilenmektedir.


Gebeliğin herhangi bir döneminde, canlı doğan bebeğin, birinci doğum gününü göremeden ölmesi, nüfus bilim (demografi) ve tıp alanında bebek ölümü olarak kabul edilmekte, tanımlanmaktadır. author: Elizabeth Weill-Greenberg
title: Tablets Make Communication Easier Behind Bars — But Deaf People Are Left Behind
content:
A lawsuit in Illinois charges that prisons blocking videophone capabilities violate the Americans with Disabilities Act.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Tablet computers have revolutionized communication inside prisons for hearing prisoners. Prison systems from across the country — including in New York, California, and Illinois — have distributed tens of thousands of tablets to incarcerated people, which they can use to call home, watch movies, message loved ones, or attend virtual classes (although they are often charged predatory fees for accessing these benefits). As of 2022, 25 state prison systems had tablet distribution programs, according to the Electronic Privacy Information Center.

But as the rollout of such tablets continues, many deaf incarcerated people have been left behind.

Disability justice organization HEARD points out that it’s unknown how many deaf people are incarcerated in U.S. prisons, but a 2015 report by the Bureau of Labor Statistics estimated that 6.2 percent of incarcerated people in state and federal prisons have a hearing disability, which would equal about 71,000 people.

Daniel Valenzuela, who is deaf, is incarcerated at Danville Correctional Center in Illinois. Last year, the Illinois Department of Corrections (IDOC) distributed tablets to all incarcerated people. But IDOC blocks videophone capabilities, preventing Valenzuela from communicating in his primary language, American Sign Language (ASL).

In September, Valenzuela sued the IDOC director for violating the Americans with Disabilities Act.

“I have six kids, four grandkids, and one of my sons is in the military. I cherish and love my family so much,” said Valenzuela in a press release announcing the lawsuit. “I just want to tell them happy birthday and I am so grieved when I can’t call because I don’t want them to think I forgot.”

There are at least three other deaf individuals at Danville who primarily use ASL to communicate, according to the complaint filed by Disability Rights Advocates, Equip for Equality, and the law firm Much Shelist.

“Across the Illinois Department of Corrections, people can use tablets to communicate with their loved ones, which has been a game changer in removing restrictions on communication,” Valenzuela’s attorney, Rachel Weisberg, the directing attorney at Disability Rights Advocates, told Truthout. “But for Mr. Valenzuela and other deaf people who use American Sign Language, that same access simply isn’t available.”

IDOC did not respond to a request for comment by the time of publication.

Last year, in addition to distributing tablets to incarcerated people, IDOC announced it would provide every incarcerated person with 775 free domestic phone call minutes per month. In a press release, IDOC said that these initiatives, working in tandem, “enhance family connections and increase access to technology that supports rehabilitation.”

But deaf prisoners are excluded from accessing these critical programs.

Unlike hearing prisoners who can use their tablets to make calls from their cells, Valenzuela must get a guard’s permission to walk to another building to use the one videophone that’s available to him. In at least one instance, Valenzuela had to go out in the pouring rain to use the videophone, according to the complaint.

“When prison officials don’t communicate with deaf/disabled people in ways they can understand, they may be written up for being ‘non-compliant.'”

The videophone is often unavailable because the unit itself breaks down, the prison is on lockdown, or a guard denies his request, according to the complaint. Last year, Valenzuela was unable to speak with his family during the holidays because the phone was not working for 54 straight days, from November 2025 to January 2026. However, if the tablets malfunction, there are several backup phones that incarcerated hearing people can use, the complaint says.

“We’re asking for equal access, as that’s what the law requires,” said Weisberg. “Equal access is not static — it must reflect the benefits currently offered to others and account for the needs of people with disabilities as technology and communication systems evolve.”

These issues are not limited to Illinois. Advocates say incarcerated deaf people have to contend with discriminatory communication practices in prisons throughout the country.

author: Unknown
title: Antiterro et psychiatrie : un bref récap de la loi Rodwell
content:
Quelques infos sur la loi Rodwell, ou loi Philippine, passée fin juillet 2026


La loi Rodwell ou loi Philippine (oui oui, Philippine comme la meuf assassinée par un type sortant de

CRA

 en septembre 2024, provoquant une campagne de haine raciste et xénophobe), ou loi du 27 juillet 2026, est une loi qui mixe le droit pénal, le droit de la santé et le droit des étrangers pour «

 

prévenir le passage à l'acte terroriste

 

» - ambiance minority report.


Pour résumer, c'est un renforcement ou une adaptation de mesures répressives qui étaient déjà souvent présentes - et mises en place - dans le droit français : il y a peu de choses complètement nouvelles. On trouve intéressant d'analyser ici quelques unes de ses principales mesures, notamment du fait des liens étroits entre répression et psychiatrie, qui sont très explicites dans la loi.


La loi met en place :


1) Une rétention de sûreté terroriste à l'issue de la peine : enfermement d'une personne dans des établissements «

 

socio-médico-judiciaires de sûreté

 

» après l'exécution complète de sa peine. Cette mesure concernerait les personnes condamnées à une peine d'au moins quinze ans pour un crime de terrorisme. Une commission, peu avant la fin de la peine, doit déterminer si la personne présente une «

 

particulière dangerosité

 

», concept carrément flou évalué notamment sur des critères encore plus flous comme le «

 

risque de récidive

 

», «

 

l'adhésion persistante à une idéologie terroriste

 

» et un «

 

trouble grave de la personnalité

 

»...


Comme pour la plupart des mesures d'enfermement dans des établissements assimilables à des

HP

, il n'y a pas de durée maximale prévue par la loi - en général c'est un an, reconductible à peu près indéfiniment (le principe c'est que la personne y reste jusqu'à ce qu'elle ne représente plus un danger pour la société...)


Il est intéressant de noter que des mesures similaires existaient déjà depuis 2008 pour certains crimes de «

 

droit commun

 

» : meurtre, viol, torture, actes de barbarie, séquestration et enlèvement. Ça concernerait très peu de personnes actuellement, mais on se doute que cette loi va permettre de renflouer les dispositifs existants.


2) Une injonction préfectorale d'examen psychiatrique : de ce qu'on comprend, à n'importe quel moment (pas besoin d'être en gav ou en examen, ou même d'avoir «

 

troublé l'ordre public

 

»), le préfet peut obliger une personne à subir un examen psychiatrique approfondi - par un psychiatre figurant sur une liste établie par la cour d'appel. C'est vraiment sur la base de suspicion de «

 

radicalisation

 

» et de «

 

troubles mentaux

 

». Et bon quand on sait que les fichiers d'Hopsyweb sur les personnes hospitalisées sous contraintes sont croisés avec ceux des «

 

fichiers de traitement des signalements pour la prévention de la radicalisation à caractère terroriste

 

», cela fait déjà une bonne liste de potentiels suspects. Si le certificat médical émis par le psychiatre va dans ce sens, le préfet peut décider d'interner la personne en

HP

 sans son consentement (mais ça, ça existait déjà bien avant). Autant préciser que cette visite au toubib n'est pas facultative : on a la possibilité de faire appel au juge administratif en théorie, mais si on refuse de voir le psychiatre ou si on ne s'y présente pas dans le délai imparti, c'est perquiz, pour se rendre au rendez-vous sous escorte.


3) Une mesure judiciaire de rétention pour les condamnés de droit commun «

 

radicalisés

 

» - là, la loi viserait spécifiquement les gens qui seraient passés par la taule (au moins 10 ans) pour des faits non-liés au terrorisme, mais se seraient «

 

radicalisés

 

» en prison. Là encore, en fin de peine, une commission évalue si le détenu présente une «

 

dangerosité particulière

 

». Si oui, et contrairement à la rétention de sûreté terroriste, la personne n'est pas ré-enfermée, mais elle a droit à l'équivalent d'un suivi

SPIP

 très renforcé, pour veiller à sa «

 

réintégration

 

» : ce suivi peut inclure une obligation de taff ou de formation, un suivi psychiatrique, l'obligation d'habiter dans une zone déterminée... En gros, un contrôle très approfondi de la vie de la personne dans ses moindres aspects.


4) Le renforcement des

MICAS

title: Gök yarılırken cepheye sürülür gibi: İstanbul’un altında kalanlar
content:
Valilik “zorunlu olmadıkça dışarı çıkmayın” dedi. Fabrikada, tersanede, sokakta, hastanede çalışanlar için o zorunluluğu yine patronlar belirledi.

19 yaşındaki Mazlum Gürbüz, 29 Eylül'de Eyüpsultan Kemerburgaz'daki bir şantiyede yağmur hafifler hafiflemez tabela montajı için sahaya geri çağrıldı. Elindeki metal çıta yüksek gerilim hattına değdi, bir haftalık yaşam mücadelesinin ardından 5 Ekim'de hayatını kaybetti. Çocukluk arkadaşı Levent Çelik, o gün neden işi bırakamadıklarını şöyle anlatmıştı: “İşten çıkarılma korkusuyla mecbur kaldık, çalıştık.”

Aradan iki hafta geçmeden İstanbul ve çevresi çok daha büyük bir sağanakla boğuştu. Valilik okulları tatil etti, kamuda yalnızca belli gruplara idari izin verdi, motokuryeleri trafikten çekti ve halka “zorunlu olmadıkça dışarı çıkmayın” çağrısı yaptı. Özel sektörde çalışan milyonlar için ise tek bir düzenleme çıkmadı.

Kocaeli Başiskele'de Hayat Kimya ve Özka Lastik fabrikalarını su bastı, işçi servisleri tekerlek hizasına kadar suya gömüldü. Arslanbey OSB'de işçiler fabrikaya suların içinden geçerek ulaştı. Ford Otosan'da su basan bölümlerde işçiler sırılsıklam çalıştı. Tuzla ve Yalova tersanelerinde üretim bir an bile aksamadı, vinçlerin yalnızca “kontrollü” kullanılması istendi.

Bunlar ulaşabildiklerimiz. Ulaşamadığımız nice işyerinde de afet koşullarında bile kâr hesabı işçinin canının önüne kondu. Bu koşullarda çalıştırılan her işçi, kapıda bekleyen yeni bir Mazlum Gürbüz demek.

PTT'de taşeron olarak çalışan üç çocuk babası bir dağıtımcı, paketleri sokak sokak yürüyerek dağıtıyor. Çarşamba 165 paketle çıktı, ancak 135'ini teslim edebildi. Dün yine sokaktaydı: “Valilik 'zorunlu olmadıkça çıkmayın' demiş ama bize kimse 'bugün çalışmayın' demedi. Bu sabah da 130 paketle çıktım, bu en az 15 kilometre yol demek. Bizim gibi insanlar için zorunluluk bu.”

Dağıtımcıları yağmurda sokağa iten prim sistemi. 60 paketin üzerine çıkınca prim devreye giriyor: “Üstüne bir 60 daha koyarsam bir yevmiye daha almış gibi oluyorum. Böyle çalışmasam yetiremem. Böyle de yetmiyor gerçi.” Yetmediği için PTT'den sonra Maslak'ta servis şoförlüğü yapıyor, dün eve ancak 23.30'da girebildi: “İnsan işi değil ama başka yolu yok. PTT'den aldığım para ancak çocukların okuluna, beslenmesine gidiyor. Kirayı, faturayı kim ödeyecek?”

Uber Eats'te çalışan bir kurye, sabah birkaç paket teslim edip eve dönmüş ama çalışmayı sürdüren arkadaşlarına kızamıyor: “Hepimiz borçla yaşıyoruz. Ben çalışmadım çünkü bir dayanağım var. Dayanağı olmayan adam mecbur çalışacak, hem de bu havada daha çok çalışacak.” Sokakta kurye azalınca kişi başına düşen paket artıyor, sağanak birçok kurye için bir “fırsata” dönüşüyor. Boynuna kadar suya gömülmüş kurye görüntüsü için şunları söylüyor: “O insanı zincirle sürüsen suya sokamazsın. Ama bizi kendilerine köle ettiler, sıcak evimizden kendi ayağımızla çıkıp suyun içine giriyoruz.”

Motokurye yasağı ise sabit ücreti olmayan kurye için gelirsiz gün demek: “Millet ne yiyecek diye düşünmek yasağı koyanların görevi değil mi? Bunu ücretli izne dönüştürmek çok mu zor? Şirket paketini düşünüyor, devlet gelişigüzel yasak koyuyor, kurye ne yapacak? Beni düşünmediğin yasak önlem değil.”

Bakırköy Belediyesi'nin süpürge işçileri yağmurun bıraktıklarını temizlemek için sahaya sürüldü. Daha önce de haberlerimize konu olan soyunma kulübeleri artık kullanılamaz durumda: “Sivil kıyafetlerimizi koyacak yerimiz bile yok. Dün mesai bitiminde üstümü değiştirmeye girdiğimde kıyafetlerimi su içinde buldum. Herkes evine kaçmanın yolunu ararken kenti temizleyen işçilere reva gördükleri soyunma yeri bu mu?” İşçiler insani dinlenme alanı talebini yılın başında, sözleşme sürecinde dile getirmişti: “Kulak arkası ettiler. Şimdi damı akan, çamur içindeki kulübelerde üstümüzü değiştiriyoruz.”

Park bahçeler ve fen işleri müdürlüğündeki işçi sayısı ise eski başkan Kerimoğlu döneminde 95'ken işten çıkarmalar ve emekliliklerle 35'e düşmüş. Bir işçi anlatıyor: “Dün koca Bakırköy'ün felaketini 5 işçi 24 saat çalışarak toparlamaya çalıştı. 20'nin üzerinde ağaç devrilmiş, onlarca evi, dükkânı su basmış. Hepsine yetişmeye çalışıyoruz.”

Okmeydanı Perpa'da özel bir şirkette çalışan bir emekçi, dün 16.00'da izin alıp çıktı. 40 dakika otobüs bekledi, Sünnet Köprüsü'nde trafik kilitlenince yağmurun altında Alibeyköy metrosuna yürüdü: “Yanımızda kadın, erkek, genç, yaşlı vardı. Hasta bir teyzenin koluna girip oraya kadar getirdik.” Metrodan sonra Gazi'nin girişine kadar yine yürüdü, eve 19.50'de varabildi. Evi uzak iş …

author: Majid00
title: روش‌های سازمان‌یابی کمونیستی
content:
This essay is the second part of The Dislocation of Vendémiaire, following Part I, “The Disruptors of the 21st Century and the Ideological Collusion.” While Part I interprets the 2026 France-centered student-led protest wave as a politically dislocated movement—one misread by mainstream discourse as a multi-class coalition when it is in fact an expression of fragmentation within the proletariat—Part II develops the theoretical argument behind that claim. Drawing on Marx’s thesis of society’s polarization into two hostile camps, it distinguishes between “property” and “proletarianization” in the sense of national economics and in the sense of political economy. The essay argues that class should be analyzed through the actual control over the production of labor-power, and that digital capitalism increasingly enables capital to dominate labor-power directly, beyond the mediation of formal ownership of physical means of production. On this basis, it explains why many who appear as middle-class or petty-producer subjects in national-economic terms—scholars, franchise shopkeepers, senior programmers, platform creators—are in political-economic terms being proletarianized, while carrying petty-bourgeois habits of political compromise, individualism, hostility to centralized discipline, and identity- or interest-based linkage. The result is a form of struggle that is radical in appearance but conservative and spontaneous in its core: it completes the first step of linkage through identity and affinity, but fails to return to the common ground of class interests and to connect with the broader industrial working class.

¿QUÉ es el patriotismo? ¿Es el amor por el lugar donde uno nació, el lugar de los recuerdos y las esperanzas de la infancia, de los sueños y las aspiraciones? ¿Es el lugar donde, con ingenuidad infantil, contemplábamos las nubes fugaces y nos preguntábamos por qué nosotros tampoco podíamos correr tan rápido? ¿El lugar donde contábamos los miles de millones de estrellas centelleantes, aterrorizados ante la idea de que cada una de ellas fuera «un ojo» que traspasara lo más profundo de nuestras pequeñas almas? ¿Es el lugar donde escuchábamos el canto de los pájaros y anhelábamos tener alas para volar, como ellos, hacia tierras lejanas? ¿O el lugar donde nos sentábamos a los pies de nuestra madre, embelesados por maravillosos relatos de grandes hazañas y conquistas? En resumen, ¿es el amor por ese lugar, donde cada pulgada representa recuerdos queridos y preciosos de una infancia feliz, alegre y juguetona?

Si eso fuera patriotismo, pocos hombres estadounidenses de hoy en día podrían considerarse patriotas, ya que el lugar de juego se ha convertido en fábrica, molino y mina, mientras que los sonidos ensordecedores de la maquinaria han sustituido a la música de los pájaros. Tampoco podemos ya escuchar las historias de grandes hazañas, pues las que cuentan hoy nuestras madres no son más que historias de dolor, lágrimas y aflicción.

¿Qué es, entonces, el patriotismo? «El patriotismo, señor, es el último recurso de los sinvergüenzas», dijo el Dr. Johnson. León Tolstói, el mayor antipatriota de nuestro tiempo, define el patriotismo como el principio que justifica la formación de asesinos en masa; un oficio que requiere mejor equipamiento para el ejercicio del asesinato que para la fabricación de artículos de primera necesidad como zapatos, ropa y viviendas; un oficio que garantiza mejores beneficios y mayor gloria que el del trabajador medio.

Gustave Hervé [1], otro gran antipatriota, califica acertadamente el patriotismo de superstición —una mucho más perjudicial, brutal e inhumana que la religión—. La superstición de la religión tuvo su origen en la incapacidad del hombre para explicar los fenómenos naturales. Es decir, cuando el hombre primitivo oía un trueno o veía un relámpago, no podía dar una explicación a ninguno de ellos y, por lo tanto, concluía que detrás de ellos debía de haber una fuerza mayor que él mismo. Del mismo modo, veía una fuerza sobrenatural en la lluvia y en los diversos cambios que se producen en la naturaleza. El patriotismo, por el contrario, es una superstición creada artificialmente y mantenida a través de una red de mentiras y falsedades; una superstición que despoja al hombre de su autoestima y dignidad, y aumenta su arrogancia y vanidad.

De hecho, la vanidad, la arrogancia y el egoísmo son los elementos esenciales del patriotismo. Permítanme ilustrarlo. El patriotismo parte de la base de que nuestro planeta está dividido en pequeños rincones, cada uno rodeado por una verja de hierro. Quienes han tenido la suerte de nacer en un rincón concreto se consideran mejores, más nobles, más grandiosos y más inteligentes que los seres vivos que habitan en cualquier otro rincón. Por lo tanto, es deber de todo aquel que vive en ese rincón elegido luchar, matar y morir en el intento de imponer su superioridad sobre todos los demás.
