author: The Canadian Press
title: Feds investing $1 billion for road to Ring of Fire in Ontario: Carney
content:
The federal government will put down

$1 billion

 to help build a controversial road to the Ring of Fire region in northern Ontario, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Wednesday.


The region is said to be rich in nickel, chromite, copper and gold and Carney said its development will secure Canada’s critical mineral supply chain.


“Canada is matching Ontario’s $1-billion investment to build road infrastructure to reach the Ring of Fire,” Carney said as he and Premier Doug Ford announced an $8.7-billion joint plan to help Ontario’s tariff-affected industries, including steel and automotive sectors.


The Ring of Fire sits partially in the James Bay lowlands, part of North America’s largest wetland, and is home to a number of remote, fly-in First Nations. Its mineral development has been a major focus for Ford since he took office in 2018.


Earlier this year, Ford announced construction had begun on two of the roads that will eventually connect the provincial highway system to the mining area some 500 kilometres north of Thunder Bay, Ont.


A map of the Ring of Fire in Ontario.


 


Ford had long called for the federal government to match his government’s $1-billion investment in the road project. Ontario’s previous Liberal government had also asked Ottawa to match that money.


“Last December, I joined the prime minister here in Ottawa to sign an agreement that would eliminate federal duplication for the roads to the Ring of Fire,” Ford said Wednesday.


“Thanks to that agreement, we got shovels in the ground on the roads to the Ring of Fire this summer and are well on our way to unlocking, as the prime minister mentioned, 70,000 jobs and $22 billion in economic activity that will be powered by the Ring of Fire’s critical minerals.”


The province has signed partnerships with three First Nations who want the road, while many others are decidedly against it.


Webequie First Nation and Marten Falls First Nation, both remote fly-in communities, want a road to connect to the provincial highway system as well as the economic opportunities in mining the Ring of Fire. They both say it will lift their communities out of poverty.


Aroland First Nation sits further south and its road will be upgraded to handle greater traffic.


Read More: 


Friends of Attawapiskat River file for judicial review over road to Ring of Fire 


However, many other First Nations in northern Ontario are against the proposed road. They say they haven’t been consulted and the road will change their way of life.


Neskantaga First Nation and Attawapiskat First Nation have built a settlement where the proposed road will cross the Attawapiskat River.


The Canadian Press visited the region last year, including the settlement, where community members plan to block the road whenever construction crews arrive, years from now.


Story by Liam Casey

author: Unknown
title: Ephéméride des luttes : 21 octobre
content:
L'éphéméride des luttes du 21 octobre, comme toutes les autres, sert à se nourrir des luttes passées pour comprendre celles que nous menons au présent et au futur. L'Histoire est une matière qui peut être modelée, alors souvenons-nous de notre histoire, ou de nos histoires.


1894 :

 Révolte des forçats du bagne des Îles du Salut : "

En septembre 1894, au bagne des Îles du Salut, un surveillant tue le forçat anarchiste François Briens. Celui-ci déclare, avant de mourir :"Je meurs pour l'anarchie, les anarchistes me vengeront".


Le 21 octobre 1894, le surveillant est tué à son tour, à coup de poignard, ainsi que trois autres gardiens. La révolte se propage, mais la répression ne tarde pas. Le lendemain, 22 octobre 1894, 11 forçats seront tués dont des anarchistes connus comme Jules Léauthier, Pierre Meyrveis, Benoît Chevenet, Simon (dit Biscuit), réfugié dans un arbre, abattu après avoir crié "Vive l'anarchie". Edouard Marpeaux, sera tué au matin du 23 octobre

".


Repris de l'éphéméride anarchiste.


1902 :

 Aux USA, une grève de mineurs prend fin après cinq mois de mobilisation.


1928 :

 Naissance à Milan de Giuseppe Pinelli, cheminot anarchiste qui sera accusé en décembre 1969 d'avoir posé la bombe de Piazza Fontana, qui avait en réalité été placée par un groupe néofasciste. Pinelli mourra jeté par la fenêtre du commissariat de Milan, le 15 décembre 1969.


1964 :

 A Copenhague, une bombe explose dans l'ambassade espagnole pour lutter contre la dictature franquiste. La FIJL et le groupe anarchiste Primero de Mayo sont derrière tout ça.


1967 :

 A Washington, plus de 100.000 personnes participent à une marche contre la guerre du Vietnam. Celle-ci sera suivie d'une marche sur le Pentagone, où de durs affrontements auront lieu contre la garde nationale.


1970 :

 En Argentine, les FAR (

Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias

) incendient un patrouille de police à l'aide d'un lance-flammes.


1972 :

 - Dans la banlieue de Barcelone, le Mouvement Ibérique de Libération (MIL, entre anarchisme et conseillisme) braque la Caisse d'Epargne de Mataro et repart avec un million de pesetas, qui serviront à alimenter une imprimerie clandestine.


 A Latina, des explosifs sautent sur les marches du Palais de Justice.

 A Roccella Jonica en Calabre, deux répétiteurs téléphoniques sont endommagés par des explosifs.


1976 :

 A Rennes, le Front de Libération de la Bretagne/Armée Révolutionnaire Bretonne (FLB/ARB) fait sauter une bombe au centre des impôts.


1977 :

 - A Paris, plusieurs manifestations de soutien à la Fraction Armée Rouge (RAF) ont lieu suite à la mort

quelques jours plus tôt

 de plusieurs de ses militants en prison. Le soir, des groupes autonomes incendient des bus de tourisme allemands. Enormément d'actions ont eu lieu les jours précédents (

19

 et

20

 octobre).


 A Trento, un concessionnaire Volkswagen est attaqué au cocktail molotov. Dans l'après-midi, un bus de touristes allemands est incendié dans le centre-ville.

 A Vicenza, une bombe fait sauter les locaux du concessionnaire Mercedes, tandis qu'un magasin de Volkswagen est attaqué de 3 molotov.

 A San Sebastian/Donostia, un groupe anarchiste fait sauter deux bombes contre le consulat d'Allemagne de l'Ouest.

 Les NAPAP (Noyaux Armés Pour l'Autonomie Populaire) font sauter un hangar Mercedes dans la nuit.


1979 :

 Dans l'Aude, en Haute-Garonne et dans l'Hérault, trois futurs pylônes de THT sont endommagés par des charges d'explosif (à La Gaudière, Lanta et Saint-Gélydu-Fesc).


1992 :

 A Bangor en Irlande du Nord, l'IRA fait sauter une grosse bombe dans une des rues principales, causant de gros dégâts alentours. La rue avait été évacuée avant explosion.

author: Andrea DiP
title: Que a injustiça não te entristeça, que te radicalize
content:
Cerca de 500 mil pessoas foram às ruas em protestos na França nos últimos dias, em atos que começaram pedindo reformas no sistema educacional e evoluíram para reivindicações sociais mais amplas, que já influenciam outros países da Europa.


Os protestos começaram em setembro, quando estudantes bloquearam o acesso a uma escola na região de Paris para exigir mais recursos para a educação. Rapidamente, alunos de outras escolas aderiram, e as manifestações se espalharam pelo país, reivindicando mais professores, mais recursos e a melhora da estrutura dos prédios.

A demanda escalou, e se transformou na manifestação de uma insatisfação generalizada com o alto custo de vida, a queda na qualidade dos serviços públicos e com o governo.


O governo tem falado em atos de violência, depredação de patrimônio e incêndios. As autoridades francesas detiveram mais de 6,8 mil pessoas – mais de 5 mil menores de idade.


As manifestações inspiraram levantes na Itália, Albânia e Portugal.


Na Grécia, os estudantes reclamam do custo de vida e do aumento de mensalidades e taxas. Na Espanha, professores exigem melhores salários. Na Albânia, estudantes protestam contra as condições nas universidades, os custos do ensino superior e a falta de apoio financeiro. Em Portugal, a demanda é também por custos mais baixos de taxas nas universidades. 


Na Argentina, milhares de estudantes e professores foram às ruas na última quinta-feira, 15 de outubro, em protesto contra o governo de Javier Milei.


Essa onda de protestos também tem sua contrapartida no Brasil. “Estamos na rua contra a extrema direita e, sobretudo, contra o que ela representa de retrocesso no nosso país” me disse em entrevista

no último Pauta Pública

 o vice-presidente da União Nacional dos Estudantes, Gutemberg Rodrigues, sobre os atos e assembleias que têm sido organizados de forma espontânea por todo o país desde o dia 5 de outubro, sobretudo em apoio à reeleição de Lula, e que têm levado milhares de pessoas às ruas.


É sempre muito bonito ver os estudantes ocuparem os espaços públicos, e o Brasil tem momentos históricos importantes nesse sentido – seja na época da ditadura militar, com a Passeata dos Cem Mil em 1968, o movimento pelo Passe Livre em 2013, ou quando os secundaristas ocuparam as escolas de São Paulo em 2015.


Neste momento, em que tanto está em jogo no futuro do país dependendo do resultado das eleições que acontecem em poucos dias, e que ouvimos apenas que a juventude tem se radicalizado à direita, que há uma apatia na GenZ, que o elo de rebeldia com a esquerda se desfez e que não há mais pensamento crítico ou pautas coletivas, esse levante jovem no mundo é um alívio para nossos corações cansados.


Que esse levante dos estudantes, no Brasil e pelo mundo, nos sirva de inspiração  e nos dê energia nestes poucos dias que faltam para o segundo turno, em que nossas cabeças estão cheias, nossos corações estão pesados e parece que a energia vai acabar a qualquer momento. 


Mas que nos inspire também para além destas eleições, porque a luta não acaba com a apuração de votos, seja qual for o resultado.


Tem aquela frase bonita que o artista mexicano Enrique Cedillo criou para o Partido Comunista Mexicano e que eu gosto de lembrar sempre: “Que a injustiça não te entristeça, que te radicalize”.

author: Keelan Jacobs
title: Ottawa’s $800K Indigenous online safety fund is ‘not enough,’ NAFC CEO says
content:
While the federal government’s investment of $800,000 over five years to protect Indigenous youth from online sexual exploitation is only a first step, it falls short of what is needed, according to the head of the National Association of Friendship Centres (NAFC). 


“We see this as the first phase. I definitely don’t think it’s enough for our national network, especially to fund all friendship centre initiatives that are needed in this space,” said CEO Jennifer Rankin. 


She added that “$160,000 roughly a year gives us some initial capacity to start pulling resources together. But, to really get the impact in communities, we need to see something at a larger scale.”


Public Safety Minister Gary Anandasangaree announced the money on Oct.15.

 


Public Safety Minister Gary Anandasangaree. Photo by: APTN


According to the announcement, the money will support the Bringing Empowerment Awareness, Culture and Online Navigation project known as BEACON. 


Through the BEACON project, friendship centres across Canada will “provide culturally relevant online safety education,” said the announcement. The money will help to  “strengthen prevention efforts, support those at risk and help build safer communities.”


The project will also “improve the collection of information on Indigenous youth experiences online, helping to ensure future policies, programs and prevention strategies are informed by and responsive to Indigenous perspectives and experiences.”  


Rankin also stressed the importance of trusted community spaces. 


“We need to make sure that there are safe and secure spaces where people feel comfortable having those conversations about the risks that youth face today in the digital age,” she said. 


She pointed to emerging technological pressures as well. And that the “increase with AI is challenging youth to question things and to not take everything at face value.”


The

NAFC

 is the national body representing friendship centres that serve urban Indigenous people. 


Read More:


NAFC lobbies Ottawa for millions in funding for programs


The announcement does not specify how many centres will deliver BEACON programming or when the first sessions will begin. It states the work will occur through the network and be turned into practical support in communities across the country.


The money flows through the Contribution Program to Combat Serious and Organized Crime. Public Safety Canada describes online child sexual exploitation “as a complex and growing issue that cannot be addressed by any single program or organization.”


The investment sits within Canada’s National Strategy for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation on the Internet, in place since 2004. The government spends more than $27 million a year under that strategy on prevention, awareness, law enforcement, victim protection, research and partnerships.


According to the Canadian Centre for Child Protection’s

 Project Arachnid,

the system has detected and issued more than 50 million notices for the removal of child sexual abuse material worldwide since 2017, reflecting the volume of online content that continues to circulate.


The

RCMP’s Child Exploitation Crime Centre


reports that it processes thousands of reports of online child sexual exploitation each year and works with domestic and international partners to investigate and disrupt offenders.


According to the government, the BEACON money focuses strictly on prevention and education delivered through friendship centres. It does not create new enforcement powers, alter platform rules, or replace existing police or child-protection work under the national strategy.


Separately, the government has tabled a proposed law called the Safe Social Media Act (Bill C-34). According to public safety, it will introduce new safety requirements for social media platforms and AI chatbot services, increase platform accountability and transparency, and set a minimum age of 16 for social media accounts, with possible exemptions for platforms that demonstrate adequate safeguards. Bill C-34 has not become law, and the BEACON investment does not depend on it.

Ottawa’s $800K Indigenous online safety fund is ‘not enough,’ NAFC CEO says

APTN News

title: Lies the Fur Industry Tells!
content:
Mink and fox killers and their apologists often say the most ridiculous things to try and mitigate their losses after raids like the two we have seen in the last couple of months, in which 3000 or more captive mink were liberated from horrific captivity. Sample absurdities spouted as fact include:

Lie #1: Many or most of the escaped animals were run over and killed by cars.

– The absurdity of this statement is that before liberation, death was 100% certain. Every animal on the farm was bred to die by the end of November. While it is true a small number may be hit by cars after being released, most will not, and if nothing else they have been given a chance at freedom. In reality, fox and mink farms are located in rural areas with little traffic, the animals are quick and solitary animals, and it beggars belief to imagine them aggregating in the road waiting to be run over by the rare passing vehicle.

– Mink are in fact only a few generations removed from their wild cousins and have not yet had their wild instincts bred out. The “Mink Rehabilitation Project” led by convicted ALF liberator Rod Coronado proved this decades ago. Mink legally purchased from a fur farm were released into the wild and shown through observation to retain natural survival instincts and thrive in the wild after a lifetime in a cage. Studies with radio-collared mink demonstrate clearly the animals are capable of surviving in the wild. No, they won’t starve or freeze to death or die from dehydration. Most areas where mink are imprisoned are actually native habitat for American mink.

Lie #3: Most of the mink are recaptured

Its absurd to imagine hundreds of wild animals being recaptured by lunkhead farmers running around looking for them. Our hearts go out to those few recaptured who were given a shot at life and now have only suffering ahead.

There may be some minimal impact on the local ecosystems temporarily while the animals disperse and learn their way around, but no habitats are decimated or overrun or rendered free of other small animals. And no, the animals do not kill wantonly and more than they need to survive, and they certainly don’t attack human bystanders, as some apologists have had the audacity to suggest.

Liberationists break the law in adherence to a higher law – one which states animals are not commodities, not objects, but sentient creatures with a right to live. They will fight for the lives of these animals “as if they were our own.”

The Animal Liberation Front and other anonymous activists utilize economic sabotage in addition to the direct liberation of animals from conditions of abuse and imprisonment to halt needless animal suffering. By making it more expensive to trade in the lives of innocent, sentient beings, they maintain the atrocities against our brothers and sisters are likely to occur in smaller numbers; their goal is to abolish the exploitation, imprisonment, torture and killing of all innocent, non-human animals.

Join the ALF – Historically, those wishing to participate in direct action have either acted alone or gotten together with others they could trust of like mind and just started doing actions. author: Daron Letts
title: City closer to approving $216M budget for infrastructure in 2027
content:
Water infrastructure and related upgrades make up more than half of the City of Iqaluit’s proposed $216-million capital budget for 2027.


Wastewater system upgrades soak up more than $80 million of the budget. Water infrastructure accounts for another $75 million, which includes $38 million for raw water intake, supply and storage.


Peter Tumilty, the city’s chief financial officer, introduced the proposed budget to councillors during Tuesday’s governance and priorities committee meeting. He began his presentation with an explanation as to why this year’s proposed budget is

more than double

 last year’s $90-million capital plan.


“We have elected this year to show the entire cost of the project in the current year rather than spreading it out over the life of the project based on expected annual spending,” Tumilty said.


In the past, the city has spread project costs over multiple years to minimize the impact on the city’s finances, he said. This year, projects that are fully or substantially funded by third parties, such as the federal government, are fully costed into the budget.


For example, the city is planning to spend $60 million on wastewater system

upgrades

 next year with money from the federal Building Canada Strong Fund.


This improves the city’s ability to plan multi-year projects and to optimize sealift scheduling, Tumilty said.


Other projects include $16 million toward drainage and roadway improvements and $12 million for city facility improvements, including the fire hall, shooting range relocation, and increasing equipment garage storage capacity.


The budget proposes $4.5 million for vehicle and equipment purchases, with a $750,000 grader being among the most costly.


Three playground replacements and outfield turf for the city’s softball diamond will share $750,000 in funding. Absent are arena upgrades and a long sought after community hall.


“It’s very much a practical budget, fixing the foundations and the infrastructure deficit that we have,” said deputy Mayor Kim Smith in a phone interview on Wednesday.


Councillors have not forsaken new recreational infrastructure and upgrades, she added.


“Once we get our feet back under us as far as critical infrastructure goes, we’ll be able to offer our residents a bit more of a fun budget where we can focus a bit more on recreation,” she said.


The improvements to water and wastewater systems will open up opportunities for much-needed housing in the community, she added.


Following Tumilty’s presentation, committee members unanimously moved to present the plan to city council.

author: Unknown
title: PJAK calls on Iran to disclose Xalid Berzincî’s whereabouts
content:
The Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) issued a written statement after losing contact with its member Xalid Berzincî following his detention by the Iranian regime. PJAK held the Iranian regime directly responsible for Berzincî’s fate, calling for an end to the policy of enforced disappearances and demanding clarification of his situation.


According to the statement, Berzincî was detained by regime forces on July 9, 2026, in the village of Ûçtepe, near Bokan. PJAK emphasized that no clear or reliable information has been provided about his whereabouts or legal status since his detention.


PJAK stated that the Iranian regime’s refusal to disclose Berzincî’s fate has raised serious concerns about his health and the conditions of his detention.


“The Iranian regime is directly responsible for the fate of Xalid Berzincî. The regime must put an end to its policy of enforced disappearances,” the statement said.


Emphasizing that the Iranian regime is responsible for protecting Berzincî’s life, physical health, and safety, PJAK stated that the authorities must immediately disclose information about his place of detention, health condition, and legal status.


The statement stressed that leaving questions about Berzincî’s situation unanswered and withholding information is unacceptable, issuing the following call:


“Any failure to provide clear answers regarding our comrade’s situation, or any concealment of information, is unacceptable. The Iranian regime bears direct responsibility for the consequences of any negligence or practices that violate fundamental standards of humanity. The concealment of our comrade’s fate must end, and his situation must be clarified as soon as possible.”

author: Unknown
title: Two women killed in Sulaymaniyah and Mardin
content:
Two women have died in Sulaymaniyah in South Kurdistan and in Mardin in North Kurdistan. Kîjan Bûrhan was shot by her father and succumbed to her severe injuries, while Remziye Damar was found dead in her home under unexplained circumstances.


Kîjan Bûrhan was shot by her father in Sulaymaniyah on Monday evening. The 30-year-old woman was struck by three bullets. She was taken for medical treatment in critical condition but died from her injuries on Tuesday afternoon.


Meanwhile, Remziye Damar was found lifeless in her home in the village of Boxazîyê in Kızıltepe district. Emergency services arrived following a call for assistance and confirmed her death. Her body was taken to the forensic medicine department of Kızıltepe State Hospital for an autopsy. Following the completion of the examinations, Damar was laid to rest in her home village of Boxazîyê.

author: Brad Reed
title: FCC Chair Brendan Carr Threatens Broadcasters Over Poll Coverage
content:
A Democratic strategist points out that “it’s not illegal to tell the American people that Trump is a failed president.”

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr on Wednesday threatened broadcasters that cover what he described as “fake polls,” which he said hurt “voter turnout and enthusiasm.”

In a social media post, Carr attacked news outlets for “amplifying or airing these polls without regard to basic journalistic ethics and without informing the public that those polls lack a scientific, accurate, or even real basis.”

Carr did not provide a single specific example of a “fake” opinion poll, nor did he name a broadcaster who has promoted one. President Donald Trump, who nominated Carr to head the FCC, has repeatedly decried polls as “fake” as they’ve shown his approval ratings at record lows.

Later in the post, Carr hinted that the FCC would take direct action against broadcasters for informing their viewers about opinion polls.

“The FCC takes these issues seriously,” said Carr. “Broadcasters are prohibited by the terms of their federal licenses from engaging in news distortion or promoting broadcast hoaxes. It is important that broadcasters comply with their public interest obligations.”

Carr’s post drew a swift rebuke from Democratic FCC commissioner Anna Gomez.

“Pollsters who intentionally mislead the public should answer for it,” wrote Gomez, “but broadcasters who report publicly available polling data should never be punished when a poll is wrong. FCC rules on news distortion or hoaxes do not apply to a station that reports this data in good faith.”

Steve Herman, former White House bureau chief at Voice of America, wrote in a social media post that Carr’s assertions about “news distortion” are “stretching specific regulations far beyond their legal definitions,” as “the FCC can’t mandate how a broadcaster contextualizes a poll.”

“The FCC threatening broadcasters for airing specific political data is a chilling content-based restriction on speech,” Herman added, “which federal courts subject to extreme judicial review and the commission would almost certainly lose such cases, according to First Amendment scholars.”

Former TV meteorologist Chris Gloninger predicted that Carr’s post would have a chilling effect on local news stations.

“Holy shit, this is dangerous,” Gloninger wrote. “Two weeks before an election, the FCC chair is threatening broadcaster licenses over polls he calls ‘fake.’ No GM will risk that, so polls vanish.”

Mark Jacob, former metro editor at the Chicago Tribune, called Carr “anti-free-speech” for “threatening to punish news outlets that publish polls showing Trump’s deep unpopularity.”

“We are sliding into a dictatorship,” Jacob said, “and it would be helpful if major media would do their duty and warn the public.”

Adam Klasfeld, editor-in-chief at All Rise News, described Carr as the president’s “censorship czar” who is warning news outlets against “the dissemination of data disfavored by the state.”

Princeton historian Kevin Kruse argued Carr’s threats warranted his impeachment and removal from office.

“The president shouting ‘fake news’ is bad enough,” wrote Kruse, “but the FCC commissioner threatening to punish broadcasters for promoting ‘fake news’ like ‘the president is historically unpopular’ is so much worse.”

Carr’s post drew ridicule from Democratic strategist Adam Parkhomenko, who informed the FCC chair that “it’s not illegal to tell the American people that Trump is a failed president.”

Max Steele, senior director of communications at gun safety advocacy organization Everytown, similarly ridiculed Carr.

“It is ILLEGAL to say the brave and smart President Trump is at historic polling lows!!!” he wrote sarcastically.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant …

author: Simon Feisthauer Fournet
title: Dispatch From Paris: Student-Led Protests Spread, Despite Brutal Policing
content:
Weeks of student-led demonstrations have spread nationwide, with arrests, reports of police brutality, and restrictions.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Paris, France — The march on the iconic Place de la République in the French capital had barely begun when riot police — known as the Compagnies républicaines de sécurité, or CRS — fired tear gas in the square. The demonstration on October 17, 2026, had been officially declared to the Paris prefecture, which banned the longer route organizers planned through the center of the city but allowed a march departing from the square. Even so, police launched tear gas that incapacitated the 400 musicians of the Orchestre du Nouveau Monde, an activist classical ensemble that had played at earlier high school protests and came to perform again.

The heavy police presence did not deter protesters who dressed the statue of Marianne, a figure personifying the French Republic, at the center of the square in a giant yellow vest — a reference to the “yellow vest” protest movement that began in 2018 over rising fuel prices and cost of living and has recently joined forces with the French high schoolers’ protests. An inscription on the statue read: “2026, the police mutilate high schoolers.”

Similar crowds filled cities and towns across France. Organizers counted about 800,000 people among the protesters while authorities reported 550,000. Officials had expected far fewer, about 200,000, and Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez later conceded the state had been caught off guard.

The movement began in early September with blockades at high schools in France’s overseas territories — where students denounced decaying buildings, unfilled teaching posts and shrinking budgets — and then spread to underserved Paris suburbs and the rest of the country, in part through social media.

The police sometimes used force to contain and arrest students who were protesting and blocking off their schools. By October 1, the Collectif d’action judiciaire, a group of lawyers defending arrested students, said police in the Parisian suburb of Saint-Denis had pressured, blackmailed, and even beaten detained high schoolers. Several cases of police wounding students have been reported.

Unions, student organizations, and activist groups joined the movement, tying the school-related grievances to frustrations with the cost of living and anger at the government in a general convergence of struggles.

Daniel, 29, said French mainstream media tended to ignore the students’ demands, which is why the movement started on social media. “It breaks the dialogue, so it has to go through social media, where a freer thought for young people in general can emerge,” he said.

He argued that the French government in recent years has ignored every democratic channel, from the left’s win in the 2024 legislative elections after the National Assembly was dissolved by President Emmanuel Macron to citizen petitions against laws passed without debate.

“All of that creates a break between two parts of society, the elites in power and the rest of society, with those elites telling us, essentially, ‘you lot don’t understand anything, you’re idealists,’” he said.

Videos of police brutality shared on social media brought Éric, 32, into the streets on October 17, he said, adding that he was impressed by the scale of the Gen Z mobilization: “It took very little time to mobilize this many young people, and that’s impressive.”

With at least 1,400 arrests, 3,000 businesses robbed, and several public buildings set ablaze that day, media coverage in France and abroad has generally focused on looting and arson on the margins on the protests, which some organizers and independent media have denounced, pointing to escalation from the police and anger built up over weeks of heavy-handed repression against students.

For Éric, the anger has been building for years. “Everything that has been done since the Macron era, such as the abolition of the TV license fee [a tax that funded public broadcasting] that brought the public service to its knees, with the rest of the media largely owned by far right billionaires — we’ve reached a critical point in the history of France and of Macron’s two terms, and it’s catastrophic,” he said.

author: Aldrey Olegario
title: Políticos têm rede ‘paralela’ na Meta sem declarar ao TSE
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


Candidatos nas eleições deste ano estão usando uma estratégia em comum:

além das contas oficiais nas redes sociais com milhões de seguidores que foram declaradas ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), muitos têm uma rede paralela de perfis de apoio que copiam parte do conteúdo das páginas dos políticos.

 Esse “exército alternativo” turbina o alcance, com menções cruzadas e postagens iguais feitas quase ao mesmo tempo.


Segundo a

Agência Pública

 apurou,

Flávio Bolsonaro, que disputa a presidência, tem ao menos sete perfis de apoio não declarados ao TSE com mais de 100 mil seguidores cada. Juntos eles reúnem mais de 2,5 milhões de seguidores.

 Para se ter uma comparação, o principal perfil oficial de Flávio declarado ao TSE tem 14,8 milhões.


Além de fazerem propaganda com o número de urna do candidato, essa rede de perfis de apoio divulga links para grupos oficiais de Bolsonaro e o @ oficial de Flávio.


Algumas delas postam o mesmo conteúdo com minutos de diferença. Isso aconteceu no último final de semana, quando uma conta de apoio com mais de 770 mil seguidores publicou o mesmo corte da entrevista de Flávio para a Rede Globo com minutos de diferença, indicando o perfil oficial.


O mesmo corte da entrevista à Globo foi divulgado pelo perfil oficial de Flávio e uma das páginas de apoio com minutos de diferença. A única diferença foi a inclusão de letterings


Os perfis de Flávio não são recentes. A maioria deles foi criada em 2022 ou fim de 2023, quando Lula tomou posse. Do outro lado da disputa, André Janones, deputado federal (Rede-MG) e a principal cabeça por trás da estratégia digital de Lula (PT) no segundo turno, também tem uma página de apoio no Instagram que não foi declarada ao TSE nem por Lula, nem pelo deputado. Nesse caso, o perfil de Janones foi criado em 6 de outubro deste ano, quando o político afirmou que a sua conta oficial estava sendo alvo de perseguição por grupos bolsonaristas e corria risco de ser derrubada. No vídeo, ele assume a criação da página.


O perfil de apoio de Janones traz um link tanto para o @ oficial do político, quanto para o de Lula. Com 1,6 milhão de seguidores, a página também divulga o canal de WhatsApp do “Exército de Lula”, onde são compartilhadas as diretrizes para engajar a favor do candidato.


A

Pública

 apurou com especialistas em direito eleitoral que explicam que

ter uma conta de apoio não configura um crime, porém, há limites para o que essas contas podem fazer – e que ficam mais difíceis de serem fiscalizados pela falta de transparência das plataformas.


Como a

Pública

 já

mostrou

, a Meta deixou anúncios pagos com dinheiro estrangeiro circularem sem rótulo de conteúdo político nestas eleições, o que impede saber quem pagou pelos anúncios e quais postagens foram impulsionadas. A

Pública

 também

revelou

 que a plataforma não tem sido transparente nos critérios que usa para ampliar ou derrubar o alcance de contas.


A advogada Caroline Lacerda, doutora em Direito Eleitoral pela Universidade de Brasília, explica que as campanhas exploram essas contas paralelas de forma estratégica. Um dos motivos é contornar a regra do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral que impede as plataformas de recomendarem os perfis oficiais dos candidatos políticos para os usuários. As páginas de apoio não estão sujeitas a essa limitação.


“A regra de não recomendação cria um incentivo evidente para que as campanhas terceirizem o alcance em perfis paralelos”, explica ela. “As páginas de apoio funcionam, na prática, como caminho alternativo para furar o bloqueio de recomendação dos perfis oficiais. Isso é lícito quando a página é espontânea e sem dinheiro por trás.”


O advogado Fernando Neisser reforça que as publicações em contas de apoio não podem ser impulsionadas através de pagamento.

“Por não serem contas oficiais da campanha, elas não precisam ser informadas ao TSE. Por outro lado, essas contas não podem fazer impulsionamento pago de absolutamente nenhum conteúdo eleitoral”,

 diz.


É aí que a falta de transparência da Meta dificulta a fiscalização. Só é possível saber se houve algum pagamento não declarado através de uma investigação – como o

procedimento

 aberto a pedido da Procuradoria Federal dos Direitos do Cidadão (PFDC) contra a empresa – ou se a própria Meta identificar alguma irregularidade, e decidir combatê-la.


Com base …

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Video game helps Inuit youth learn mental wellness strategies
content:
When Letia Kalluk wrote her song

Maana

 for a contest in the Northwest Territories, she did not know it would eventually be featured in a game that aims to improve the mental wellness of Inuit youth.


In

Virtual Qaggiq

, billed as the first Inuit-designed video game for mobile devices, the Inuktitut song plays alongside videos of elders.


“The lyrics go something like, ‘A wise man told me that you’re still young. You have a lot to live for. You haven’t seen the whole world yet,’” said Kalluk, who is from Arctic Bay, in an interview.


“It’s really good for [youth] to hear music in their own language. It’s been very fulfilling for me as an artist to contribute to that.”


York University researchers, Inuit youth and cultural advisers started developing the game in 2022.


It follows Alaasua, the main character, through seven quests that pair Inuit cultural activities with mental wellness strategies, said project co-ordinator Yogita Singh.


In one quest, mythical creatures tempt Alaasua to drink spoiled water while she gathers fresh water and ice. Players learn to resist the temptation and manage stress without turning to substance use, Singh said.


The soundtrack includes a rap track by Kinngait artist Iola Oshoweetok, a drumming instrumental by Kimmirut artist Leo Temela, and throat-singing tracks by Yellowknife duo Tiffany Kuliktana Ayalik and Kayley Inuksuk Mackay, also known as Piqsiq.


The game’s testing phase took place from October 2025 to July, with 276 Inuit youth from 21 communities in Nunavut and 16 other communities across Canada taking part, Singh said.


Participants completed a 39-question wellness questionnaire before and after playing, with in-person workshops held in Arctic Bay, Kinngait, Pangnirtung, Iqaluit, Baker Lake and Ottawa.


Others tested the game from home, Singh said.


“Youth felt they had learned strategies to help themselves cope better with negative thoughts, make themselves feel better and feel more comfortable asking for help, for example, when they feel a bad mood coming on,” said Yvonne Bohr, the project’s principal investigator at York University.


“Usually, it takes a while for lessons to sink in, but the fact that there were changes even right afterward is very encouraging,” she added. 


Researchers also found no negative changes in participants’ wellness after playing the game.


Kalluk said she helped translate 12 interviews with elders from Arctic Bay, Kinngait, Baker Lake and Pangnirtung, which can be accessed by players in the digital qaggiq, or traditional meeting space within the game.


“There are a few videos that talk about fishing, going out hunting, as well as mental health aspects. An elder’s point of view is very important, and it’s important to have these kinds of resources readily available for youth,” said Kalluk. 


The team is working to make the game available on iPads and is in discussion with the territorial Education Department about using it in schools.


Singh said the hope is to make

Virtual Qaggiq

 available in early 2027 on iPhone and Android devices.


“It makes me feel very proud as an Inuk to be part of something like this, something so groundbreaking for our youth in Nunavut,” Kalluq said.

author: Ed Wanderley
title: Bolsonarista, Gusttavo Lima pressionou Vorcaro por acordo para movimentar R$ 23 bilhões
content:
De óculos e chapéu de couro marrons, camisa e calça pretas e cordão de ouro no pescoço, o cantor sertanejo Gusttavo Lima recebeu em sua residência o candidato à presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a quem declarou apoio ao lado de duas dúvidas de estrelas do gênero, todos homens, nesta terça-feira (20). Em vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, o Embaixador, como é conhecido, falou sobre o momento difícil para o povo brasileiro que não teria poder de compra e reclamou como hoje “com R$ 100, você não faz nem um churrasco”, “porque está tudo tão desonesto, uma taxa de juros desonesta”, sintetizou, gravando ao lado do seu candidato, no andar de cima da residência em frente a uma janela de vidro que revelava, de fundo, um jatinho executivo à disposição da dupla.


Gusttavo Lima e Flávio Bolsonaro posam para foto com jatinho ao fundo


“Quando eu era criança, eu só tive oportunidade de estudar porque eu tive Bolsa-escola, Bolsa Família…”, afirma o Embaixador sertanejo, ao que o filho 01 de Jair Bolsonaro responde “vai ser tudo mantido, tá garantido”, atribuindo o discurso de risco de corte de investimento em educação ou programas sociais, como houve no governo de seu pai, a “fake news”. 


Além de Lima, estiveram na fazenda do senador Wilder Morais (PL) para a reunião em apoio ao presidenciável nomes como Amado Batista, Murilo Huff, Zezé Di Camargo, Rodolffo, da dupla com Israel, Marrone, da dupla com Bruno, Jorge, da dupla com Mateus, e Hugo, da dupla com Guilherme.


Mensagens interceptadas pela Polícia Federal (PF), obtidas pela

Agência Pública

, revelam que o hoje Embaixador e defensor da economia brasileira quase foi Gusttavo Lima, da dupla com Vorcaro, protagonista em um dos maiores escândalos de corrupção e fraudes financeiras da história recente do Brasil.


Flávio Bolsonaro durante encontro com cantores sertanejos


O diálogo do dia 6 de novembro de 2024 inclui uma proposta de movimentação de R$ 23 bilhões em um ano por parte do “Embaixador” para o empresário, preso por suspeita de fraude financeira desde março na Operação Compliance Zero.

 As mensagens compreendem o período de julho de 2024 a novembro de 2025.


A “oportunidade” se referia ao fornecimento de maquininhas de cartão de crédito. Vorcaro não tinha sociedade pública ou formal com empresas do setor; porém, investigações da Polícia Federal (PF) e do Banco Central (BC) apontam para a suspeita de que ele usaria marcas de fintech, pertencentes ao Grupo Entre, para movimentar recursos e lavar dinheiro.


Às 9h49 da manhã, Gusttavo Lima envia a Daniel Vorcaro: “vamos falar sobre o meio de pagamento? Operação Super BH”. O Super BH em questão é uma rede de mais de 300 supermercados em 90 municípios de Minas Gerais e Espírito Santo que pertence ao bilionário Pedro Lourenço, amigo pessoal e padrinho de casamento do cantor. A rede Super BH não retornou aos pedidos de comentários por parte da reportagem.


Os amigos Lourenço e Lima já fizeram outros acordos financeiros no passado. Em 2016, o dono da rede de supermercados chegou a emprestar R$ 6 milhões ao cantor para financiar a gravação de um DVD

, conforme relato do próprio artista em entrevista ao podcast André Piunti, em outubro de 2025. 


A fortuna de Lourenço é diversificada em vários empreendimentos. Em abril de 2025, ele se tornou sócio majoritário do clube de futebol Cruzeiro, adquirido por ele por cerca de R$ 600 milhões. O antigo dono era o ex-jogador Ronaldo “Fenômeno”, que também tinha ligações com Vorcaro e, em 2024, captou R$ 25 milhões em capital de giro por meio do Fundo Victória, que pertencia ao Banco Master, como revelou a

Veja

. A

Pública

 procurou Lourenço para comentar sobre o negócio, mas, até o momento, não obteve resposta. Em caso de manifestação, este espaço será atualizado.


O Embaixador dá continuidade ao diálogo e adverte: “temos que andar rápido ou perdemos”. Vorcaro responde “vamos”. Posteriormente, os dois entram em uma chamada de voz durante 2 minutos e 28 segundos e o cantor envia dois arquivos nomeados como “Pedro – taxas atualizadas” e complementa: “Vamos distribuir as maquininhas em cada loja física. 23 bi ano que vem é o movimento”. 


A projeção é bem dimensionada. Naquele ano, o faturamento, segundo dados publicados pela própria rede, foi de R$ 21 bilhões. No ano seguinte, R$ 25,72 bilhões. Vorcaro, no entanto, passa 12 dias em silêncio. Àquela altura, o Master já havia adquirido o Will Bank e estava a quatro meses de ser comprado pelo Banco de Brasília (BRB), mas, nos …

author: Rindala Alajaji
title: EFF’s State Legislative Agenda to End ALPR Mass Surveillance
content:
Police agencies across the U.S. have deployed Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) to capture images of passing vehicles along with time, date, and GPS coordinates. While the technology itself isn’t new (ALPRs have existed in various forms for more than 50 years, and in the U.S. since 1998), the surveillance landscape has shifted dramatically. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence and national data sharing have transformed police ALPRs into an interconnected, nationwide tracking network. It is pitched to city councils by law enforcement and private vendors like Flock Safety, Motorola Solutions (Vigilant), and Axon as an essential tool for solving violent crime.

In reality, it is an inherently dangerous infrastructure of mass surveillance.

Since 2012, EFF has worked with others to expose the severe digital rights harms of ALPR systems. For example, we’ve recently documented how these camera networks allow law enforcement to search for immigrants, track peaceful protesters, target Romani communities, and track women seeking reproductive healthcare. Police also routinely use ALPRs for low-level matters like enforcing school residency requirements or investigating noise complaints. Many officers also use ALPR databases to stalk past romantic partners. Recent EFF analysis revealed officers using the system without legitimate justification—logging search reasons like "LOL" and "LMAO."

Understandably, the public backlash to police ALPR technology is accelerating, and state lawmakers across the country are taking action.

New Hampshire enacted the nation’s first state law on ALPR use in 2007, but technological advances and misconduct have driven even more recent legislative action. In 2026 alone, six states enacted laws that limit police use of ALPRs: Connecticut, Kentucky, New Jersey, New Mexico, Oregon and Washington.

This is a good start, but far more is needed. This blog presents a framework for state legislators who want to stop ALPR mass police surveillance:

Just ban it. It is incompatible with a free society and cannot be fixed.

In the absence of a flat ban, reduce its harms. Most importantly: limit police use of ALPRs to real-time comparison of passing plates to hotlists; require a warrant to place a plate on a hotlist; impose strict limits on the creation and use of those hotlists; and prohibit the storage of ALPR data (and thus prevent the subsequent search and disclosure of that data).

In the absence of a prohibition on storing ALPR data, reduce its harms. Most importantly, place strict limits on police storage, search, and disclosure of ALPR data.

Ban three especially dangerous police practices: placement of ALPRs near sensitive locations like hospitals; purchase of ALPR data; and use of ALPR data to try to predict crime.

Require transparency about ALPR mass surveillance, including: a 30-day public notice before a city procures police ALPRs; a statewide registry of all police ALPRs; and regular, public audits and statistical reports about police usage.

Ensure effective enforcement of all new ALPR restraints, including by means of a private right of action and the exclusionary rule.

These policy battles often unfold locally, so state legislators must ensure that state law is a regulatory floor, never a ceiling. State preemption should never force unwanted camera networks onto communities that have chosen to reject them. Local government must retain authority to enact full bans, deny funding, reject contracts, and decommission existing camera networks.

The Gold Standard: Statewide Bans on ALPR Mass Surveillance

Strict Limits on Real-time Use of ALPRs Limits on creating hotlistsLimits on using hotlists

Strict Limits on Storage, Search, and Disclosure of ALPR DataStorage limits Search limits Disclosure limits

As in our previous post on ALPR policy, our focus here is ALPR mass surveillance: the continuous dragnet collection and retention of location data on innocent drivers. Different issues are raised by automated traffic enforcement (ATE) systems, such as standalone red-light or speed cameras that solely photograph and ticket specific traffic violations, without building a searchable network about uninvolved drivers. As such, state laws against ALPR mass surveillance should not cover ATE. This is the approach in at least six states: Connecticut, Minnesota, North Carolina, Oregon, Virginia, and Washington. The most common approach is to exclude ATE from the law’s definition of “ALPR.”

author: Rubén Morvolution
title: La huelga como medio, la clase como sujeto: una respuesta al debate sobre el movimiento de vivienda
content:
La huelga como medio, la clase como sujeto: una respuesta al debate sobre el movimiento de vivienda

Sobre la centralidad histórica de la huelga y las posibilidades de articulación entre las luchas laborales y por la vivienda.

El artículo El movimiento de vivienda ante su Rubicón, de Alfredo Apilánez, plantea un debate que considero necesario. La crisis de acceso a la vivienda, las limitaciones de las organizaciones sindicales y la relación entre las reivindicaciones inmediatas y la transformación social son cuestiones que no podemos eludir.

Comparto la preocupación por el riesgo de que los movimientos sociales terminen subordinados a las instituciones, atrapados en calendarios electorales o limitados a reclamar reformas que no alteren las relaciones de poder existentes. Sin embargo, discrepo de la orientación estratégica que se desprende del artículo, especialmente cuando contrapone las posibilidades de la huelga general a la construcción de espacios autogestionados y experiencias de okupación.

La cuestión fundamental, a mi entender, no consiste en determinar qué práctica expresa una mayor radicalidad, sino qué instrumentos permiten a la clase trabajadora desarrollar una capacidad colectiva de intervención y transformación social. Desde esa perspectiva, considero necesario reivindicar la centralidad histórica de la huelga, sin convertirla en un fin en sí mismo.

Una huelga no constituye por sí sola una revolución, ni garantiza una victoria o una mayor conciencia de clase. Puede limitarse a una reivindicación salarial, quedar reducida a una convocatoria testimonial o agotarse sin producir cambios organizativos duraderos. Pero reducir su significado a los resultados inmediatos o a las concesiones que pueda arrancar al Estado supone dejar fuera una dimensión fundamental de la historia del movimiento obrero.

La huelga ha sido uno de los instrumentos mediante los cuales la clase trabajadora ha aprendido a reconocerse como fuerza colectiva. Su importancia no reside únicamente en detener temporalmente la producción, sino en la posibilidad de que quienes sostienen la actividad económica descubran, mediante su propia experiencia, la capacidad que poseen cuando actúan conjuntamente.

La preparación de una huelga exige relaciones, organización, discusión de objetivos, construcción de solidaridades y toma de decisiones. Durante el conflicto pueden aparecer nuevas formas de cooperación que, posteriormente, se mantengan, amplíen o desaparezcan. Nada de ello está garantizado, pero precisamente por eso la huelga debe entenderse como un medio dentro de un proceso de organización y lucha, no como un acontecimiento que contenga por sí mismo la transformación social.

Confundir el instrumento con su finalidad sería tan equivocado como descartarlo porque una convocatoria concreta no reúna las condiciones necesarias para alcanzar todos sus objetivos.

La centralidad del trabajo no ha desaparecido

Para comprender la importancia de la huelga en la actualidad, debemos abandonar la idea de que la clase trabajadora se limita al proletariado industrial tradicional. El mundo del trabajo ha cambiado profundamente y, con él, la composición de la propia clase trabajadora.

Hoy, la actividad económica depende tanto de la industria como del transporte, la logística, los servicios y los cuidados, entre otros sectores. Aunque las condiciones laborales y las posibilidades de organizarse son muy diferentes, todos ellos forman parte de una sociedad que continúa dependiendo del trabajo humano para funcionar. Por eso, la diversidad de la clase trabajadora no elimina su importancia ni la capacidad de la huelga para convertirse en un instrumento de lucha colectiva.

En un artículo anterior, reflexionaba sobre la recomposición de clase y la crisis de la sociedad de propietarios, planteaba que la pérdida de determinadas seguridades patrimoniales puede modificar las identidades sociales de sectores asalariados que tradicionalmente se reconocían como clases medias.

Muchos de esos sectores ya dependían de vender su fuerza de trabajo. Lo que cambia no es necesariamente su posición objetiva, sino sus expectativas de estabilidad y la forma en que comprenden su relación con el conjunto de la sociedad. Que una parte de la clase trabajadora posea una vivienda no elimina automáticamente su dependencia salarial, del mismo modo que las diferencias patrimoniales, las contradicciones internas o las orientaciones políticas reaccionarias no permiten concluir que la …

author: Unknown
title: Dersim Belediyesi işçilerinden açıklama: İşe iade kararı uygulansın, kayyım düzenine son verilsin
content:
Dersim - Dersim Belediyesi’nde kayyım yönetimi tarafından işten atılan işçiler, Seyit Rıza Meydanı’nda yaptıkları basın açıklamasında işe iade kararlarının uygulanmasını istedi. İşçiler, işten çıkarılmalarının üzerinden 650 gün geçtiğini belirterek fiili ve hukuki mücadelelerini sürdürdüklerini ifade etti. Açıklamaya Emek Partisi (EMEP) Genel Başkanı Seyit Aslan da katıldı.

Basın açıklamasını işten atılan işçilerden Ali Mükan okudu. Mahkemenin işe iade kararı verdiğini belirten Mükan, buna rağmen kayyım yönetiminin mahkeme kararını uygulamadığına dikkat çekerek kararın bir an önce uygulanmasını istediklerini söyledi.

Dersim’de işsizliğin yüksek olduğuna ve gençlerin iş bulamadıkları için kentten ayrılmak zorunda kaldığına dikkat çeken Mükan, 13 kişinin işten çıkarılmasının yalnızca işçileri değil, ailelerinin geçim koşullarını ve geleceğini de etkilediğini belirtti.

İşe iade kararının uygulanmamasına bütçenin gerekçe gösterilmesine tepki gösteren Mükan, “Belediyenin bütçesi işçi kıyımı yapılarak düzeltilmez. Bütçe açığının sorumlusu da biz değiliz” dedi. Dersim halkının iradesinin yok sayılmasına karşı çıktıklarını belirten Mükan, kayyım uygulamalarına son verilmesini ve kayyımların derhal geri çekilmesini talep etti.

Basın açıklamasında söz alan EMEP Genel Başkanı Aslan ise Saray rejiminin kayyım politikalarına tepki göstererek “Dersim halkının iradesini çalan anlayışla, Gülistan Doku’yu katleden anlayışla, işçi arkadaşlarımızın işe geri dönmesine engel olan anlayış aynı. Esenyurt'ta halk iradesi çalındı. Milyonlarca doların nasıl ortaya çıktığına hep tanık olduk. Bölgeye atanan kayyumların yolsuzluklarına tanık olduk. Çünkü Saray oligarşisi tarafından atanan kayyumlar kendilerini güvencede görüyor. İşe iade davasını kazanan işçilerin kayyım tarafından işe alınmaması Saray oligarşisinin soruna nasıl yaklaştığının göstergesidir. Tek bir işçi dahi işten atılmış olsa bu adaletsizliğin karşısında durmaya devam edeceğiz. İşçi arkadaşlarımızın işe alınması için mücadelemizi sürdürmeye devam edeceğiz. Belediyenin koltuğunda oturan kayyum bugün kendisini güvencede görüyor olabilir. Ama yarın işçiler, emekçiler bunun hesabını sorar. Yarın iktidarı kaybettiklerinde ne yapacaklarını şimdiden hesap etsinler” ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Genel-İş 11 No'lu Şube'de delege seçimleri tamamlandı: Sandıktan kırmızı liste çıktı
content:
İzmir – DİSK Genel-İş İzmir 11 No’lu Şubede iki gün süren delege seçimleri sona erdi. Sosyal Projeler, Çevre Koruma, Kent Temizlik, İdari İşler, Mezarlık, Haller, Doğal Yaşam Parkı, Atık Dönüşüm ile Park ve Bahçeler birimlerinde yapılan seçimlerde farklı listeler yarıştı.

Dokuz birimin beşinde birinci olan kırmızı liste, seçimlerden çoğunlukla çıktı. Kırmızı liste Sosyal Projeler, Çevre Koruma, Mezarlık, Haller ve Park ve Bahçeler birimlerinde seçimi kazandı. Yeşil liste Kent Temizlik ve Doğal Yaşam Parkı, mavi liste İdari İşler, beyaz liste ise Atık Dönüşüm biriminde ilk sırada yer aldı.

Sosyal Projeler biriminde kullanılan 853 oyun 15’i geçersiz sayıldı. Geçerli 838 oyun 346’sını kırmızı, 268’ini mavi, 224’ünü ise beyaz liste aldı. Kırmızı liste bu sonuçla birimde birinci oldu.

Çevre Koruma biriminde 164 oy alan kırmızı liste seçimi kazanırken Mezarlık biriminde de 212 oyla ilk sırada yer aldı. Mezarlıkta beyaz liste 175, kahverengi liste ise 117 oy aldı.

Haller biriminde kullanılan 66 oyun 4’ü geçersiz sayıldı. Geçerli 62 oyun 42’sini kırmızı, 20’sini mavi liste aldı.

Park ve Bahçeler biriminde ise kırmızı liste 422 oyla seçimi kazandı. Mavi liste 380, beyaz liste 225 oy aldı.

Kent Temizlik biriminde yeşil liste 488 oy alarak seçimi kazandı. Mavi liste ise 405 oyda kaldı.

Doğal Yaşam Parkı biriminde kullanılan 99 oyun 97’si geçerli sayıldı. Yeşil liste 51, kırmızı liste 46 oy aldı. Böylece yeşil liste bu birimde de birinci oldu.

İdari İşler biriminde mavi liste 339 oyla seçimi kazandı. Kırmızı liste 276, beyaz liste ise 161 oy aldı.

Atık Dönüşüm biriminde ise seçimi beyaz liste kazandı.

İki gün süren seçimlerin ardından kırmızı liste beş, yeşil liste iki, mavi ve beyaz listeler ise birer birimde birinci oldu.

Genel-İş İzmir 2 No’lu Şube Başkan Adayı Arif Yıldız ile delege seçimlerini kazanan kırmızı liste temsilcileri, seçimlerin ardından delegelere seslendi. Konuşmasında işçilerin uzun süredir yaşadığı sorunlara dikkat çeken Yıldız, mevcut yönetimin işçileri ayrıştırdığını belirterek yeni dönemde birlik ve mücadeleyi esas alacaklarını söyledi.

Yıldız, “Biz ‘Ayrıştırmayın, bu işi bölmeyin, şubeyi bölmeyin’ dedikçe seçim kazanabilmek adına şubeyi böldüler. İşçiyi ayrıştırdılar. Biz ilk yola çıkarken ‘Birleştireceğiz, dert yanmaya değil mücadele etmeye geliyoruz’ dedik” ifadelerini kullandı.

Aylardır havuzda bekletilen İZENERJİ işçilerinin sorunlarına değinen Yıldız, “Biz İZENERJİ emekçisinin, 4 No’lu holün önünde aylardan beri havuzda bekleyen, bizi gördüğünde ağlayan kadın arkadaşlarımızın sorununun çözümüne geliyoruz” dedi.

Toplu iş sözleşmesi sürecine de değinen Yıldız, “İZENERJİ emekçisinin içindeki mutluluğu çalmışlar. Biz yeniden o heyecanı, mutluluğu toplu sözleşmenin etrafında birleştirerek, geçmiş dönemde yaptığımız gibi madde veren değil, madde alan bir anlayışla yola devam edeceğiz” diye konuştu.

Hak-İş’e bağlı Hizmet-İş Sendikasının İzmir Büyükşehir Belediyesinde örgütlenme açıklamalarına tepki gösteren Yıldız, “Biz burada zaten 40 yıldır örgütlüyüz. Biz burada Hak-İş gibi bir sendikayı buraya sokmayacağız” dedi.

Seçim sonuçlarının işçilerin birlik talebini ortaya koyduğunu belirten Yıldız, “İZENERJİ işçisi bugünkü son sandıklarla gereken cevabı vermiştir. Bizden ayrıştıran değil, birleştiren bir süreci yürütmemizi istiyor. Hiç kimseyi ayrıştırmadan, ötekileştirmeden İZENERJİ işçisini yeniden ayağa dikeceğiz. 2 No’lu Şubeyi yeniden işçinin umudu haline getireceğiz” ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: infolibre
title: Στο ΑΠΘ διδάσκεται η «καινοτόμα επιχειρηματικότητα» του μιλιταρισμού και του θανάτου!
content:
Πρωτοβουλία Πανεπιστημιακών ΑΠΘ ΠΑΜΑΚ ΔΙΠΑΕ


Στο ΑΠΘ διδάσκεται η «καινοτόμα επιχειρηματικότητα» του μιλιταρισμού και του θανάτου


Δεν το είδαμε στον ιστότοπο του πανεπιστημίου:

https://opencoffee.gr/2026/10/17/open-coffee-thessaloniki-94/


Πρόκειται όμως για δράση του ΑΠΘ εντός του ΑΠΘ. Στις 29 Οκτωβρίου 2026 έχει κληθεί να μιλήσει στο ΚΕΔΕΑ ο διευθύνων σύμβουλος της Stark, μιας εταιρίας  παραγωγής «αμυντικών» drones, εταιρίας 3,2 δις, με συνεργάτες σε Γερμανία, Ουκρανία, Ηνωμένο Βασίλειο, Σουηδία και Ελλάδα. Στο πλαίσιο του WALK (του «επιταχυντή καινοτομίας του ΑΠΘ») φοιτητές και φοιτήτριες καλούνται να ακούσουν τον περήφανο επιχειρηματία να μιλά για το πώς, από μια μικρή startup, κατόρθωσε να πουλά τις υπηρεσίες του σε έναν κολοσσό της πολεμικής τεχνολογίας.


Αυτή είναι η εμπειρία που θεωρούν άξια να μεταδοθεί, αυτή είναι η φιλοδοξία που θέλουν να εμπνεύσουν στην επόμενη γενιά:

Πώς να θεραπεύσει τις επιστήμες του πολέμου, πώς να διαπρέψει στην παιδαγωγική του θανάτου.


Επιπλέον, προσπαθούν να διαμηνύσουν προς Θεσσαλονικείς: Ότι πρέπει να συνηθίσουμε, από τη μια την εγκαθίδρυση της ισραηλινής SK στη Σίνδο, στη θέση της πρώην ΕΛΒΟ, από την άλλη τα διάφορα «καινοτόμα» μιλιταριστικά ερευνητικά προγράμματα που προωθούνται στο ΑΠΘ και στα πανεπιστήμια ανά την επικράτεια με την DefenseEduNet.


Πριν λίγους μήνες η πανεπιστημιακή κοινότητα, φοιτήτριες, φοιτητές και ΕΣΔΕΠ καταφέραμε και διώξαμε το συνέδριο της πολεμικής οικονομίας έξω από τους χώρους του πανεπιστημίου, κάνοντας τους συμμετέχοντες να νιώσουν έστω ανεπιθύμητοι και φοβισμένοι (όχι βέβαια ντροπή, οι κυνικοί δεν έχουν ευθιξία).


Σήμερα, την ώρα που χιλιάδες εργαζόμενοι σε λιμάνια της Ευρώπης δηλώνουν «δεν δουλεύουμε για τον πόλεμό σας» και καλούν σε απεργία στις 30 Οκτωβρίου ενάντια στην αποστολή πολεμικού υλικού για τη γενοκτονία στη Γάζα και ενάντια στη στρατιωτικοποίηση παντού, ας ενώσουμε τη φωνή μας μαζί τους:


Το πανεπιστήμιο είναι χώρος έρευνας, μελέτης, διαλόγου, εκπαίδευσης, καλλιέργειας και διαπραγμάτευσης της γνώσης για την κοινωνία, για τη φύση, για τη ζωή. Δεν είναι σχεδιαστήριο όπλων για τη βιομηχανία της εξόντωσης.


Έξω η μιλιταριστική, θανατηφόρα «επιχειρηματικότητα» του πολέμου από τα πανεπιστήμια.


Θεσσαλονίκη 21 Οκτώβρη 2026

author: Daron Letts
title: Iqaluit deputy mayor calls on police foot patrols to resume
content:
Iqaluit’s deputy mayor is calling for “very successful” joint patrols between Iqaluit bylaw and RCMP to be reinstated, after the project was halted in the spring due to a lack of available police officers.


“I would like to call on the RCMP to get their staffing numbers to where we can work together again,” said Kim Smith during Tuesday’s governance and priorities meeting.

“It was very successful and we definitely saw a difference in the city.”


The pilot project ran from January through March. It ended due to a lack of available police officers, said Iqaluit’s chief municipal enforcement officer Steven Allen Tuesday during a presentation to the committee.


“While the project was in motion, it was a success, but the RCMP was unable to sustain providing a member for this project due to staffing levels,” Allen said.


Both agencies provided one officer each to patrol together daily in the afternoons. They focused on traffic-related offences and public intoxication, he said.


During an RCMP update to council in June, Iqaluit detachment commander Staff Sgt. Vlatko Nikolovski said he hoped to be able to “

secure resources

” to continue the project.


RCMP began conducting ATV patrols in June as well to compensate after the project ended, he added.


Justice Department policy director Stephen Shaddock wrote in an email to Nunatsiaq News in June that the Iqaluit detachment is currently “fully staffed and is expected to maintain regular rotations throughout the year.”


The detachment is staffed by 26 constables, four corporals and one sergeant,

 Nikolovski told council in June.


Councillors have long called on the RCMP to


step up

 enforcement of public drinking, with some

suggesting

 that closing Iqaluit’s beer and wine store might be the solution.


RCMP previously


teamed

 with Qikiqtani Inuit Association to increase foot patrols of the community.


Bylaw has its own staff vacancies, including a sergeant position and two officer positions that the city is currently seeking to fill, Allen said.

author: S. Baum
title: New Ad Calls Out GOP for “Creepy Fetish of Monitoring Children’s Bathrooms”
content:
The Progress Action Fund, a left-wing PAC, is running ads to “disrupt the right-wing media bubble.”

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A little girl walks into a bathroom and screams. Sitting there, scowling inside the stall, is the man who might be your next representative. “I’m your Republican congressman,” the man says. “Now that we’re in charge, I’m checking to make sure there’s no trans people in the wrong bathroom.” She protests; he insists. “I won the last election, and this is my priority. Now, let’s make sure you’re really a girl.”

This is the premise of the latest ad by the Progress Action Fund (PAF), a left-wing PAC running ads to “disrupt the right-wing media bubble,” as its website says.

The ad is incisive, unsettling, and to the point. It’s exactly the kind of thing this PAC is known for.

Joe Jacobson, PAF’s executive director, wants to see the left wage a meaningful counter-narrative to Republicans’ anti-trans hate. “There was no counter in 2024, and that was devastating for Democrats,” he told Erin In The Morning. “Rather than just sidestepping the issue, we need to have a counter, and the testing shows our counter is effective.”

According to independent randomized controlled testing, the “Republicans In Your Bathroom” ad can move swing voters 8 points toward Democrats, as per a press release from PAF. The group is also the creative force behind viral, in-your-face attack ads against Republicans, like “Republicans In Your Bedroom” and “Republicans Blowing Your Taxes.”

“Republicans In Your Bathroom” will primarily run in Texas and Ohio, two key battleground states in this midterm election. The ads are expected to reach 50 million Americans.

It’s a welcome antidote to the GOP’s fearmongering about trans people. This includes an Ohio ad by the Senate Leadership Fund, which featured a Texas woman who falsely claimed she underwent gender-affirming surgery as a minor, without parental consent. There was also an attack ad against James Talarico that emphasized he’s “too weak” for Texas as a trans flag waved in the background. And Iowa’s Sarah Trone Garriott was the target of an ad campaign that lambasted her for supposedly supporting trans-inclusive sports teams.

It’s no surprise, then, that Elon Musk’s PAC spent over $100 million on ads this cycle, with a heavy focus on trans issues. Nor is it a shock to learn that in 2024, Republicans spent almost $215 million on network TV ads attacking the transgender community.

Unfortunately, some Democrats in high-profile races appear to cede ground to this hateful rhetoric. Trone Garriott, for example, released an ad in response to allegations that she supported the trans community by declaring that she opposes “men in women’s locker rooms,” which is a pejorative often used to describe transgender women and girls. But Jacobson’s response? “Republicans are creepy as hell,” he said in a statement. “Democrats need to grow a spine and call Republicans out for their creepy fetish of monitoring children’s bathrooms.”

This piece was republished with permission from Erin In The Morning.

author: Chris Walker
title: Poll: 7 in 10 Americans Doubt Trump Will Accept Midterm Results
content:
The president has said that he will only accept the results of the midterms if he deems them to be “honest.”

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

A new poll demonstrates that voters are deeply skeptical over whether President Donald Trump will accept the outcome of the 2026 midterm elections, which Democrats are currently favored to win.

The Washington Post/ABC News/Ipsos poll, published earlier this week, asked respondents how confident they were regarding how Trump will react to the midterms. Only 28 percent said they were “very confident” or “somewhat confident” that he would accept the results. Meanwhile, 70 percent of Americans are “not too confident” or “not at all confident” that he will back the outcome.

The poll comes as Trump himself has repeatedly indicated that he won’t accept the results if Democrats win over Republican Party candidates.

Trump has spent much of the 2026 midterm campaign season sowing unfounded doubts about the legitimacy of American elections. His administration has acted in kind, publishing dubious reports that baselessly suggest that tens of thousands of people ineligible to vote took part in the 2020 presidential race that Trump lost. The president has also pushed states to remove residents that he claims are illegal voters from their voting rolls, and has called for “nationalizing” the elections, despite the U.S. Constitution placing management of elections in the hands of states, not the federal government.

In June, Trump reacted furiously when “Meet the Press” host Kristen Welker pressed him for evidence of his claims of voter fraud, storming out of the interview.

And in February, Trump said in an interview that he would only accept the midterm results if he deemed the elections to be “honest.” If not, “something else has to happen,” he said.

Analysts have expressed concerns about Trump’s comments regarding the midterms, with some theorizing that he is potentially setting the stage for an event similar to what happened at the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021, when a mob of his loyalists stormed the building in an attempt to overturn his loss in the 2020 presidential election.

One theory contends that Speaker of the House Mike Johnson, himself a staunch loyalist to the president, could replace the House Clerk with someone equally dedicated to helping Trump, if Democrats do indeed win the midterms. That individual could then refuse to seat the newly elected lawmakers, keeping the older, unelected ones in place, using the same baseless claims of election fraud in order to justify doing so.

Trump could also encourage his supporters to be at the Capitol on January 3, the day new lawmakers are supposed to be sworn in, to incite action from Johnson and Republicans — much like he did in 2021, when he said a “wild” event would take place at the Capitol.

Election law scholars doubt the legality of such a move, but it could still be attempted, delaying the swearing-in ceremonies or even resulting in violence, if Trump refuses to accept the results.

Notably, Johnson has behaved this way before. Earlier this year, after then-Rep.-elect Adelita Grijalva (D-Arizona) won a special election in her district, Johnson refused to seat her for several weeks, claiming he couldn’t do so because the House was out of session (despite having sworn in Republican lawmakers while the House was out of session). At the time, Grijalva was seen as being the last vote needed to pass a bill to release the Epstein files, which Johnson opposed.

Polling data indicates that Democrats are expected to win control of the House in this November’s elections, and have a strong chance of winning the Senate, too. According to polling site FiftyPlusOne, as of Wednesday morning, Democrats have a 99 percent chance of winning the House, and a 74 percent chance of taking over the Senate.

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Rogue AI Must Threaten 50 Lives Before Being Shut Down, Anthropic Suggests
content:
Anthropic is pushing legislation that would only allow the US government to shut down a rogue AI model when at least 50 people are at risk of imminent serious harm or death.


The AI firm has been quietly lobbying congress to adopt its draft bill, a copy of which was obtained by

Politico

.


Under the bill

, a state-led “blocking order” can also be triggered if there is a risk of an AI model causing at least $1bn (£750m) in damage to property. 


The rules laid out in the draft would prevent US states from enforcing tougher safety laws and make it harder for courts to put the brakes on dangerous AI systems.


They set a high threshold for federal intervention in the case of potential “catastrophic harm”. 


Federal officials, for example, would have to ascertain that any threat posed by AI was “imminent” and that no alternative could prevent catastrophe before intervening.


In a

Substack post

, Zvi Mowshowitz, a writer who focuses on AI, described this as an “absurdly high bar”.


The draft bill reads: “The term ‘catastrophic risk’ means a foreseeable and material risk that a frontier developer’s development, storage, use or deployment of a frontier model will materially contribute to the death of, or serious injury to, more than 50 people, or to more than $1bn in damage to… property arising from a single incident”.


AI safety experts, including

Nathan Calvin

,

Nat Purser

 and

Nate Soares

 have warned such a bill would weaken existing safeguards while limiting federal oversight.


Mowshowitz said the bill would make people less safe than if legislators did “nothing”. He argued that Anthropic appeared more concerned about the government enforcing safety rules than ensuring it had the power to hold the wider AI industry to account.


Anthony Cimino, head of federal affairs at Anthropic,

said on X

 that the language around risk thresholds in the draft was “pulled directly from existing standards in California law” and would not absolve companies of liability nor prevent the government from using other tools at its disposal to protect the public.


But he acknowledged that it may be “time to re-evaluate thresholds to make sure the national standard is as strong as it can be.”


Last month, former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon

 warned that AI could wipe out humanity within a decade

. 


The researcher’s comments triggered a series of similar warnings from other AI colleagues. But observers have cast doubt on the claims, as Fortune AI’s editor, Jeremy Kahn, noted, with some viewing them as a “

cynical ploy… intended to distract regulators and the public from the real and concrete risks that already exist

”.

author: Dylan Baddour
title: Texas Continued Permitting Data Centers After Greg Abbott Ordered a Pause
content:
A new report identified 35 permitting actions taken by regulators in Texas in the weeks after the governor’s moratorium.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Regulators in Texas did not stop processing permits for data center projects when Gov. Greg Abbott ordered a pause last month, according to an analysis of public records released Monday by the oil and gas watchdog group FracTracker.

Amid an upswell of public opposition to the booming buildout of digital infrastructure in Texas, Abbott directed the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality in a Sept. 21 letter “to halt all permits sought by data centers.”

But FracTracker, in collaboration with Public Citizen, identified 35 permitting actions taken by the TCEQ for data center projects in subsequent weeks.

“TCEQ has continued reviewing applications and issuing approvals that allow data center development to proceed,” the groups said in a press release Monday. “These actions do not signal an agency trying to pause.”

In response, Abbott Press Secretary Andrew Mahaleris indicated that the pause applied to approval, not processing, of permits.

“No permits have been approved,” Mahaleris said in a statement. “In line with the Governor’s directive, TCEQ has not taken and will not take any proactive actions related to the approval of data center permits.”

Abbott has described his moratorium as an opportunity for state agencies to evaluate the facilities’ impact on water resources and grid stability.

“No other state agency shall move forward with regulatory approvals related to data centers until this information is acquired,” Abbott wrote in his Sept. 21 letter to TCEQ executive director Kelly Keel.

TCEQ responded to Abbott in an Oct. 19 letter, which was provided to Inside Climate News by Ryan Vise, TCEQ’s director of external relations.

In the letter, Steven Schar, TCEQ’s interim executive director, wrote: “TCEQ staff are screening pending permit applications to determine if they are subject to the directive. If a permit application is subject to the directive, TCEQ has paused that permit application.”

Since the Sept. 21 directive, the TCEQ has fast-tracked or assigned engineers to 14 permits, approved stormwater coverage for 11, certified emissions estimates for seven and issued public notice for three, according to permitting documents collected by FracTracker and Public Citizen.

The permits regard construction of gas power generation facilities for energy-hungry facilities. All of the largest gas power projects currently proposed in Texas are specifically intended to serve data centers, which are primarily planned to run artificial intelligence.

The projects would release tens of thousands of tons of regulated pollutants, according to permitting documents, as well as more than 100 million tons per year of greenhouse gases — an enormous amount roughly equal to the annual emissions of a mid-sized industrialized country.

The day after Abbott’s pause on data center permits, on Sept. 22, FracTracker and Public Citizen found that TCEQ mailed notices of preliminary approval to three major projects: NRG Prairie Energy Center, VoltaGrid’s ABI-1 power plant and Nexus’s self-powered data center in Hubbard.

The agency opened public comment periods on two of those projects in following days.

FracTracker and Public Citizen found approvals of stormwater management permits for data center construction issued after Sept. 21, including for Caldwell Valley Technology Park in Caldwell County, Crusoe’s Abilene campus and EdgeConneX’s Cedar Creek campus. The report identified numerous other projects that continue to advance through permitting. For example, records show the TCEQ received a permit application for generators at Edged Energy in Dallas on Oct. 6, and an engineer completed an initial review on Oct. 9.

“Our research uncovered glaring inconsistencies between regulatory actions and Governor Abbott’s directives,” said Sam Law, manager of communications at FracTracker Alliance and author of the report. “We need an actual pause to study the threats posed to the land, water and livelihoods of Texans.”
